chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency GRE Words

words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.ex: The project is in abeyance until next year.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目暂时搁置，直到明年。
words.en: A state of temporary disuse or suspension.

words.tr: adj. 有节制的；饮食有度的
words.ex: He is abstemious with sugar and eats little dessert.
words.ex_cn: 他对糖很节制，吃很少的甜点。
words.en: Someone who is abstemious avoids doing too much of something enjoyable, especially eating or drinking.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.tr: n. 敏捷；活泼；欣然；乐意
words.ex: He answered the question with alacrity.
words.ex_cn: 他愉快地回答了问题。
words.en: If you do something with alacrity, you do it quickly and eagerly.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: The two companies will amalgamate next month.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司下个月将合并。
words.en: If two or more organizations amalgamate, they join together and become one organization.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.tr: n. 矛盾心理；正反感情并存
words.ex: He feels ambivalence about moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他对搬到新城市感到矛盾。
words.en: Ambivalence is the state of having mixed feelings or contradictory attitudes about something or someone.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的事；过时的事或人
words.ex: The knight in the movie uses a smartphone, which is an anachronism.
words.ex_cn: 电影中的骑士使用智能手机，这是不合时宜的。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of place in terms of time or chronology, such as an object, a custom, or an idea that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it is placed.

words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.ex: The country fell into anarchy after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这个国家陷入了混乱。
words.en: Anarchy is a state of disorder due to absence or nonrecognition of authority or other controlling systems.

words.tr: adj. 偏离规则的；反常的
words.ex: The temperature was anomalous for this season.
words.ex_cn: 这个季节的温度异常。
words.en: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.ex: He apprised her of the change.
words.ex_cn: 他通知了她这个变化。
words.en: If you are apprised of something, someone tells you about it.

words.ex: The teacher gave castigation to the student who cheated.
words.ex_cn: 老师惩罚了作弊的学生。
words.en: Castigation is the act of criticizing or punishing someone severely.

words.ex: He gave a conciliatory smile to calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他露出和解的微笑来平息争执。
words.en: If you are conciliatory, you show that you are willing to end a disagreement with someone by doing or saying things that will please them.

words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A conundrum is a confusing and difficult problem or question.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.tr:
adj. 旋绕的；费解的
v. 盘旋；卷绕；“convolute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path through the garden was convoluted.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的小路蜿蜒曲折。
words.en: If you describe something such as a story, explanation, or system as convoluted, you mean that it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.ex: He loves studying cosmology to understand the universe.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢学习宇宙学来理解宇宙。
words.en: Cosmology is the study of the origin, structure, and evolution of the universe.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.ex: The witness gave credence to the story by crying.
words.ex_cn: 证人通过哭泣使这个故事显得可信。
words.en: Credence is a belief in or acceptance of something as true.

words.tr: n. 礼貌得体；适宜的举止
words.ex: He maintained decorum during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持了得体的行为。
words.en: Decorum is behavior that is controlled, calm, and polite, especially in formal situations.

words.ex: He showed deference to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师表示尊敬。
words.en: Deference is a polite and respectful attitude towards someone, often because they are older or more experienced than you.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.ex: The book uses demotic language to reach ordinary people.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使用通俗的语言来吸引普通人。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the form of a language used by ordinary people; vernacular.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.ex: He tries to denigrate his rival's ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低对手的想法。
words.en: If you denigrate someone or something, you criticize them unfairly or insult them.

words.ex: The denouement of the story was surprising.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的结局令人惊讶。
words.en: The final part of a play, movie, or narrative in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and matters are explained or resolved.

words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.ex: The sun will desiccate the leaves in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天阳光会把叶子晒干。
words.en: To remove the moisture from something, typically in order to preserve it.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不连贯的；断续的
words.ex: He gave a desultory answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个漫无目的的回答。
words.en: Something that is desultory is done in an unplanned and disorganized way, and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: He gave a loud diatribe against the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他对新法律发表了一通激烈的抨击。
words.en: A diatribe is an angry speech or piece of writing that strongly criticizes something or someone.

words.ex: The dichotomy between good and evil is common in stories.
words.ex_cn: 善与恶的两分在故事中很常见。
words.en: A dichotomy is a division or contrast between two things that are represented as being entirely different.

words.ex: He spoke with diffidence during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上说话时很犹豫。
words.en: Diffidence is the quality of being shy and not confident of your abilities.

words.tr:
v. 弥漫；
adj. 分散的；
words.ex: Smoke began to diffuse through the room.
words.ex_cn: 烟开始弥漫在整个房间里。
words.en: If something such as knowledge or information is diffused, or if it diffuses, it is made known over a wide area or to a lot of people.

words.ex: He tried to disabuse her of the idea that money solves everything.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让她明白，钱并不能解决所有问题。
words.en: If you disabuse someone of something, you tell them or persuade them that what they believe is in fact not true.

words.tr: adj. 不调和的；不一致的；不和谐的
words.ex: The two voices sounded discordant.
words.ex_cn: 这两声音听起来不和谐。
words.en: Something that is discordant is strange or unpleasant because it does not fit in with other things.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr: adj. 不真诚的；不坦率的；虚伪的
words.ex: He gave a disingenuous answer to avoid trouble.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不真诚的回答以避免麻烦。
words.en: Someone who is disingenuous is not sincere or honest, but pretends to be so in order to deceive people.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: He never disparages his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他从不贬低他的同学。
words.en: If you disparage someone or something, you speak about them in a way which shows that you do not have a good opinion of them.

words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.tr: n. 分解；分裂；溶解；解体；解除；死亡
words.ex: The dissolution of sugar in water is quick.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中的分解很快。
words.en: The act or process of ending or breaking up an organization, agreement, or legal arrangement.

words.ex: There is a dissonance between his words and actions.
words.ex_cn: 他的言行不一致。
words.en: A lack of harmony or agreement between people or things.

words.tr:
adj. 教条（主义）的；空谈理论的
n. 教条主义者；空论家
words.ex: He is a doctrinaire who always follows rules strictly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个教条主义者，总是严格遵守规则。
words.en: If you say that someone is doctrinaire, you are criticizing them for following fixed theories or principles rather than considering practical problems.

words.tr: adj. 教条的；武断的；固执己见的
words.ex: He is dogmatic about his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念非常固执。
words.en: If you say that someone is dogmatic, you are critical of them because they are convinced that they are right, and refuse to consider that other opinions might also be justified.

words.tr: adj. 奔放的；兴高采烈的；沸腾的
words.ex: He is ebullient after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖后非常兴奋。
words.en: If you describe someone as ebullient, you mean that they are lively and full of enthusiasm or excitement about something.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.tr: adj. 衰弱的；衰败的；软弱的
words.ex: The old king was effete and could not lead.
words.ex_cn: 这位老国王虚弱无能，无法领导。
words.en: No longer productive or effective; lacking the power or will to achieve or succeed.

words.ex: The efficacy of the medicine is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是明显的。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.ex: He had the effrontery to lie to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老师撒谎。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as effrontery, you are emphasizing that it is very rude or disrespectful.

words.ex: He read an elegy for his dead dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为他去世的狗朗读了一首挽歌。
words.en: An elegy is a sad poem, often about someone who has died.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.ex: He kept his equanimity during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他在风暴中保持了冷静。
words.en: If you face a difficult situation with equanimity, you remain calm and do not get upset or angry.

words.tr: v. 含糊其辞；说模棱两可的话
words.ex: He equivocates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他含糊其辞。
words.en: If you equivocate, you use ambiguous language in order to deceive people or to avoid speaking directly about something.

words.ex: The erudite professor knows many ancient languages.
words.ex_cn: 这位博学的教授懂得许多古代语言。
words.en: Having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.ex: He used a euphemism to say he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个委婉语来表示他失业了。
words.en: A euphemism is a polite word or expression that is used to refer to things which people may find upsetting or embarrassing to talk about.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.tr:
adj. 要求严格的；要求小心仔细的；苛求的
v. 强求；急需；要求；“exact”的现在分词
words.ex: He is an exacting teacher who wants perfect work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个要求严格的老师，要求完美无缺的作业。
words.en: requiring a lot of effort, care, or attention

words.ex: The evidence helps to exculpate him.
words.ex_cn: 这些证据有助于为他开脱。
words.en: To remove blame from someone; to declare or prove someone not guilty of wrongdoing.

words.tr: adj. 该诅咒的；恶劣的；极坏的
words.ex: The food was execrable.
words.ex_cn: 这食物糟糕透顶。
words.en: If you describe something as execrable, you mean that it is extremely bad or unpleasant.

words.ex: There is an exigency, so we must act now.
words.ex_cn: 情况紧急，我们必须立刻行动。
words.en: An exigency is a pressing or urgent situation or need that requires immediate action or attention.

words.ex: His poem explores existential questions about life.
words.ex_cn: 他的诗歌探讨了有关存在的生命问题。
words.en: Relating to existence, especially human existence as viewed in the theories of existentialism.

words.ex: There are only two extant copies of the ancient book.
words.ex_cn: 这本古书现存只有两份。
words.en: If something is extant, it is still in existence, in spite of being very old.

words.ex: The extraneous noise made it hard to concentrate.
words.ex_cn: 那些无关的噪音让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: Something that is extraneous is not relevant or essential to the subject you are dealing with.

words.ex: He made an extrapolation from the data to predict the future.
words.ex_cn: 他根据数据做出了外推以预测未来。
words.en: Extrapolation is the act of estimating or concluding something by assuming that existing trends will continue or a current method will remain applicable.

words.tr: adj. 爱开玩笑的；乱引人发笑的
words.ex: He gave a facetious answer when asked about his age.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到年龄时，他给出了一个开玩笑的回答。
words.en: If you say that someone is being facetious, you are criticizing them because they are making humorous remarks or saying things that they do not mean in a situation where they ought to be serious.

words.ex: His argument is fallacious because it ignores the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是错误的，因为它忽略了事实。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or reason is fallacious, it is wrong because it is based on a fallacy.

words.tr: adj. 愚昧的；昏庸的；愚笨的
words.ex: His fatuous smile made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他那愚蠢的微笑让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe a person, action, or remark as fatuous, you mean that they are extremely silly, showing a lack of intelligence or thought.

words.tr: adj. 贴切的；恰当的；妥帖的
words.ex: His felicitous remark made everyone smile.
words.ex_cn: 他得体的言论让每个人都笑了。
words.en: Well chosen or suited to the circumstances.

words.tr:
n. 刚长齐羽毛学飞的幼鸟
adj. 新形成的；无经验的
v. 羽毛长成；用羽毛盖上；装上羽毛；“fledge”的现在分词
words.ex: The fledgling bird tried to fly for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这只幼鸟第一次尝试飞翔。
words.en: A fledgling is a young bird that has just grown its feathers and is learning to fly. It can also refer to a person or organization that is new and inexperienced.

words.ex: He tries to foment trouble between the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在邻居之间挑起纠纷。
words.en: If someone foments trouble or violent opposition, they cause it to develop.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难驾驭的；脾气不好的
words.ex: The fractious child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个脾气暴躁的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe someone as fractious, you mean they are easily upset or annoyed, and often complain.

words.ex: His frugality helped him save money for years.
words.ex_cn: 他的节俭让他多年都存下了钱。
words.en: Frugality is the quality of being careful with money or food, so that you only spend what is necessary.

words.tr: v. 大声呵斥；强烈谴责
words.ex: He fulminates against unfair laws.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈谴责不公正的法律。
words.en: To fulminate means to express vehement protest. It can also mean to explode or detonate.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.tr: adj. 不奸猾的；厚道的；坦率的
words.ex: He is a guileless boy who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个纯真无邪的男孩，总是说真话。
words.en: If you describe someone as guileless, you mean that they behave openly and truthfully and do not try to deceive people.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.tr:
n. 高谈阔论；长篇大论；大声斥责的讲话
v. 作长篇大论；高谈阔论；猛烈的批评或训斥
words.ex: The politician gave a long harangue about taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客就税收问题发表了一番长篇高谈阔论。
words.en: A harangue is a lengthy and aggressive speech, especially one delivered in public.

words.ex: His heterodox ideas shocked the traditional scholars.
words.ex_cn: 他的非正统观点让传统学者感到震惊。
words.en: Heterodox ideas, opinions, or practices are different from the accepted or official ones.

words.ex: His histrionic gestures made the play very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 他戏剧性的手势让这场戏非常精彩。
words.en: If you refer to someone's behaviour as histrionic, you are critical of it because it is very dramatic, exaggerated, and insincere.

words.ex: The priest gave a short homily after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祷告后，牧师做了一个简短的讲道。
words.en: A homily is a religious discourse which is intended to edify a congregation, typically given by a priest or minister during a service.

words.ex: The mixture is homogeneous and looks the same throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这种混合物是均一的，看起来处处都一样。
words.en: Something that is homogeneous is uniform in nature or character throughout.

words.ex: He uses hyperbole when he says he is dying of hunger.
words.ex_cn: 当他说到自己快饿死了时，他用了夸张的说法。
words.en: Hyperbole is a way of speaking or writing that makes someone or something sound bigger, better, more, etc. than they are.

words.ex: His iconoclastic ideas changed the way people think about art.
words.ex_cn: 他打破旧习的想法改变了人们对艺术的看法。
words.en: If you describe someone or their ideas as iconoclastic, you mean that they deliberately challenge established beliefs or institutions.

words.ex: He has ideological beliefs about freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他有关于自由的思想信念。
words.en: Relating to or concerned with ideas, especially of a political or economic nature.

words.tr: n. 偶像崇拜；盲目崇拜
words.ex: He worships the pop star like idolatry.
words.ex_cn: 他像崇拜偶像一样崇拜这位流行歌手。
words.en: The worship of idols or excessive admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 火成的；火的；似火的
words.ex: The rock is igneous because it came from lava.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石是火成岩，因为它来自熔岩。
words.en: Igneous rocks are rocks formed by the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.

words.tr: adj. 不可改变的；永恒不变的
words.ex: The password is immutable and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 密码是不可更改的。
words.en: If you say that something is immutable, you mean that it cannot be changed at all.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.tr: adj. 不能渗透的；不透水的
words.ex: The raincoat is impermeable and keeps you dry.
words.ex_cn: 这件雨衣不透水，能让你保持干燥。
words.en: An impermeable material does not allow liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.ex: He remained imperturbable even when the storm hit.
words.ex_cn: 即使风暴来袭，他依然镇定自若。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperturbable, you mean that they remain calm, even in disturbing or dangerous situations.

words.tr: adj. 不能渗透的；不受影响的
words.ex: The coat is impervious to rain.
words.ex_cn: 这件外套不透水。
words.en: If you are impervious to someone's actions, you are not affected or influenced by them.

words.tr: adj. 不能和解的；不能平息的
words.ex: He is an implacable enemy who never forgives.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个永不原谅的不可调和的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone is implacable, you mean that they have very strong feelings of hostility or disapproval which nobody can change.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.ex: He inadvertently dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他非故意地打翻了玻璃杯。
words.en: If you do something inadvertently, you do it without realizing it, or by accident.

words.tr: adj. 初始的；早期的；未形成的
words.ex: His idea was still inchoate.
words.ex_cn: 他的想法还很不成熟。
words.en: If something is inchoate, it is just beginning to form or is not fully developed or clear.

words.ex: The pink hat on the man looked like an incongruity.
words.ex_cn: 男人头上的粉红色帽子显得很不协调。
words.en: The state of being incongruous; incompatibility.

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不明确的
words.ex: The result is indeterminate.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不确定的。
words.en: If something is indeterminate, you cannot say exactly what it is.

words.ex: He lived in indigence after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Indigence is the state of being extremely poor.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
words.ex: The outcome was ineluctable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不可避免的。
words.en: Something that is ineluctable cannot be avoided or escaped from.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；天真的；坦率的
words.ex: He gave an ingenuous smile when he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当他讲真话时，他露出了天真无邪的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as ingenuous, you mean that they are innocent, trusting, and honest, often in a way that seems naive.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；无冒犯之意的
words.ex: The comment was innocuous and didn't upset anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个评论无害，没有惹恼任何人。
words.en: Something that is innocuous is not harmful or offensive.

words.tr: adj. （对某事物）无感觉的；未察觉的；意识不到的；失去知觉的
words.ex: He was insensible after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他失去了知觉。
words.en: If someone is insensible, they are not able to feel or notice something, often because they are unconscious or unaware.

words.ex: He insinuated that she was lying.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她在撒谎。
words.en: If you say that someone insinuates that something bad is the case, you mean that they say it in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.ex: The insularity of Japan affects its cultural traditions.
words.ex_cn: 日本的岛国特性影响了它的文化传统。
words.en: The state of being isolated or detached from others, often resulting in a narrow or limited perspective.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.tr: n. 不妥协；不让步；不妥协态度
words.ex: His intransigence stopped the peace talk.
words.ex_cn: 他的顽固阻止了和平谈判。
words.en: Intransigence is the quality of refusing to change one's views or behavior in a way that is considered unreasonable or stubborn.

words.tr: v. 淹没；泛滥；使不胜负荷；使应接不暇
words.ex: The rain inundated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 大雨淹没了这个小镇。
words.en: To inundate means to flood or overwhelm something with a large amount of water or things.

words.tr:
adj. 习惯的
v. 使习惯（于）；“inure”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is inured to loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对嘈杂的声音已经习惯了。
words.en: If you are inured to something unpleasant, you have become used to it so that it no longer affects you.

words.ex: His speech was full of invective against his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了对对手的辱骂。
words.en: Invective is rude and unpleasant things that people shout at someone they hate or are angry with.

words.ex: He is irascible when he wakes up late.
words.ex_cn: 他起床晚时容易发怒。
words.en: If you describe someone as irascible, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.tr: adj. 无决断的；犹豫不决的
words.ex: He was irresolute about which job to accept.
words.ex_cn: 他对于接受哪份工作犹豫不决。
words.en: If someone is irresolute, they are uncertain about what to do or are unable to make decisions.

words.ex: He juxtaposes old photos with new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他把老照片和新照片放在一起。
words.en: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；简明扼要的；凝练的
words.ex: He gave a laconic reply: 'Yes.'
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答：‘是的。’
words.en: If you describe someone as laconic, you mean that they use very few words to say something, so that they seem casual or unfriendly.

words.tr: n. 倦怠；疲乏；无精打采
words.ex: He felt lassitude after working all day.
words.ex_cn: 他工作了一整天后感到乏力。
words.en: A state of physical or mental weariness; lack of energy.

words.ex: The teacher lauded the student for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 老师称赞了这名学生努力学习。
words.en: If people laud someone, they praise and admire them.

words.tr: adj. 慵懒的；没精打采的；懒洋洋的
words.ex: He felt lethargic after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you are lethargic, you do not have much energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；清晰的
words.ex: The lake water is limpid and clear.
words.ex_cn: 湖水清澈透明。
words.en: Clear and transparent, especially in a way that makes it easy to understand.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这道数学题做了一个易懂的解释。
words.en: If someone is lucid, they are able to understand things clearly and think clearly, especially when they have been very ill or confused.

words.ex: He showed magnanimity by forgiving his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽恕了敌人，展现了宽宏大量。
words.en: Magnanimity is the quality of being kind, generous, and forgiving, especially towards someone who has wronged you.

words.ex: He was accused of malingering to avoid military service.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控装病以逃避兵役。
words.en: If someone is malingering, they pretend to be ill in order to avoid work or duties.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.tr: adj. 撒谎的；不真实的；捏造的
words.ex: She was known for her mendacious stories.
words.ex_cn: 她以编造虚假故事而闻名。
words.en: If someone is mendacious, they are not telling the truth.

words.tr: adj. 俗气的；华而不实的；虚有其表的
words.ex: The decoration was meretricious and lacked any real artistic merit.
words.ex_cn: 装饰俗气，缺乏真正的艺术价值。
words.en: Something that is meretricious is attractive in a showy or cheap way, often without having any real value or quality.

words.ex: The caterpillar's metamorphosis into a butterfly takes weeks.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫变成蝴蝶的变形需要几周时间。
words.en: Metamorphosis is a process of transformation from an immature form to an adult form in two or more distinct stages.

words.ex: He is thinking about metaphysical questions.
words.ex_cn: 他正在思考形而上学的问题。
words.en: Metaphysical means relating to metaphysics, which is the branch of philosophy that deals with the first principles of things, including abstract concepts such as being, knowing, substance, cause, identity, time, and space.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.tr: n. 厌恶世人者；遁世者
words.ex: He is a misanthrope who avoids people.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个避世的人，不喜欢与人交往。
words.en: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes and avoids other people.

words.ex: He was known as a misogynist who often made derogatory comments about women.
words.ex_cn: 他以厌恶女人著称，经常对女性发表贬低性言论。
words.en: A misogynist is a man who dislikes, despises, or is strongly prejudiced against women.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: n. 新信徒；新手；初学者
words.ex: The neophyte learned the prayers from the elder.
words.ex_cn: 新信徒向长者学习祷告。
words.en: A neophyte is someone who is new to a particular activity, subject, or religion and is therefore inexperienced.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；逢迎的；谄媚的
words.ex: He was obsequious to his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他为了得到晋升，对老板阿谀奉承。
words.en: If you describe someone as obsequious, you are criticizing them because they are too eager to help or agree with someone more important than them.

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.ex: The leaf occluded the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 叶子堵住了管道。
words.en: To occlude means to block or stop up a passage, opening, or vessel.

words.tr: adj. 爱发号施令的；多管闲事的
words.ex: The officious clerk refused to help unless I filled out another form.
words.ex_cn: 那位爱多管闲事的职员拒绝帮忙，除非我再填一份表格。
words.en: If you describe someone as officious, you are critical of them because they are eager to tell people what to do when you think they should not.

words.ex: The onerous workload made her tired every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量让她每天都很累。
words.en: If you describe a task as onerous, you dislike having to do it because you find it difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: He faced opprobrium for lying to the public.
words.ex_cn: 他因对公众撒谎而遭到谴责。
words.en: Opprobrium is harsh criticism or censure; public disgrace arising from shameful conduct.

words.ex: The pendulum oscillate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆缓慢地摆动。
words.en: If an object oscillates, it moves repeatedly from one position to another and back again, or if a figure or value oscillates, it keeps moving up and down.

words.tr: adj. 炫耀的；浮华的；卖弄的
words.ex: He wore an ostentatious gold watch to show off his wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一块华丽的金表来炫耀他的财富。
words.en: If you describe something as ostentatious, you disapprove of it because it is expensive and is intended to impress people.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.tr: adj. 病理学的；病理的；病态的
words.ex: The doctor found a pathological change in the tissue.
words.ex_cn: 医生在组织中发现了一种病理性的变化。
words.en: Pathological means relating to pathology, which is the study of diseases, or it can describe a behavior or condition that is extreme and not normal, often in a way that is harmful or undesirable.

words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.ex: He gave a pedantic answer about grammar rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对语法规则给出了一个迂腐的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as pedantic, you mean that they are too concerned with unimportant details or traditional rules, especially in connection with academic subjects.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；易懂的
words.ex: The water in the mountain stream was so pellucid that we could see the fish swimming.
words.ex_cn: 山间溪流中的水如此清澈，我们可以看到鱼儿在游动。
words.en: If something is pellucid, it is very clear and easy to understand.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.ex: He lives in penury after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Penury is the state of being extremely poor.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something that is done as perfunctory, you mean that it is done as a duty or a formality, without much care or interest.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.ex: He is phlegmatic even when things go wrong.
words.ex_cn: 即使事情出错，他依然冷静。
words.en: A phlegmatic person does not usually get emotional or excited about things.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.ex: The school will rescind the rule next month.
words.ex_cn: 学校下个月将撤销这项规定。
words.en: If a government or a group of people in power rescind a law or agreement, they officially withdraw it and state that it is no longer valid.

words.tr: adj. 坚决的；毅然的；有决心的；
words.ex: He was resolute in his decision to quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他决心戒烟。
words.en: If you describe someone as resolute, you approve of them because they are very determined not to change their mind or not to give up a course of action.

words.tr: v. 解决；“resolve”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He resolved the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快解决了这个问题。
words.en: If you are resolved to do something, you have made a firm decision to do it and will not let anything stop you.

words.tr: adj. 沉默寡言的；讳莫如深的
words.ex: He is reticent about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的感受很沉默。
words.en: If you are reticent about something, you are unwilling to talk about it or make your feelings known.

words.ex: He showed reverence for his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他对祖父表示尊敬。
words.en: A feeling of profound respect for someone or something.

words.ex: She added sage to the stuffing for Thanksgiving dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她在感恩节晚餐的填料中加入了鼠尾草。
words.en: A sage is a person who is regarded as being very wise, especially someone who is known for their good judgment and deep understanding of life.

words.tr: adj. 有益健康的；环境宜人的
words.ex: The air in the mountains is salubrious.
words.ex_cn: 山里的空气有益健康。
words.en: A salubrious place is pleasant, healthy, and good for you.

words.ex: The experience was a salutary lesson in the importance of preparation.
words.ex_cn: 这次经历是一个关于准备重要性的有益教训。
words.en: A salutary experience or warning is one that has a good effect or influence, especially by showing you the bad results of a particular action or behaviour.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: He has a sartorial style that impresses everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种令人印象深刻的服装风格。
words.en: Sartorial relates to tailoring, clothes, or style of dress.

words.tr: v. 使饱足；使厌腻；充分满足
words.ex: The big meal satiated his hunger.
words.ex_cn: 这顿丰盛的饭填饱了他的肚子。
words.en: To satisfy a desire or need fully.

words.tr: adj. 感官的；肉欲的；愉悦感官的；耽于肉欲的
words.ex: The sensual smell of fresh bread made her hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的感官香味让她感到饥饿。
words.en: Relating to or involving gratification of the senses and physical, especially sexual, pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 感觉上的；感官的；（引起）美感的
words.ex: She wore a sensuous silk dress.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件性感的丝绸裙子。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the senses rather than the intellect; characterized by a pleasing or luxurious quality that appeals to the senses.

words.tr: adj. 有知觉的；有感觉力的；
words.ex: The robot became sentient and could feel pain.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人变得有知觉，能够感受到疼痛。
words.en: A sentient being is capable of perception or feeling.

words.tr: n. 怀疑论者；怀疑宗教主张的人；无神论者
words.ex: He is a skeptic about new health claims.
words.ex_cn: 他对新的健康说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: A skeptic is a person who questions the validity or authenticity of something purporting to be factual.

words.tr: adj. 关怀的；切望的；惦记的；悬虑的
words.ex: He was solicitous about her health.
words.ex_cn: 他非常关心她的健康。
words.en: If you are solicitous, you are very concerned about someone's safety, health, or comfort.

words.tr:
adj. 催眠的；让人瞌睡的
n. 安眠药
words.ex: The monotonous lecture was so soporific that I couldn't keep my eyes open.
words.ex_cn: 那个单调乏味的讲座让我昏昏欲睡，眼睛都睁不开了。
words.en: A soporific substance or activity makes you feel sleepy.

words.tr: adj. 似是而非的；貌似有理的
words.ex: His argument is specious and misleading.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点看似有理但具有误导性。
words.en: Something that is specious seems to be good, sound, or correct but is actually wrong or false.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.ex: He felt the stigma of being unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了失业的耻辱。
words.en: A stigma is a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something, especially when this is unfair.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr: adj. 不动声色的；无动于衷的；不易激动的
words.ex: He remained stolid in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 面对逆境，他依然冷漠。
words.en: If you describe someone as stolid, you mean that they do not show much emotion or are not very exciting or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 有条纹的；有条痕的
words.ex: The rock had a striated surface, showing layers of different minerals.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石的表面有条纹，显示了不同矿物的层理。
words.en: Marked with striae; striped or grooved.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.ex: The rule subsumes all similar cases.
words.ex_cn: 这个规则涵盖所有类似的情况。
words.en: If something is subsumed within a larger group or class, it is included within it, rather than being considered as something separate.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.tr: adj. 心照不宣的；不作声的
words.ex: They have a tacit understanding about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们对规则有一种心照不宣的理解。
words.en: If you refer to someone's tacit agreement or approval, you mean they are agreeing to something or approving it without actually saying so, often because they are unwilling to admit to doing so.

words.ex: He is taciturn and rarely speaks.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默寡言，很少说话。
words.en: A taciturn person does not say very much and can seem unfriendly.

words.ex: His comment was tangential to the main topic.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论离题了。
words.en: If you describe something as tangential, you mean that it has only a slight or indirect connection with the thing you are concerned with, and is therefore not worth considering seriously.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.tr: n. 长篇抨击激烈演说
words.ex: He went on a tirade about slow internet.
words.ex_cn: 他大发雷霆，抱怨网速太慢。
words.en: A tirade is a long, angry speech of criticism or accusation.

words.ex: The cold weather put the animal into torpor.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的天气让动物陷入麻木状态。
words.en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.ex: He committed a transgression by stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了过错。
words.en: A transgression is an act that goes against a law, rule, or code of conduct; an offense.

words.ex: The truculence of the opponent's team was evident in their aggressive play.
words.ex_cn: 对手球队的好战性在他们激烈的比赛中显而易见。
words.en: The quality of being eager or quick to argue, fight, or start a conflict; aggressiveness.

words.tr: adj. 浮肿的；肿胀的；浮夸的
words.ex: His legs looked turgid after the long walk.
words.ex_cn: 他长时间走路后，双腿看起来浮肿了。
words.en: If you describe something such as a piece of writing or a speech as turgid, you think it is boring and difficult to understand because it is too serious or complicated.

words.tr: adj. 难以捍卫的；站不住脚的；不堪一击的
words.ex: His excuse was untenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口站不住脚。
words.en: If an argument, theory, or position is untenable, it cannot be defended or supported against criticism.

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.tr: adj. 乏味的；无味的；枯燥的
words.ex: The movie was vapid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影乏味又无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vapid, you are criticizing them because they are dull and uninteresting.

words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；说实话的；准确的
words.ex: He is a veracious person who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个诚实的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is veracious is truthful and honest.

words.ex: He gave a verbose answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对简单的问题给出了冗长的回答。
words.en: Using or containing more words than are necessary; long-winded.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: Honey is a viscous liquid.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是一种黏稠的液体。
words.en: A viscous liquid is thick and sticky and does not flow easily.

words.tr: v. 使变质；损害；使失效
words.ex: The poison vitiated the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒物使水源变质。
words.en: To vitiate something means to impair or reduce the quality, value, or effectiveness of it.

words.tr: adj. 充满辱骂的；责骂的
words.ex: His vituperative remarks were uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他那些责骂的话是多余的。
words.en: If you describe something that is said or written as vituperative, you mean that it is full of bitter criticism or anger.

words.ex: The alcohol is volatile and evaporates quickly.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是易挥发的，会迅速蒸发。
words.en: A volatile situation or person is one that is likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially by getting worse.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

words.ex: He is a zealot for environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心者。
words.en: A zealot is someone who is extremely enthusiastic about something, especially religion or politics.

chapters.name: Essential Words for the GRE

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.ex: The king decided to abdicate in favor of his son.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定退位，让位给他的儿子。
words.en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.ex: The project is in abeyance until next year.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目暂时搁置，直到明年。
words.en: A state of temporary disuse or suspension.

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.tr: v. 公开放弃；发誓断绝
words.ex: He had to abjure his old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不放弃他的旧信仰。
words.en: If you abjure something such as a belief or way of life, you state publicly that you will give it up or that you reject it.

words.ex: The process of abscission allows plants to shed leaves in response to environmental changes.
words.ex_cn: 脱落过程使植物能够根据环境变化脱落叶子。
words.en: The act of cutting off or the natural separation of a part from the main body, especially in plants.

words.ex: He absconded with the money last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚携款逃跑了。
words.en: If someone absconds from somewhere, they leave there quickly and secretly because they have something to hide or are afraid of being caught.

words.tr: adj. 有节制的；饮食有度的
words.ex: He is abstemious with sugar and eats little dessert.
words.ex_cn: 他对糖很节制，吃很少的甜点。
words.en: Someone who is abstemious avoids doing too much of something enjoyable, especially eating or drinking.

words.ex: He practices abstinence from alcohol.
words.ex_cn: 他戒酒。
words.en: The practice of restraining oneself from indulging in something, typically alcohol or sex.

words.tr: adj. 深不可测的；极坏的；糟透的
words.ex: The abysmal depth of the ocean scared the divers.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的深不可测吓到了潜水员。
words.en: If you describe a situation or the condition of something as abysmal, you think that it is very bad or poor in quality.

words.ex: He was adamant about not changing his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他坚定不移地不改变主意。
words.en: If someone is adamant about something, they are determined not to change their mind about it.

words.tr:
n. 附属物；
adj. 附属的；
words.ex: The printer is an adjunct to the computer.
words.ex_cn: 打印机是电脑的附属物。
words.en: Something that is added or attached to something else but is not essential to it.

words.ex: The teacher admonished the student to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师劝告学生完成作业。
words.en: To admonish someone means to tell them in a serious way that they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He adulterates milk with water to make more money.
words.ex_cn: 他往牛奶里加水以赚更多钱。
words.en: To make something poorer in quality by adding another substance to it.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.tr: v. 影响；“affect”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 染病的；受感动的；
words.ex: The rain affected the game.
words.ex_cn: 雨影响了比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as affected, you disapprove of the fact that they behave in an unnatural way that is intended to impress other people.

words.tr: n. 喜爱；类同；密切关系；亲和力
words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.ex: He tries to aggrandize himself by lying about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他通过吹嘘自己的成就来抬高自己。
words.en: To increase the power, status, or wealth of someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.tr: n. 敏捷；活泼；欣然；乐意
words.ex: He answered the question with alacrity.
words.ex_cn: 他愉快地回答了问题。
words.en: If you do something with alacrity, you do it quickly and eagerly.

words.ex: He is learning alchemy from an old book.
words.ex_cn: 他正从一本旧书中学习炼金术。
words.en: Alchemy is an ancient practice that aimed to transform base metals into gold and to discover a universal cure for disease and a way of extending life.

words.ex: She sang softly to allay his fears.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声唱歌以缓解他的恐惧。
words.en: If you allay someone's fears or doubts, you stop them feeling afraid or doubtful.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.tr:
n. 合金
v. 把…铸成合金
words.ex: He made a strong alloy from copper and zinc.
words.ex_cn: 他用铜和锌制造了一种坚固的合金。
words.en: An alloy is a metal made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: The two companies will amalgamate next month.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司下个月将合并。
words.en: If two or more organizations amalgamate, they join together and become one organization.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.tr: n. 矛盾心理；正反感情并存
words.ex: He feels ambivalence about moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他对搬到新城市感到矛盾。
words.en: Ambivalence is the state of having mixed feelings or contradictory attitudes about something or someone.

words.ex: The dessert was ambrosia, a true feast for the gods.
words.ex_cn: 这道甜点是特别美味的，真是神的食物。
words.en: In Greek and Roman mythology, ambrosia is the food or drink of the gods, often depicted as conferring longevity or immortality upon whoever consumed it. In a more general sense, it can refer to any especially delicious food or drink.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.tr: n. 便利设施；舒适条件；公共设施；
words.ex: The apartment has good amenities like a gym and a swimming pool.
words.ex_cn: 这套公寓有健身房和游泳池等便利设施。
words.en: An amenity is something that makes a place more pleasant or comfortable to live in.

words.ex: She wore an amulet around her neck for protection.
words.ex_cn: 她脖子上戴着护身符以求保护。
words.en: An amulet is an object that is worn because it is believed to protect against evil, danger, or disease.

words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.ex: The country fell into anarchy after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这个国家陷入了混乱。
words.en: Anarchy is a state of disorder due to absence or nonrecognition of authority or other controlling systems.

words.tr:
adj. 乏味无趣的；四平八稳的；不得罪人的；止痛的
n. 止痛药
words.ex: The meeting was anodyne and made everyone sleepy.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议乏味无趣，让所有人都犯困。
words.en: An anodyne is something that soothes, comforts, or relieves pain.

words.tr: adj. 偏离规则的；反常的
words.ex: The temperature was anomalous for this season.
words.ex_cn: 这个季节的温度异常。
words.en: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.tr:
n. 前情；先行词；祖先（常复）
adj. 在 ... 之前的
words.ex: The word 'dog' is the antecedent of 'it' in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 在这句话中，'dog' 是 'it' 的先行词。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.tr:
adj. （《圣经》中所说的大洪水前的）古老的；过时的
n.  年迈的人；不合时宜的人
words.ex: He uses an antediluvian typewriter to write letters.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台远古的打字机写信。
words.en: Belonging to the time before the biblical Flood; very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.ex: The apex of the mountain is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 山的最高点被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or top of something; the climax or culmination of something.

words.ex: The moon reached its apogee last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚月亮到达了远地点。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; a climax or culmination.

words.ex: The teacher often quoted an apothegm to emphasize a point.
words.ex_cn: 老师经常引用一句格言来强调一个观点。
words.en: An apothegm is a short, pithy, and instructive saying or formulation; a maxim.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: The appellation 'Doctor' is used to address a person with a medical degree.
words.ex_cn: 称呼 'Doctor' 用于称呼拥有医学学位的人。
words.en: An appellation is a name or title that someone or something is known by.

words.ex: His answer was apposite to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题很贴切。
words.en: Something that is apposite is suitable for or appropriate to what is happening or being discussed.

words.ex: He apprised her of the change.
words.ex_cn: 他通知了她这个变化。
words.en: If you are apprised of something, someone tells you about it.

words.ex: His work finally received the approbation of his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他的工作最终得到了同行的认可。
words.en: Official approval or agreement.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.tr:
adj. 恰当的；适宜的
adv. 恰当地；适宜地
prep. 关于；至于
words.ex: Your suggestion is apropos to our current needs.
words.ex_cn: 你的建议恰好符合我们当前的需求。
words.en: If something is apropos, it is suitable in a particular situation.

words.tr: n. 阿拉贝斯克舞姿；阿拉伯式花纹
words.ex: The artist used arabesque patterns to decorate the walls.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家使用蔓藤花纹来装饰墙壁。
words.en: An arabesque is a complex, ornate design of intertwined flowing lines, originally found in Arabic art, or a ballet position in which the dancer stands on one leg with the other leg extended behind.

words.ex: He loves archaeology and digs old artifacts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱考古学，挖掘古代文物。
words.en: Archaeology is the study of the societies and peoples of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: He speaks with great ardor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Ardor is a strong, intense feeling of love or enthusiasm for someone or something.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.tr: n. 行话；暗号； 隐语
words.ex: The boys use street argot to talk secretly.
words.ex_cn: 这些男孩用街头黑话秘密交谈。
words.en: A specialized language or set of expressions used by a particular group, especially thieves or other criminals.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.tr: n. 人工制品；手工艺品；加工品
words.ex: The museum has an ancient artifact.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一件古代文物。
words.en: An artifact is an object that is made by a person, especially something of historical or cultural interest.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；自然的；不做作的
words.ex: Her artless smile made everyone feel at ease.
words.ex_cn: 她那天真的微笑让每个人都感到轻松。
words.en: If you describe someone as artless, you mean that they are simple and honest, and do not try to deceive other people.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.ex: The asperity of the terrain made the hike difficult.
words.ex_cn: 地形的粗糙使得徒步旅行变得困难。
words.en: If you say something with asperity, you say it in a harsh, severe way.

words.tr: n. 中伤，诽谤（aspersion 的复数）
words.ex: He denied the aspersions about his honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了关于他诚实性的污蔑。
words.en: If someone casts aspersions on you, they suggest that you are not as good or honest as people think.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.ex: She drank water to assuage her thirst.
words.ex_cn: 她喝水来缓解口渴。
words.en: If you assuage an unpleasant feeling that someone has, you make them feel it less strongly. To assuage a problem or situation means to make it less intense or severe.

words.tr:
adj. 收敛性的；止血的；辛辣的；严厉的；涩的
n. 收敛剂； 止血药
words.ex: The astringent lotion helps reduce swelling.
words.ex_cn: 这种收敛性的爽肤水有助于减轻肿胀。
words.en: An astringent substance causes the contraction of body tissues, typically used to reduce bleeding from minor abrasions or as a skin toner.

words.tr: n. 收容所；避难所；精神病院；（政治）庇护
words.ex: The old building now serves as an asylum for the homeless.
words.ex_cn: 这栋旧建筑现在是无家可归者的收容所。
words.en: An asylum is a place where people who are in danger or who have no homes can go for safety and protection.

words.ex: His fear of the dark is an atavism from our ancestors.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗的恐惧是我们祖先的返祖现象。
words.en: The reappearance in an organism of characteristics of some remote ancestor that have been absent in intervening generations.

words.tr: v. 使减细；使减小；使减弱
words.ex: The wire attenuates as it gets longer.
words.ex_cn: 这根电线随着变长而变细。
words.en: To reduce the force, effect, or value of something.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.ex: His avarice knew no bounds, always seeking more wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪无止境，总是追求更多的财富。
words.en: Avarice is extremely strong desire for money and possessions.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: His avocation is painting on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他的业余爱好是周末画画。
words.en: An avocation is an activity that you do because you are interested in it, rather than as your main job.

words.tr: adj. 像伯伯（或叔叔）似的；长辈风范的；慈爱的
words.ex: His avuncular demeanor put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他慈祥的态度让每个人都感到轻松。
words.en: If someone is avuncular, they are kind and helpful towards younger or less experienced people, in a way that is typical of an uncle.

words.ex: The system is based on axiomatic rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个系统基于公理化的规则。
words.en: If something is axiomatic, it is accepted as true without needing to be proved.

words.ex: The party turned into a bacchanalian revelry.
words.ex_cn: 派对变成了狂饮作乐的狂欢。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of the god Bacchus; marked by drunken revelry and excess.

words.ex: The movie had a banal plot that everyone had seen before.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的剧情平庸得让人看过了无数次。
words.en: If you describe something as banal, you do not like it because you think that it is so ordinary that it is not at all effective or interesting.

words.tr:
n. 轻松说笑
v. 轻松说笑
words.ex: They enjoy banter during lunch break.
words.ex_cn: 他们在午餐休息时喜欢开玩笑。
words.en: the playful and friendly exchange of teasing remarks

words.ex: The bard sang a song about love and war.
words.ex_cn: 这位吟游诗人唱了一首关于爱情与战争的歌。
words.en: A bard is a poet, traditionally one who recites epic poems and is associated with a particular oral tradition.

words.tr: adj. 淫秽的；败坏风俗的
words.ex: The play contains some bawdy jokes that are not suitable for children.
words.ex_cn: 这出戏包含一些不适合儿童的猥亵笑话。
words.en: Bawdy humor or language refers to jokes or remarks about sex in a way that some people find offensive.

words.ex: She will beautify her garden with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她将用花朵美化她的花园。
words.en: To make something more attractive or beautiful.

words.tr: v. 把…打扮得俗里俗气
words.ex: She bedizened herself with gaudy jewelry.
words.ex_cn: 她用俗艳的珠宝打扮自己。
words.en: To bedizen means to dress or decorate in a showy or gaudy manner.

words.tr: n. 巨兽；庞然大物；巨头
words.ex: The company is a behemoth in the tech industry.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是科技行业中的巨无霸。
words.en: A behemoth is something that is extremely large and powerful, often referring to an organization, project, or thing that is so large it is difficult to manage or control.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.ex: The beneficent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: A beneficent person or organization helps people or results in something good.

words.tr: v. （使）分成两叉；（使）分成两支
words.ex: The river bifurcates into two smaller streams.
words.ex_cn: 这条河分岔成两条小溪。
words.en: To bifurcate means to divide or fork into two branches or parts.

words.ex: She used a lot of blandishment to get what she wanted.
words.ex_cn: 她使用了许多奉承话来达到她的目的。
words.en: Blandishment refers to the act of flattering or coaxing someone in order to persuade them to do something.

words.tr: adj. 对（享乐）感到厌倦的；（因司空见惯而）无动于衷的
words.ex: He is blase about the new phone because he has one every year.
words.ex_cn: 他对新手机无动于衷，因为他每年都换一部。
words.en: If you describe someone as blasé, you mean that they are not easily impressed, excited, or worried by things, usually because they have seen or experienced them before.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr: adj. 夸大的；言过其实的
words.ex: He gave a bombastic speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as bombastic, you are criticizing them for trying to impress other people by saying things that sound impressive but have little meaning.

words.tr: adj. 乡巴佬的；粗野的；粗鄙的
words.ex: His boorish behavior made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他粗俗的行为让所有人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as boorish, you mean their behavior is unrefined, insensitive, or rude.

words.tr:
adj. 牛的；似牛的；迟钝的
n. 牛；牛科动物
words.ex: The bovine grazed quietly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 那头牛在田野里安静地吃草。
words.en: Relating to or resembling cattle; slow or dull in manner.

words.tr: adj. 黄铜制的；黄铜色的；厚颜无耻的
words.ex: The brazen statue sparkled in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 这尊黄铜雕像在阳光下闪闪发光。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as brazen, you mean that they are doing something shocking or immoral in a very open way, without trying to hide it.

words.tr:
v. 钻孔开口；开瓶；提出一个话题讨论
n. 胸针；钻头
words.ex: He broached a hole in the metal plate.
words.ex_cn: 他在金属板上钻了一个孔。
words.en: To broach a subject is to mention it in order to start a discussion on it. A broach is also a tool used for making holes.

words.ex: He loves the bucolic life in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢乡村的田园生活。
words.en: Relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life.

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.tr:
v. 擦亮；磨光
n. 光泽
words.ex: He burnishes the old metal every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末都抛光那块旧金属。
words.en: To burnish something means to polish it and make it shine by rubbing it.

words.tr:
n. 扶墙；拱壁
v. 支持
words.ex: The old wall needs a buttress to stay standing.
words.ex_cn: 这面旧墙需要一个支撑物来保持不倒。
words.en: A buttress is a structure built against or projecting from a wall which serves to support or reinforce the wall. As a verb, to buttress means to support or strengthen something.

words.ex: The cacophonous noise made her cover her ears.
words.ex_cn: 刺耳的噪音让她捂住了耳朵。
words.en: If you describe a mixture of sounds as cacophonous, you mean that they are loud and unpleasant.

words.ex: He would often cadge cigarettes from strangers.
words.ex_cn: 他经常向陌生人乞讨香烟。
words.en: To cadge means to ask for and obtain something without paying for it, often by persuading someone to give it to you.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.ex: He spread calumny about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: A false statement made to damage someone's reputation.

words.ex: The story was a complete canard, spread by those with vested interests.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事完全是一个谣言，是由那些有既得利益的人散布的。
words.en: A canard is a false or baseless story or piece of information, especially one that is deliberately misleading.

words.tr: n. 教规；准则；真作集；精品集；大教堂教士
words.ex: The church follows the canon of its faith.
words.ex_cn: 教会遵循其信仰的教规。
words.en: A canon is a rule or principle that is considered to be established, accepted, or authoritative, especially in the fields of religion, literature, or law.

words.ex: I can't swim.
words.ex_cn: 我不会游泳。
words.en: Cannot; used to indicate that something is not possible or allowed.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；爱吵架的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: The cantankerous old man yells at his neighbors every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那位脾气暴躁的老人每天早上都对邻居大喊大叫。
words.en: Someone who is cantankerous is bad-tempered and quarrels with people.

words.tr: adj. 变化无常的；任性的
words.ex: He is capricious and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他喜怒无常，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is capricious often changes their mind unexpectedly.

words.tr: adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑剔的
words.ex: He made a captious comment about the small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对一个小错误发表了挑剔的评论。
words.en: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.tr: adj. 肉体的；肉欲的；性欲的
words.ex: He denied any carnal desires.
words.ex_cn: 他否认有任何肉体的欲望。
words.en: Carnal is used to describe things relating to the body or to sexual desires, often in contrast to spiritual or intellectual matters.

words.ex: The teacher gave castigation to the student who cheated.
words.ex_cn: 老师惩罚了作弊的学生。
words.en: Castigation is the act of criticizing or punishing someone severely.

words.ex: The earthquake was a sudden cataclysm.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场突如其来的灾难。
words.en: A cataclysm is an event that causes great damage or makes a big change to something.

words.ex: The enzyme acts as a catalyst in the reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶在反应中充当催化剂。
words.en: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a person or thing that precipitates a change.

words.tr: adj. 绝对的；确定无疑的；分类的
words.ex: He gave a categorical no to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了明确的拒绝。
words.en: If you are categorical about something, you state your views very definitely and firmly.

words.tr: n. 政党会议；核心小组会议；特别利益集团
words.ex: The caucus decided on a new strategy for the upcoming election.
words.ex_cn: 党团会议决定了一项新的选举策略。
words.en: A caucus is a meeting of the members of a political party to select candidates or decide policy.

words.ex: The study found a causal link between smoking and lung cancer.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究发现了吸烟与肺癌之间的因果关系。
words.en: A causal factor or event is one that causes or leads to something else.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；苛性的；尖酸刻薄的
n. 腐蚀剂
words.ex: The caustic liquid burned through the metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种腐蚀性的液体腐蚀了金属。
words.en: A caustic substance is able to burn or destroy organic tissue by chemical action. Caustic remarks are extremely critical, sarcastic, or bitter.

words.tr: adj. 天空的；天体的；天国的；
words.ex: The celestial lights shone brightly in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 天空中的光芒在夜空中明亮地闪耀。
words.en: Relating to the sky or the heavens; belonging or relating to heaven as the abode of the gods.

words.ex: The centrifugal force pushes the water outward.
words.ex_cn: 离心力把水向外推。
words.en: Moving or tending to move away from a center.

words.ex: The centripetal force keeps the ball moving in a circle.
words.ex_cn: 向心力使球保持圆周运动。
words.en: Moving or tending to move toward a center.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.ex: The coach chastened the team for their poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 教练因球队表现不佳而惩罚了他们。
words.en: If you are chastened by something, it makes you regret that you have behaved badly or stupidly.

words.ex: He resorted to chicanery to win the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠狡辩赢得了争论。
words.en: The use of trickery to achieve a political, financial, or legal purpose.

words.tr: n. 骑士精神；骑士制度；
words.ex: He showed chivalry by helping the lady carry her bags.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助那位女士提包，展现了骑士精神。
words.en: Chivalry is a set of qualities such as bravery, courtesy, honor, and gallantry toward women, associated with the medieval institution of knighthood.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；无礼的；脾气坏的
words.ex: His churlish behavior at the meeting was uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的粗鲁行为是完全没有必要的。
words.en: If someone is churlish, they are rude, bad-tempered, and impolite.

words.ex: He took a circuitous route to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他绕了远路以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A circuitous route, journey, or piece of writing is longer than it needs to be because it is not direct.

words.tr:
n. 透视者；千里眼的人；有洞察力的人
adj.  透视的；有洞察力的
words.ex: The clairvoyant claimed to foresee the future events.
words.ex_cn: 这位能预知未来的人声称可以预见未来的事件。
words.en: A clairvoyant is someone who claims to have the ability to perceive events in the future or beyond normal sensory contact.

words.tr:
n. 喧嚷；大声的要求
v. 喧嚷；大声地要求
words.ex: The crowd made a loud clamor for justice.
words.ex_cn: 人群为正义发出大声喧哗。
words.en: If people are clamoring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.

words.tr: n. 派系；小集团；小圈子
words.ex: She found it hard to break into the clique at school.
words.ex_cn: 她发现很难融入学校的小圈子。
words.en: A clique is a small group of people who spend their time together and do not allow others to join them.

words.tr:
n. （修道院等的）回廊；修道院
v. 关在…（修道院等）里；使…与世隔绝
words.ex: The monks lived a life of quiet contemplation in the cloister.
words.ex_cn: 修道士们在修道院中过着宁静沉思的生活。
words.en: A cloister is a covered walk in a convent, monastery, college, or cathedral, typically with a wall on one side and a colonnade open to a quadrangle on the other.

words.ex: The blood will coagulate if it is left outside the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液如果留在体外，就会凝结。
words.en: If a liquid coagulates, it becomes thick and almost solid.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.ex: The coda of the symphony brought the concert to a powerful conclusion.
words.ex_cn: 交响乐的终曲为音乐会带来了强有力的结束。
words.en: The concluding passage of a piece or movement, typically forming an addition to the basic structure.

words.ex: The government decided to codify the old laws.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定将旧法律编纂成典。
words.en: To codify means to arrange laws, rules, etc. into a systematic code.

words.tr: adj. 认识的；知晓的；察知的
words.ex: He is cognizant of the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他了解这些规则。
words.en: If someone is cognizant of something, they are aware of it or understand it.

words.tr: n. 拼贴画；拼贴艺术；杂烩
words.ex: He made a collage from old magazine pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧杂志的图片做了一幅拼贴画。
words.en: A collage is a picture that has been made by sticking pieces of colored paper, cloth, or photographs onto a surface.

words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.ex: He read a compendium of math rules.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本数学规则的汇编。
words.en: A compendium is a short but complete collection of information, usually in a book.

words.tr: adj. 自满的；自鸣得意的
words.ex: He is complacent about his good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的好成绩感到自满。
words.en: A complacent person is very pleased with themselves or feels that they do not need to do anything about a situation, even though the situation may be uncertain or dangerous.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: The child was compliant and followed all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子很顺从，遵守了所有规则。
words.en: If someone or something is compliant, they act in accordance with rules, standards, or laws.

words.tr: n. 良心的责备；后悔；悔恨
words.ex: He felt no compunction about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他撒谎骗朋友时毫无愧疚。
words.en: A feeling of guilt or moral scruple that prevents or follows the doing of something bad.

words.ex: The spoon has a concave surface.
words.ex_cn: 勺子有一个凹的表面。
words.en: A concave surface is curved inward, like the inside of a bowl.

words.ex: He gave a conciliatory smile to calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他露出和解的微笑来平息争执。
