words.en: Archaeology is the study of the societies and peoples of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: The hero in the story is an archetype of courage.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的英雄是勇气的原型。
words.en: An archetype is a very typical example of a certain person or thing.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ARM/ARMA

words.ex: The armistice was signed to end the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 停战协议的签署结束了冲突。
words.en: An armistice is a formal agreement of warring parties to stop fighting. It is not necessarily the end of a war, since it might be just a cessation of hostilities while an attempt is made to negotiate a lasting peace.

words.tr: n. 舰队；西班牙无敌舰队
words.ex: The Spanish armada sailed to attack England.
words.ex_cn: 西班牙无敌舰队驶向进攻英格兰。
words.en: An armada is a large group of armed ships that are ready for battle.

words.tr: n. 裁减军备；解除武装；缴械
words.ex: The two countries agreed on disarmament to reduce weapons.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家同意进行裁军以减少武器。
words.en: The reduction or withdrawal of military forces and weapons.

words.ex: The knight wore heavy armor in the battle.
words.ex_cn: 骑士在战斗中穿着沉重的盔甲。
words.en: Armor is a protective covering that is used to prevent damage from being inflicted to an object, individual, or vehicle by direct contact weapons or projectiles, usually during combat.

words.ex: The armadillo rolled itself into a ball for protection.
words.ex_cn: 犰狳为了保护自己蜷缩成一个球。
words.en: An armadillo is a small animal whose body is covered with large bony plates and which can roll itself into a ball to protect itself from danger.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ART

words.ex: The artisan makes handmade pottery.
words.ex_cn: 这位工匠制作手工陶器。
words.en: An artisan is someone who makes things by hand, especially using traditional methods.

words.tr: n. 人工制品；手工艺品；加工品
words.ex: The museum has an ancient artifact.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一件古代文物。
words.en: An artifact is an object that is made by a person, especially something of historical or cultural interest.

words.tr: phrase. 一种19世纪末20世纪初流行的装饰艺术风格，以流畅的曲线、自然形态和有机图案为特征，中文称为‘新艺术风格’
words.ex: The building was designed in the Art Nouveau style, characterized by its intricate floral patterns.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑采用新艺术运动风格设计，以其复杂的花卉图案为特征。
words.en: Art Nouveau is an international style of art, architecture, and applied art, especially the decorative arts, that was most popular between 1890 and 1910.

words.ex: The flowers in the garden are artificial.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的花是人造的。
words.en: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.ex: He used artifice to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计赢得了比赛。
words.en: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially as used to trick or deceive others.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ASTR/ASTER

words.tr:
n. 星号
v. 给…注上星号
words.ex: She put an asterisk next to the word.
words.ex_cn: 她在那个词旁边加了一个星号。
words.en: An asterisk is a symbol (*) used in text to indicate a footnote or to highlight something important.

words.ex: The astral plane is believed to be a level of existence beyond the physical world.
words.ex_cn: 人们相信星界是超越物质世界的一个存在层面。
words.en: Relating to or resembling the stars.

words.ex: The astronaut walked on the moon.
words.ex_cn: 这名宇航员在月球上行走。
words.en: An astronaut is a person who is trained to travel in a spacecraft.

words.ex: He reads his horoscope every morning because he believes in astrology.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看星座运势，因为他相信占星术。
words.en: Astrology is the study of the movements and relative positions of celestial bodies interpreted as having an influence on human affairs and the natural world.

words.ex: He loves watching stars and learning astronomy.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢看星星并学习天文学。
words.en: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial objects, space, and the physical universe as a whole.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes AUD/AUDI/AUS

words.ex: The school concert was held in the auditorium.
words.ex_cn: 学校的音乐会是在礼堂举行的。
words.en: An auditorium is the part of a theatre, concert hall, or other public building in which the audience sits.

words.ex: The whisper was barely audible.
words.ex_cn: 那耳语几乎听不见。
words.en: If a sound is audible, it is loud enough for you to hear it.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.ex: He had the audacity to lie to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老板撒谎。
words.en: Audacity is the willingness to take bold risks, often in a way that shocks or surprises people.

words.ex: The doctor performed auscultation to check the patient's lungs.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了听诊以检查病人的肺部。
words.en: Auscultation is the act of listening to the internal sounds of the body, usually using a stethoscope, as a method of diagnosis.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes AUG/AUX

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.ex: He was born in August.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在八月。
words.en: August is the eighth month of the Gregorian calendar, following July and preceding September.

words.tr:
v. 预言；预测
n. （古罗马）占兆官；占卜师
words.ex: The early reviews augur well for the success of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 早期的评论预示着这部电影将取得成功。
words.en: to predict or foretell, especially from signs or omens

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 辅助物；附属物；助动词
words.ex: He used an auxiliary verb to form the past tense.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个助动词来构成过去时。
words.en: An auxiliary is a person or thing that provides additional help or support.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes AUTO-

words.ex: The door opens automatically when you get close.
words.ex_cn: 当你靠近时，门会自动打开。
words.en: If something happens automatically, it happens as a part of the normal process or system, without needing to be started by someone.

words.tr:
n. 亲笔签名；亲笔稿
v. 亲笔签名于；亲笔书写
words.ex: He asked the singer for an autograph.
words.ex_cn: 他向歌手要了一张签名。
words.en: An autograph is a person's own signature, especially that of a famous person, or a manuscript in the author's own handwriting.

words.ex: The autonomic nervous system controls involuntary functions like heart rate.
words.ex_cn: 自主神经系统控制着像心率这样的非自主功能。
words.en: Relating to or controlled by the autonomic nervous system.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.ex: He wrote his autobiography when he was 70.
words.ex_cn: 他70岁时写了自传。
words.en: An autobiography is a book about the life of a person, written by that person.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes BE-

words.tr: adj. 昏沉的，糊里糊涂的; v. 使……迷惑；使……烂醉（befuddle 的过去分词）
words.ex: He was befuddled by the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他被这个简单的数学题搞糊涂了。
words.en: If someone is befuddled, they cannot understand something or think clearly about it, often because they are tired or have drunk too much alcohol.

words.tr: v. 诱骗；消遣；迷住；消磨
words.ex: He beguiles her with sweet words.
words.ex_cn: 他用甜言蜜语哄骗她。
words.en: If someone beguiles you, they charm you in a way that makes you trust them or like them, often so that they can deceive you.

words.tr: v．玷污，诽谤：弄脏或损害某人或某物的名声。
words.ex: Her reputation was besmirched by the false accusations.
words.ex_cn: 她的名声被这些虚假的指控玷污了。
words.en: If something besmirches someone or something, it damages their reputation or good name.

words.ex: The streets were bedecked with colorful banners.
words.ex_cn: 街道上装饰着五彩缤纷的横幅。
words.en: If a place is bedecked with things, it has many decorations or bright colours in it.

words.tr: v. 把…打扮得俗里俗气
words.ex: She bedizened herself with gaudy jewelry.
words.ex_cn: 她用俗艳的珠宝打扮自己。
words.en: To bedizen means to dress or decorate in a showy or gaudy manner.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes BEL/BELL

words.ex: The rebel fought against the king's rules.
words.ex_cn: 这位叛逆者反抗国王的法令。
words.en: A rebel is a person who opposes or fights against people in authority.

words.ex: He is bellicose when he drinks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了时就好战。
words.en: Having or showing a tendency to argue or fight.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: The house was built in the antebellum period.
words.ex_cn: 这座房子建于内战前时期。
words.en: Belonging to the period before a war, especially the American Civil War.

words.tr: adj. 美国南北战争后的
words.ex: The postbellum era saw significant economic and social changes.
words.ex_cn: 南北战争后的时期见证了显著的经济和社会变革。
words.en: Relating to the period after a war, especially the American Civil War.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes BEN-/BON-

words.tr: adj. 美国南北战争后的
words.ex: The postbellum era saw significant economic and social changes.
words.ex_cn: 南北战争后的时期见证了显著的经济和社会变革。
words.en: Relating to the period after a war, especially the American Civil War.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes BI-

words.tr: adj. 美国南北战争后的
words.ex: The postbellum era saw significant economic and social changes.
words.ex_cn: 南北战争后的时期见证了显著的经济和社会变革。
words.en: Relating to the period after a war, especially the American Civil War.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes BIO

words.ex: The biologist studies animals in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这位生物学家在森林里研究动物。
words.en: A biologist is a scientist who studies living organisms and their relationship to their environment.

words.ex: The biosphere includes all living things on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 生物圈包括地球上所有生物。
words.en: The biosphere is the part of the Earth's surface and atmosphere in which plants and animals can live.

words.ex: The robot uses bionics to move like a human.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人使用仿生学来像人类一样移动。
words.en: Bionics is the study of mechanical systems that function like living organisms or parts of living organisms.

words.ex: The biotic factors affect the growth of plants.
words.ex_cn: 生物因素影响植物的生长。
words.en: Relating to or resulting from living organisms.

words.tr: adj. 共栖的；共生的；互惠互利的；
words.ex: The clownfish and the sea anemone have a symbiotic relationship.
words.ex_cn: 小丑鱼和海葵有共栖关系。
words.en: Involving interaction between two different organisms living in close physical association, typically to the advantage of both.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes BREV

words.ex: He abbreviates the word 'example' as 'ex.'.
words.ex_cn: 他把单词 'example' 缩写为 'ex.'。
words.en: To abbreviate something means to make it shorter, especially by using a particular word or phrase to represent it.

words.ex: He used an abbreviation for 'company' in his note.
words.ex_cn: 他在笔记中用了'company'的缩写。
words.en: An abbreviation is a shortened form of a word or phrase.

words.ex: The brevity of his speech surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他讲话的短暂让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Brevity is the use of only a few words to say something, or the quality of being short in time.

words.tr: n. （罗马教皇的）谕令；二全音符，短弱音符; n. （Breve）人名；（意）布雷韦
words.ex: The composer used a breve to indicate a long note.
words.ex_cn: 作曲家使用二全音符来表示一个长音符。
words.en: A breve is a musical note that is typically twice as long as a whole note. In linguistics, it refers to a diacritical mark (˘) used to indicate a short or unstressed vowel.

words.ex: The priest carries a breviary for daily prayers.
words.ex_cn: 牧师带着每日祈祷书进行日常祈祷。
words.en: A breviary is a book containing the prayers, hymns, psalms, and readings for the canonical hours of the Roman Catholic Church.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CAP/CAPT/CEPT/CIP

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability or potential to do it.

words.ex: The police intercepted the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察拦截了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If you intercept someone or something that is going from one place to another, you stop them before they get there.

words.tr: adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑剔的
words.ex: He made a captious comment about the small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对一个小错误发表了挑剔的评论。
words.en: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.

words.tr: n. (尤指道德方面的)戒律；准则
words.ex: He follows the precept to be kind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循要善良的教诲。
words.en: A precept is a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought.

words.tr:
v. 记录；准确地描述；俘虏；吸引；
n. 抓捕；
words.ex: The camera can capture the moment clearly.
words.ex_cn: 相机可以清晰地记录下这一瞬间。
words.en: To capture someone or something means to catch them, especially after a chase.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CAP/CAPIT

words.ex: The income per capita is high in this country.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的人均收入很高。
words.en: Per capita is used to describe the average amount of something per person in a particular place.

words.ex: The Capitol is the seat of the United States Congress.
words.ex_cn: 国会是美国国会的所在地。
words.en: A building in which a state legislative body meets; also, the building in which the United States Congress meets in Washington, D.C.

words.ex: The villain tried to decapitate the hero with a sword.
words.ex_cn: 反派试图用剑砍下英雄的头。
words.en: To decapitate someone means to cut off their head.

words.ex: The army will not capitulate to the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 军队不会向敌人投降。
words.en: If you capitulate, you stop resisting and do what someone else wants you to do.

words.ex: The captain sailed the ship across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 船长驾驶船穿越了海洋。
words.en: A captain is the person in charge of a ship or an aircraft, or a leader of a team or group.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CARD/CORD

words.ex: The cardiac patient needs to rest daily.
words.ex_cn: 这位心脏病人需要每天休息。
words.en: Cardiac means relating to the heart.

words.ex: He specialized in cardiology after completing his medical degree.
words.ex_cn: 他在完成医学学位后专攻心脏病学。
words.en: Cardiology is the branch of medicine that deals with diseases and abnormalities of the heart.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

words.ex: The two countries reached a concord on trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上达成了一致。
words.en: Concord is a state of agreement or harmony between people or groups.

words.tr: adj. 不调和的；不一致的；不和谐的
words.ex: The two voices sounded discordant.
words.ex_cn: 这两声音听起来不和谐。
words.en: Something that is discordant is strange or unpleasant because it does not fit in with other things.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CARN

words.tr: adj. 肉体的；肉欲的；性欲的
words.ex: He denied any carnal desires.
words.ex_cn: 他否认有任何肉体的欲望。
words.en: Carnal is used to describe things relating to the body or to sexual desires, often in contrast to spiritual or intellectual matters.

words.ex: She gave her mom a red carnation on Mother's Day.
words.ex_cn: 她在母亲节送了妈妈一朵红色的康乃馨。
words.en: A carnation is a type of flower with a sweet smell, which is often worn on special occasions such as weddings or funerals.

words.ex: Lions are carnivores that eat meat.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是吃肉的食肉动物。
words.en: A carnivore is an animal that eats the flesh of other animals.

words.tr:
adj. 化身的；人体化的
v. 化身为；体现
words.ex: He is the incarnate form of justice.
words.ex_cn: 他是正义的化身。
words.en: If you say that someone is a quality incarnate, you mean that they represent that quality or are typical of it in an extreme form.

words.ex: The war caused terrible carnage on both sides.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争在双方都造成了惨烈的大屠杀。
words.en: The killing of a large number of people, especially in a violent way.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CATA-

words.ex: The enzyme acts as a catalyst in the reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶在反应中充当催化剂。
words.en: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a person or thing that precipitates a change.

words.ex: The old man has a cataract in his right eye.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人右眼有白内障。
words.en: A cataract is a medical condition in which the lens of the eye becomes progressively opaque, resulting in blurred vision. It can also refer to a large waterfall.

words.tr:
n. 弹弓；石弩；弹射器
v. 用弩炮（等）发射；（使）突然处于…情况
words.ex: The boys used a catapult to launch stones.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们用投石机发射石头。
words.en: A catapult is a device used to throw or hurl a projectile a great distance without the aid of explosive devices—particularly various types of ancient and medieval siege engines. In a more modern context, it can also refer to a device that launches aircraft from a ship, or metaphorically, to propel someone to fame or success suddenly.

words.ex: The earthquake was a sudden cataclysm.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场突如其来的灾难。
words.en: A cataclysm is an event that causes great damage or makes a big change to something.

words.ex: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: A catastrophic event or situation is one that causes great damage or suffering.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CED/CEED/CESS

words.tr: v. 割让（领土）；放弃（权力）
words.ex: He will cede his land to the government.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地让给政府。
words.en: To give up control or possession of something, especially land or territory, often as a result of war or negotiation.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.tr:
n. 前情；先行词；祖先（常复）
adj. 在 ... 之前的
words.ex: The word 'dog' is the antecedent of 'it' in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 在这句话中，'dog' 是 'it' 的先行词。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CELER

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.tr: n. 促进剂；触媒; adj. 促进的；加速的；催速的
words.ex: The use of accelerants in arson cases is a serious crime.
words.ex_cn: 在纵火案中使用助燃剂是严重的犯罪行为。
words.en: An accelerant is a substance that is used to increase the speed of a process, especially a chemical reaction or the spread of a fire.

words.ex: The project was completed with remarkable celerity.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目以惊人的速度完成了。
words.en: Celerity is the quality of being swift or rapid.

words.ex: The sudden deceleration of the car caused the passengers to lurch forward.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的突然减速使乘客们向前冲去。
words.en: A reduction in speed or rate.

words.tr: n. 渐速音; adj. 渐速的; adv. 渐速地
words.ex: The conductor signaled the orchestra to play accelerando.
words.ex_cn: 指挥示意管弦乐队渐速演奏。
words.en: (used as a direction in music) gradually increasing in speed.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CENTR

words.ex: The circles are concentric and share the same center.
words.ex_cn: 这些圆是同心的，拥有同一个中心。
words.en: Having a common center, as circles or spheres.

words.ex: The centrifugal force pushes the water outward.
words.ex_cn: 离心力把水向外推。
words.en: Moving or tending to move away from a center.

words.ex: The centripetal force keeps the ball moving in a circle.
words.ex_cn: 向心力使球保持圆周运动。
words.en: Moving or tending to move toward a center.

words.ex: You must concentrate on your homework.
words.ex_cn: 你必须集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you concentrate on something, you give it your full attention and think about it carefully.

words.ex: The earth is not centric to the solar system.
words.ex_cn: 地球并不是太阳系的中心。
words.en: If something is centric, it is central or focused around a particular point or area.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CENT-

words.ex: The pencil is 15 centimeters long.
words.ex_cn: 这支铅笔有15厘米长。
words.en: A centimeter is a unit of length in the metric system equal to one hundredth of a meter.

words.tr: n. 一百周年纪念；一百年；
words.ex: The town held a party for the centenary of its founding.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇为建镇一百周年纪念举行了派对。
words.en: A centenary is the one hundredth anniversary of a significant event.

words.ex: The centenarian walks every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位百岁老人每天早上散步。
words.en: A centenarian is a person who is 100 years old or older.

words.ex: The first century had no computers.
words.ex_cn: 第一个世纪没有电脑。
words.en: A century is a period of one hundred years.

words.tr:
adj. 一百年的
n. 百年纪念
words.ex: The city held a centennial parade to celebrate 100 years.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市举行了一场百年游行来庆祝一百周年。
words.en: A centennial is the one-hundredth anniversary of an event, or something that happens every hundred years.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CERN

words.tr:
n. 担忧；关注；
v. 涉及；
words.ex: His main concern is his child's safety.
words.ex_cn: 他主要的担忧是孩子的安全。
words.en: If something concerns you, it worries you or causes you to feel anxious.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.tr: adj. 有辨别力的；能洞悉的；眼光敏锐的； v. “discern”的现在分词；
words.ex: She is a discerning shopper who always finds the best quality.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有辨别力的购物者，总是能找到最好的质量。
words.en: If you describe someone as discerning, you mean that they are able to judge which things of a particular kind are good and which are bad.

words.tr: adj. 难识别的；觉察不出的
words.ex: The distant mountains were indiscernible in the fog.
words.ex_cn: 远处的山在雾中难以辨认。
words.en: If something is indiscernible, it is impossible to see or understand clearly.

words.tr: adv. 不在乎地；漠不关心地
words.ex: He spoke unconcernedly about the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他对事故漠不关心地谈论着。
words.en: In a manner that shows a lack of concern or worry.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CERT

words.ex: The doctor will certify that you are healthy.
words.ex_cn: 医生将证明你身体健康。
words.en: To officially declare something to be true, correct, or genuine, often in writing.

words.ex: He received a certificate for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证书。
words.en: A certificate is an official document attesting a fact, in particular.

words.ex: There is no certainty that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天是否会下雨还没有确定。
words.en: Something that is certain is sure to happen or is definitely true.

words.ex: He spoke with certitude about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他对于这个答案说话时充满确信。
words.en: A feeling of being certain or convinced about something.

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CHRON

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.tr: n. 计时机；精密的时计；天文钟
words.ex: He uses a chronometer to measure time precisely.
words.ex_cn: 他使用精密计时器来精确测量时间。
words.en: A chronometer is a very accurate clock, especially one used for scientific purposes or for measuring time at sea.

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的事；过时的事或人
words.ex: The knight in the movie uses a smartphone, which is an anachronism.
words.ex_cn: 电影中的骑士使用智能手机，这是不合时宜的。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of place in terms of time or chronology, such as an object, a custom, or an idea that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it is placed.

words.tr: n. 年代学；年表；按年代次序的排列
words.ex: He wrote the chronology of ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他写了古罗马的年代顺序。
words.en: Chronology is the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CID/CIS

words.ex: The police investigated the homicide case.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了这起凶杀案。
words.en: The act of killing another person, especially when it is considered a crime.

words.ex: She cut the paper with scissors.
words.ex_cn: 她用剪刀剪了纸。
words.en: Scissors are a tool used for cutting paper, cloth, hair, etc., consisting of two sharp blades fastened together in the middle so that the sharp edges slide against each other.

words.tr: v. 驱（魔）；除去（痛苦的想法等）
words.ex: The priest tried to exorcise the demon from the house.
words.ex_cn: 牧师试图将恶魔从房子里驱逐出去。
words.en: To exorcise means to drive out or attempt to drive out (a supposed evil spirit) from a person or place.

words.ex: The excision of the tumor was successful.
words.ex_cn: 肿瘤的切除手术很成功。
words.en: The act of cutting out or off, especially the surgical removal of a part of the body.

words.ex: The process of abscission allows plants to shed leaves in response to environmental changes.
words.ex_cn: 脱落过程使植物能够根据环境变化脱落叶子。
words.en: The act of cutting off or the natural separation of a part from the main body, especially in plants.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CIRCU-/CIRCUM-

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.tr: n. 音调符号; adj. 弯曲的；有声调符号的; v. 标有抑扬音符；弯曲
words.ex: The circumflex accent is used in French to indicate a rising and then falling pitch.
words.ex_cn: 法语中使用抑扬音符来表示先升后降的音调。
words.en: A circumflex is a mark (^) placed over a vowel in some languages to indicate a particular pronunciation, length, or stress, or over a consonant in some scripts to indicate a particular sound.

words.ex: He took a circuitous route to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他绕了远路以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A circuitous route, journey, or piece of writing is longer than it needs to be because it is not direct.

words.tr: n. 迂回累赘的陈述；遁词
words.ex: He used circumlocution to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用绕圈子的说法来避免回答问题。
words.en: Circumlocution is the use of many words where fewer would do, especially in a deliberate attempt to be vague or evasive.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CIT/CITAT

words.ex: He cited a book in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他在文章中引用了一本书。
words.en: To cite something means to quote it or mention it as evidence or proof of what you are saying.

words.ex: The passage from the book is highly citable.
words.ex_cn: 这本书中的这段话非常值得引用。
words.en: Capable of being cited or quoted, especially as an authority or example.

words.ex: He gave a citation from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他引用了这本书中的一段话。
words.en: A citation is a reference to a published or unpublished source (not always the original source). More precisely, a citation is an abbreviated alphanumeric expression embedded in the body of an intellectual work that denotes an entry in the bibliographic references section of the work for the purpose of acknowledging the relevance of the works of others to the topic of discussion at the spot where the citation appears.

words.ex: The child recites the poem every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子每天早上背诵这首诗。
words.en: To repeat aloud or declaim (a poem or passage) from memory before an audience.

words.tr: adj. 宣叙调; 背诵的，吟诵的，叙述的
words.ex: The opera singer performed a recitative section with great emotion.
words.ex_cn: 这位歌剧演唱家用极大的情感表演了一段宣叙调。
words.en: A style of delivery in which a singer is allowed to adopt the rhythms of ordinary speech. It is used in opera, oratorio, cantata, and other vocal works.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CIVI

words.tr: adj. 国内的；公民的；民用的；
words.ex: The country is recovering from a civil war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在从一场内战中恢复。
words.en: relating to ordinary citizens and their concerns, as distinct from military or ecclesiastical matters.

words.ex: He volunteers for civic projects in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他为家乡的市民项目做志愿者。
words.en: Relating to a city or town, especially its administration; relating to the duties or activities of people in relation to their town, city, or local area.

words.tr: v. 使开化；使文明；教化
words.ex: They tried to civilize the wild tribe.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图使这个原始部落文明化。
words.en: To civilize means to bring a place or people to a stage of social, cultural, and moral development considered to be more advanced.

words.ex: The civilian population stayed safe during the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 平民在冲突期间保持安全。
words.en: A civilian is a person who is not a member of the military or of a police or firefighting force.

words.ex: He showed civility even when he was angry.
words.ex_cn: 即使他生气了，他依然表现出礼貌。
words.en: Civility is polite, reasonable, and respectful behaviour.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CLAM/CLAIM

words.ex: He exclaim when he saw the surprise.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到惊喜时，他大喊起来。
words.en: If you exclaim, you say something suddenly and loudly, often because you are surprised, excited, or angry.

words.ex: He shouted an exclamation of surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他惊讶地喊了一声。
words.en: An exclamation is a sound, word, or sentence that is spoken suddenly, loudly, or emphatically and that expresses excitement, admiration, shock, or anger.

words.tr:
n. 喧嚷；大声的要求
v. 喧嚷；大声地要求
words.ex: The crowd made a loud clamor for justice.
words.ex_cn: 人群为正义发出大声喧哗。
words.en: If people are clamoring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr: n. 欢呼，喝彩；鼓掌欢呼表示通过
words.ex: The decision was met with loud acclamation.
words.ex_cn: 这一决定受到了热烈的欢呼。
words.en: Acclamation is a loud and enthusiastic approval or welcome, typically given by a group of people.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CLEMEN

words.ex: The judge showed clemency and reduced the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 法官表现出宽大，减轻了刑罚。
words.en: Clemency is kindness and forgiveness, especially towards someone who could be punished severely.

words.ex: The clement teacher gave students extra time.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师给了学生更多时间。
words.en: Mild or merciful in disposition or character; lenient; compassionate.

words.ex: The weather was inclement, so we stayed home.
words.ex_cn: 天气恶劣，所以我们待在家里。
words.en: (of weather) unpleasantly cold or wet.

words.tr: n. 严酷，气候严酷；天气险恶
words.ex: The inclemency of the weather made the journey treacherous.
words.ex_cn: 恶劣的天气使得旅途充满危险。
words.en: The quality of being inclement, especially severe or harsh weather.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CLAUD/CLAUS/CLOS/CLUD/CLUS

words.ex: The sentence has a clause that explains why he left.
words.ex_cn: 这个句子有一个解释他为什么离开的从句。
words.en: A clause is a particular section of a legal document such as a contract, will, or treaty, that contains a condition or stipulation.

words.ex: The rule excludes children under 12.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则排除了12岁以下的孩子。
words.en: To exclude someone or something means to prevent them from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

words.tr: n. 隐居者；遁世者；隐士
words.ex: He lives as a recluse in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他住在树林里，过着隐居的生活。
words.en: A recluse is a person who lives alone and avoids other people.

words.ex: The leaf occluded the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 叶子堵住了管道。
words.en: To occlude means to block or stop up a passage, opening, or vessel.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CLI/CLIN/CLIV

words.ex: The climax of the movie was a big chase scene.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的高潮是一场大追捕场景。
words.en: The climax is the most exciting or important part of a play, film, or piece of music, which usually happens near the end.

words.ex: He has an inclination to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他有帮助他人的倾向。
words.en: An inclination is a feeling that makes you want to act in a particular way, or a tendency to do something.

words.ex: He has a disinclination to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意在公众场合讲话。
words.en: A disinclination to do something is a feeling of not wanting to do it.

words.ex: The synclinal fold in the rock layers was clearly visible.
words.ex_cn: 岩石层中的向斜褶皱清晰可见。
words.en: A synclinal is a geological structure consisting of a fold in the Earth's crust that is concave upwards, with the youngest rock layers in the center.

words.ex: He has a proclivity for solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有解决数学问题的倾向。
words.en: A proclivity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way or to like a particular thing.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CO-/COL-/COM-/CON-/COR-

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.ex: They communicate well with each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此沟通得很好。
words.en: To communicate means to share or exchange information, news, or ideas, especially by speaking or writing.

words.ex: He showed conformity with the group's rules.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守了小组的规定。
words.en: Conformity is the act of matching attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors to group norms or standards.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes COD

words.tr: n. 代码；编码；行为准则；密码；法典；
words.ex: He wrote a simple code to solve the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一段简单的代码来解决这个数学问题。
words.en: A code is a system of words, letters, figures, or other symbols substituted for other words, letters, etc., especially for the purposes of secrecy. As a verb, it means to convert (a message or other information) into a code.

words.ex: He can decode the secret message.
words.ex_cn: 他能译解这个秘密信息。
words.en: To convert coded data into intelligible form.

words.ex: The government decided to codify the old laws.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定将旧法律编纂成典。
words.en: To codify means to arrange laws, rules, etc. into a systematic code.

words.ex: The codex contains ancient texts that have been preserved for centuries.
words.ex_cn: 这部古抄本包含着几个世纪以来保存下来的古代文献。
words.en: A codex is an ancient manuscript text in book form. The term is now usually only used to describe manuscript books, with handwritten contents, from late antiquity and the Middle Ages.

words.ex: He added a codicil to his will, specifying additional bequests.
words.ex_cn: 他在遗嘱中添加了一个附录，指定了额外的遗产分配。
words.en: A codicil is an addition or supplement that explains, modifies, or revokes a will or part of one.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes COGNI/GNO

words.ex: Children develop cognition as they learn to understand the world.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在学习理解世界时发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognition is the mental action or process of acquiring knowledge and understanding through thought, experience, and the senses.

words.tr:
adj. 隐姓埋名的；化名的
adv. 隐姓埋名地；匿名地
words.ex: He traveled incognito to avoid being recognized.
words.ex_cn: 他隐瞒身份旅行以避免被认出。
words.en: If someone does something incognito, they do it without letting people know who they are.

words.ex: The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查了症状后做出了诊断。
words.en: The identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

words.ex: He tries to prognosticate the weather tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他试图预测明天的天气。
words.en: To prognosticate means to foretell or predict something based on present signs or symptoms.

words.tr: n. [内科] 认识不能，部分或全部丧失感官之辨别力
words.ex: Agnosia can manifest as an inability to recognize familiar faces.
words.ex_cn: 认识不能可能表现为无法识别熟悉的面孔。
words.en: Agnosia is a neurological disorder characterized by an inability to process sensory information, leading to difficulties in recognizing objects, persons, sounds, shapes, or smells while the specific sense is not defective nor is there any significant memory loss.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CONTRA-/CONTRO-

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.tr:
n. 相反；
adj. 相反的；
words.ex: The contrary of hot is cold.
words.ex_cn: 热的相反是冷。
words.en: If you say that something is true contrary to other people's beliefs or opinions, you are emphasizing that it is true and that they are wrong.

words.ex: He contravenes the school rules by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: To contravene a law or rule means to do something that is forbidden by it.

words.tr: v. 禁忌；表明...的不可取性
words.ex: The doctor said that surgery was contraindicated for her condition.
words.ex_cn: 医生说她的情况禁忌手术。
words.en: To indicate the inadvisability of (a particular treatment or procedure) in a specific case, usually because of a risk of harm or adverse effects.

words.ex: There was a controversy about the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 关于新校规，人们展开了争论。
words.en: A controversy is a disagreement or argument about something that involves many people and generates strong feelings.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CORP

words.ex: The police found a corpse near the river.
words.ex_cn: 警察在河边发现了一具尸体。
words.en: A corpse is a dead body, especially the dead body of a human.

words.ex: The corpulent man walks slowly.
words.ex_cn: 这位肥胖的男人走得很慢。
words.en: If you describe someone as corpulent, you mean they are fat.

words.tr: adj. 物质的；有形的；实体的；身体的
words.ex: He believes that the soul is not corporeal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信灵魂不是物质的。
words.en: Relating to a person's body, especially as opposed to their spirit.

words.ex: The linguist analyzed the English corpus to find common phrases.
words.ex_cn: 语言学家分析了英语语料库以寻找常用短语。
words.en: A corpus is a large collection of written or spoken texts that is used for language research.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes COSM

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.tr: n. 微观世界；小宇宙；缩影
words.ex: The classroom is a microcosm of society.
words.ex_cn: 教室是社会的一个缩影。
words.en: A microcosm is a small, representative system having analogies to a larger system in constitution, configuration, or development.

words.ex: He loves studying cosmology to understand the universe.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢学习宇宙学来理解宇宙。
words.en: Cosmology is the study of the origin, structure, and evolution of the universe.

words.ex: He loves to watch the cosmos at night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在夜晚观看宇宙。
words.en: The cosmos refers to the universe seen as a well-ordered whole, or to any system or structure that is complex and orderly.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CRACY/CRAT

words.tr: n. 贵族政治；贵族统治；贵族
words.ex: The aristocracy lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族住在巨大的城堡里。
words.en: The highest class in certain societies, especially those holding hereditary titles or offices.

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚机构
words.ex: He hates the bureaucracy in government offices.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌政府办公室里的官僚主义。
words.en: Bureaucracy refers to a system of government or business that has many complicated rules and ways of doing things.

words.tr: n. 富豪；财阀；财阀政治；富豪统治
words.ex: The country is often criticized for being a plutocracy where wealth determines political power.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经常因为财富决定政治权力的富豪统治而受到批评。
words.en: A plutocracy is a society or system that is ruled or controlled by people of great wealth or income.

words.ex: The theocracy ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 神权政体以铁腕统治。
words.en: A theocracy is a form of government in which a deity is recognized as the supreme civil ruler, the deity's laws being interpreted by ecclesiastical authorities.

words.ex: The technocrat proposed a new system for managing the city's infrastructure.
words.ex_cn: 这位技术统治论者提出了一套新的城市基础设施管理体系。
words.en: A technocrat is someone who has a lot of knowledge about technology and uses it to manage or control a government, industry, or organization.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CREA

words.ex: He creates beautiful paintings with colors.
words.ex_cn: 他用色彩创造美丽的画作。
words.en: To create means to bring something into existence or to cause something to happen as a result of one's actions.

words.ex: The creature lived in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这个生物生活在森林里。
words.en: A creature is a living thing, especially an animal.

words.ex: The movie recreates the battle of Waterloo.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影再现了滑铁卢战役。
words.en: To recreate something means to make it exist or happen again, or to make a copy of something that existed in the past.

words.ex: Animals engage in procreation to continue their species.
words.ex_cn: 动物通过生殖来延续它们的物种。
words.en: Procreation is the act of producing young or offspring.

words.tr: vt.误造，误创，误作; 错造（弄成奇性怪状）
words.ex: The artist's attempt to miscreate a masterpiece resulted in a grotesque sculpture.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家试图误创一件杰作，结果创作出了一件奇形怪状的雕塑。
words.en: To create something in a wrong or distorted manner, often resulting in a flawed or malformed outcome.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CRED

words.ex: His credo is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A credo is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way a person lives or works.

words.ex: He showed his credentials to get the job.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了资历来获得这份工作。
words.en: Credentials are documents that prove your identity or qualifications.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.ex: The witness gave credence to the story by crying.
words.ex_cn: 证人通过哭泣使这个故事显得可信。
words.en: Credence is a belief in or acceptance of something as true.

words.ex: He looked incredulous when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他一脸难以置信。
words.en: If someone is incredulous, they are unable to believe something because it is very surprising or shocking.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CRE/CRESC/CRET/CRU

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.ex: The moon looks like a crescent tonight.
words.ex_cn: 今晚的月亮像一弯新月。
words.en: A crescent is a curved shape that is wider in the middle and pointed at the ends, like the shape of the moon in its first or last quarter.

words.tr: n. 声音渐增；高潮；顶峰
words.ex: The music reached a loud crescendo at the end.
words.ex_cn: 音乐在结尾处达到响亮的高潮。
words.en: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness or intensity in music, or any situation where there is a gradual increase in intensity.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.ex: The moon is increscent tonight.
words.ex_cn: 今晚月亮正在变圆。
words.en: Becoming gradually larger or more intense.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CRIT

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.ex: He is hypocritical when he says he hates lying but lies all the time.
words.ex_cn: 他说他讨厌撒谎，却总是撒谎，这很虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being hypocritical, you mean that they pretend to have qualities, beliefs, or feelings that they do not really have.

words.ex: He received criticism for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而受到批评。
words.en: Criticism is the act of expressing disapproval of someone or something and of the faults they have or the mistakes they have made.

words.ex: The teacher will critique the student's essay tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会对学生的作文发表评论。
words.en: A critique is a detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes COUR/CUR

words.tr: n. 同时发生；赞同；合作
words.ex: There is concurrence between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告是一致的。
words.en: The fact of two or more events or circumstances happening or existing at the same time.

words.ex: The courier delivered the letter quickly.
words.ex_cn: 信使迅速送来了这封信。
words.en: A courier is a person or company that delivers messages, packages, and mail.

words.ex: The school changed its curriculum last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年学校更改了课程。
words.en: A curriculum is the subjects that are studied in a school, college, or university.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.tr:
adj. 当前的；流通的；
n. （水、气、电）流；趋势；
words.ex: The current weather is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 当前的天气非常热。
words.en: belonging to the present time; happening or being used or done now

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CUR/CURA

words.ex: The curator arranged the paintings in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 馆长在博物馆里布置了这些画作。
words.en: A curator is someone who is in charge of the objects or works of art in a museum or art gallery.

words.tr:
n. 治疗；疗法；
v. 治愈；治疗；
words.ex: The new medicine is a cure for the disease.
words.ex_cn: 这种新药是这种疾病的治疗方法。
words.en: If doctors or medical treatments cure an illness or injury, they cause it to end or disappear. If a person or animal is cured of an illness or injury, they become well again.

words.tr: n. 刮匙；刮器；耳挖; vt. 用刮匙刮
words.ex: The doctor used a curette to remove the tissue.
words.ex_cn: 医生用刮匙移除了组织。
words.en: A curette is a surgical instrument designed for scraping or debriding biological tissue or debris in a biopsy, excision, or cleaning procedure.

words.ex: The curative treatment helped him recover quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种医疗治疗帮助他迅速康复。
words.en: Curative means having the ability to cure or heal, especially of a disease or medical condition.

words.tr: n. （某教区的）助理牧师；堂区牧师; v. 操持（收藏品或展品的）展出；组织（音乐节的）演出
words.ex: He curates art exhibits at the museum.
words.ex_cn: 他在博物馆策展。
words.en: A curate is a priest who is a member of the clergy in the Anglican Church, especially one who is an assistant to a vicar or rector. As a verb, to curate means to select, organize, and look after the items in a collection or exhibition.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes CYCL/CYCLO

words.ex: The economy has a cyclical pattern of growth and decline.
words.ex_cn: 经济有增长和衰退的周期性模式。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in cycles; regularly repeated.

words.ex: The plant cell shows cyclosis under the microscope.
words.ex_cn: 在显微镜下，这个植物细胞显示出细胞质环流。
words.en: Cyclosis refers to the movement of the cytoplasm within a cell, facilitating the transport of nutrients, organelles, and other substances throughout the cell.

words.tr: n. 摆线，圆滚线; adj. 圆形的；情绪起伏不定的
words.ex: The point on the wheel traces a cycloid as it rolls.
words.ex_cn: 轮子上的点在滚动时描绘出一条摆线。
words.en: A cycloid is the curve traced by a point on the rim of a circular wheel as the wheel rolls along a straight line without slipping.

words.tr: n. 库克罗普斯（独眼巨人）
words.ex: The boy saw a cyclops in the storybook.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在故事书里看到了一个独眼巨人。
words.en: A cyclops is a member of a race of giants in Greek mythology, each having a single eye in the center of the forehead.

words.tr: n. 躁郁性气质；[内科] 循环性精神病；躁狂抑郁精神病
words.ex: He has cyclothymia and feels happy one day, sad the next.
words.ex_cn: 他患有环性心境障碍，今天开心，明天就难过。
words.en: Cyclothymia is a chronic mood disorder which consists of periods of hypomania and depression.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DE-

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.tr: v. 谴责；强烈反对；悲叹
words.ex: He deplores the violence on TV.
words.ex_cn: 他谴责电视上的暴力。
words.en: If you deplore something, you think it is very wrong or very bad.

words.ex: They deride him for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他们嘲笑他穿旧衣服。
words.en: If you deride someone or something, you say that they are stupid or have no value.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.tr: v. 对…表示极不赞成；强烈反对；轻视
words.ex: They deprecate old software.
words.ex_cn: 他们不推荐使用旧软件。
words.en: If you deprecate something, you criticize it or express your disapproval of it.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DEC-/DECA-

words.ex: The ten commandments are called the decalogue.
words.ex_cn: 十诫被称为十诫。
words.en: The Decalogue refers to the Ten Commandments, a set of biblical laws relating to ethics and worship, which are fundamental to both Judaism and Christianity.

words.tr: v. 大批杀死；大量毁灭
words.ex: The storm decimated the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个村庄。
words.en: To decimate something such as a group of people or animals means to destroy a very large number of them.

words.ex: He lived in Paris for a decade.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎生活了十年。
words.en: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example 1980 to 1989.

words.ex: The model shows a decahedron with ten faces.
words.ex_cn: 这个模型展示了一个有十个面的十面体。
words.en: A decahedron is a polyhedron with ten faces.

words.tr: n. 十足类动物（蟹、虾等）；十腕类动物（乌贼等）; adj. 有十脚的；有十臂的
words.ex: The crab is a decapod with ten legs.
words.ex_cn: 螃蟹是一种有十条腿的十足目动物。
words.en: A decapod is any crustacean of the order Decapoda, having five pairs of walking legs, including crabs, lobsters, and shrimp.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DEI/DIV

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.ex: The statue represents the divinity of the ancient gods.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像代表了古代众神的神性。
words.en: Divinity refers to the state or quality of being divine, or a divine being. It can also refer to the study of religion or theology.

words.tr: v. 神化；把…奉若神明；崇拜
words.ex: They deify their ancient heroes.
words.ex_cn: 他们崇拜自己的古代英雄。
words.en: To treat someone or something as a god or goddess, or to consider them as if they were divine.

words.ex: He believes in deism, not in organized religion.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自然神论，而不是有组织的宗教。
words.en: Deism is the belief in the existence of a supreme being, specifically of a creator who does not intervene in the universe.

words.tr: adj. 予以神化的；神圣的；奉为神的
words.ex: The ancient people believed the king was deific.
words.ex_cn: 古代人相信这位国王是神一般的。
words.en: If you describe something as deific, you mean it is divine or godlike in nature.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DEMI-

words.tr: n. 受崇拜的人，英雄人物；半神半人；小神
words.ex: He believes he is a demigod because of his strength.
words.ex_cn: 他因为自己的力量而相信自己是半神。
words.en: A demigod is a being with partial or lesser divine status, such as a minor deity, the offspring of a god and a mortal, or a mortal raised to divine rank.

words.tr: n. （法）暗娼阶层；品德有问题的女人；风月场（由暗娼组成的）
words.ex: He moved in the demimonde of artists and poets.
words.ex_cn: 他出入于艺术家和诗人的半上流社会。
words.en: The demimonde refers to a class of women considered to be of doubtful morality and social standing, often associated with the fringes of respectable society in the 19th century.

words.ex: The statue has a demirelief on its base.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像的底座上有一个半浮雕。
words.en: A sculptural relief where the figures project less than half their depth from the background.

words.tr: n. （法）娼妓；情妇；贞洁可疑的妇女
words.ex: He is a demirep who works at the factory.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名半工半读的工人，在工厂工作。
words.en: A woman whose social position is considered to be between that of a respectable woman and a prostitute.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DEM

words.ex: The statue has a demirelief on its base.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像的底座上有一个半浮雕。
words.en: A sculptural relief where the figures project less than half their depth from the background.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DERM

words.ex: The statue has a demirelief on its base.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像的底座上有一个半浮雕。
words.en: A sculptural relief where the figures project less than half their depth from the background.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DI-

words.ex: The system goes through diphase changes during heating.
words.ex_cn: 系统在加热过程中经历两相变化。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of two phases.

words.ex: The statue has a demirelief on its base.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像的底座上有一个半浮雕。
words.en: A sculptural relief where the figures project less than half their depth from the background.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DIA-

words.ex: The statue has a demirelief on its base.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像的底座上有一个半浮雕。
words.en: A sculptural relief where the figures project less than half their depth from the background.

words.tr: adj. 探求现象变化的；历经时间长河的
words.ex: The diachronic study shows how words change over time.
words.ex_cn: 历时研究展示了词语如何随时间变化。
words.en: Diachronic refers to phenomena as they occur over time, especially in the context of historical development and change.

words.ex: He gave a loud diatribe against the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他对新法律发表了一通激烈的抨击。
words.en: A diatribe is an angry speech or piece of writing that strongly criticizes something or someone.

words.ex: The dialogue in the movie was very funny.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影中的对白非常幽默。
words.en: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people in a book, play, or film.

words.ex: The diaphanous curtain let in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 那层薄纱窗帘让晨光透了进来。
words.en: A diaphanous substance or fabric is very thin and almost transparent.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DIC/DICT

words.ex: The king issued an edict to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An edict is an official order or proclamation issued by a person in authority.

words.ex: The priest gave a benediction at the end of the service.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在仪式结束时给予了祝福。
words.en: A benediction is a prayer asking for God's blessing, especially one at the end of a religious service.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: He shouted a malediction at the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他对着小偷咒骂了一句。
words.en: A malediction is a curse or the act of uttering a curse.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DIF-/DIS-

words.ex: He shouted a malediction at the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他对着小偷咒骂了一句。
words.en: A malediction is a curse or the act of uttering a curse.

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.ex: He tried to dissuade her from quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 他试图劝她不要辞掉工作。
words.en: If you dissuade someone from doing something, you persuade them not to do it.

words.tr: adj. 不动感情的；冷静的；平心静气的
words.ex: She remained dispassionate throughout the heated debate.
words.ex_cn: 她在激烈的辩论中始终保持冷静。
words.en: If you are dispassionate, you are able to act calmly and reasonably and not be influenced by your feelings or by personal opinions.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DOC/DOCT

words.tr:
adj. 教条（主义）的；空谈理论的
n. 教条主义者；空论家
words.ex: He is a doctrinaire who always follows rules strictly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个教条主义者，总是严格遵守规则。
words.en: If you say that someone is doctrinaire, you are criticizing them for following fixed theories or principles rather than considering practical problems.

words.tr: n. 讲师；讲解员; n. （Docent）人名；（芬）多森特
words.ex: The docent explains the paintings to visitors.
words.ex_cn: 讲解员向游客解释这些画作。
words.en: A docent is a person who acts as a guide, typically on a voluntary basis, in a museum, art gallery, or zoo.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

words.ex: They tried to indoctrinate the children with their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图用他们的信仰灌输孩子们。
words.en: To indoctrinate someone means to teach them a particular belief or set of beliefs, especially with the aim of making them accept it without questioning it.

words.ex: The docile dog followed its owner quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这只温顺的狗安静地跟着主人。
words.en: A docile person or animal is quiet, not aggressive, and easily controlled.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DON

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: The hospital received a donation of books.
words.ex_cn: 医院收到了一批书籍捐赠。
words.en: A donation is a gift which is given to a charity or other organization.

words.ex: The donor gave money to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 捐赠者向医院捐了钱。
words.en: A donor is a person or organization that gives something, especially money, to a charity or other organization.

words.tr: n. 受赠者，[经] 受赠人
words.ex: The donee received a gift from her uncle.
words.ex_cn: 受赠人收到了她叔叔的礼物。
words.en: A donee is a person who receives a gift or donation.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DOG/DOX

words.tr: n. 受赠者，[经] 受赠人
words.ex: The donee received a gift from her uncle.
words.ex_cn: 受赠人收到了她叔叔的礼物。
words.en: A donee is a person who receives a gift or donation.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DOM/DOMIN

words.tr: n. 受赠者，[经] 受赠人
words.ex: The donee received a gift from her uncle.
words.ex_cn: 受赠人收到了她叔叔的礼物。
words.en: A donee is a person who receives a gift or donation.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DORM

words.tr: n. 受赠者，[经] 受赠人
words.ex: The donee received a gift from her uncle.
words.ex_cn: 受赠人收到了她叔叔的礼物。
words.en: A donee is a person who receives a gift or donation.

words.ex: The old machine is dormient now.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: In a state of rest or inactivity; latent.

words.tr: adj. 安眠的；催眠的; n. 安眠药；麻醉剂
words.ex: The dormitive power of the drug made him fall asleep.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的催眠作用让他睡着了。
words.en: A dormitive is a substance or drug that induces sleep.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DROM/DROME

words.tr: n. 受赠者，[经] 受赠人
words.ex: The donee received a gift from her uncle.
words.ex_cn: 受赠人收到了她叔叔的礼物。
words.en: A donee is a person who receives a gift or donation.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DU-

words.tr: n. 受赠者，[经] 受赠人
words.ex: The donee received a gift from her uncle.
words.ex_cn: 受赠人收到了她叔叔的礼物。
words.en: A donee is a person who receives a gift or donation.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DUC/DUCT

words.tr: n. 受赠者，[经] 受赠人
words.ex: The donee received a gift from her uncle.
words.ex_cn: 受赠人收到了她叔叔的礼物。
words.en: A donee is a person who receives a gift or donation.

words.ex: He tried to seduce her with flowers and gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和礼物引诱她。
words.en: To seduce someone means to persuade them to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by making it seem attractive or exciting.

words.ex: The aliens abduct the man at night.
words.ex_cn: 外星人在晚上绑架了那个男人。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force or deception; kidnap.

words.ex: The train goes over a long viaduct.
words.ex_cn: 火车驶过一座长长的高架桥。
words.en: A viaduct is a long, high bridge that carries a road or a railway across a valley or a low area.

words.tr: adj. 可延展的；易于塑造的
words.ex: The gold is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 金具有延展性，可以拉成细丝。
words.en: A ductile material is one that can be stretched into a wire or hammered into a thin sheet without breaking.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DUR

words.ex: This bag is durable and lasts for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个包很耐用，可以用很多年。
words.en: Something that is durable is strong and lasts a long time without breaking or becoming weaker.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: He signed the paper under duress.
words.ex_cn: 他在胁迫下签了那张纸。
words.en: Duress is a situation in which someone is forced to do something against their will, typically by the use of threats or force.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DYN/DYNAM

words.ex: The workers used dynamite to break the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 工人们使用炸药来炸开岩石。
words.en: Dynamite is a type of explosive that is used in mining and construction. It is also used metaphorically to describe something that is highly effective or potentially dangerous.

words.ex: The old factory uses a dynamo to produce electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这家老工厂使用一台发电机来发电。
words.en: A dynamo is a device for converting mechanical energy into electrical energy, typically by rotating coils of copper wire in a magnetic field.

words.ex: The Tang dynasty was famous for its poetry and art.
words.ex_cn: 唐朝以诗歌和艺术而闻名。
words.en: A dynasty is a series of rulers of a country who all belong to the same family.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.tr: v. 使（交变无线电信号）混合以产生外差效果; adj. （无线电传播中）外差的，外差法的
words.ex: The radio uses a heterodyne circuit to pick up signals.
words.ex_cn: 这台收音机使用差频电路来接收信号。
words.en: Pertaining to the production of a new frequency by the combination of two different frequencies, especially in radio technology.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes DYS-

words.tr: adj. 功能失调的；出现障碍的；
words.ex: The dysfunctional family rarely ate meals together.
words.ex_cn: 这个功能失调的家庭很少一起吃饭。
words.en: Not operating normally or properly.

words.ex: He has dyslexia, so he reads slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他有阅读障碍，所以读得慢。
words.en: Dyslexia is a learning difficulty that primarily affects the skills involved in accurate and fluent word reading and spelling.

words.tr: n. 糟透的社会；地狱般的处境；非理想化的地方
words.ex: The book shows a dark dystopia where people have no freedom.
words.ex_cn: 这本书描绘了一个人们没有自由的黑暗反乌托邦。
words.en: A dystopia is an imagined state or society in which there is great suffering or injustice, typically one that is totalitarian or post-apocalyptic.

words.ex: He got dysentery from drinking dirty water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了脏水后得了痢疾。
words.en: Dysentery is an infection of the intestines that causes severe diarrhea with blood.

words.ex: He has dyspepsia after eating spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃辣食后消化不良。
words.en: A medical condition characterized by chronic or recurrent discomfort in the upper abdomen, often associated with eating.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes E-/EX-

words.ex: The lamp emits a soft light.
words.ex_cn: 灯发出柔和的光。
words.en: To emit means to send out something such as light, heat, sound, gas, etc.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.ex: He helped extricate the car from the mud.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助把车从泥里解脱出来。
words.en: If you extricate someone or something from a place where they are trapped or caught, you succeed in freeing them.

words.ex: He exhale slowly after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后慢慢呼出气。
words.en: To exhale means to breathe out air from your lungs.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ECTO-

words.tr: adj. [动] 外生的；体外生活的
words.ex: The infection is ectogenous.
words.ex_cn: 这种感染是外源性的。
words.en: Originating or produced outside the organism.

words.tr: n. [细胞] 外质，[细胞] 外胚层质
words.ex: The ghost story mentioned ectoplasm coming out of the medium.
words.ex_cn: 这个鬼故事提到灵媒身上出现了灵质。
words.en: Ectoplasm refers to a supernatural viscous substance that is supposed to exude from the body of a medium during a spiritualistic trance and to form the material for the manifestation of spirits.

words.ex: The ectoderm forms the skin in embryos.
words.ex_cn: 外胚层在胚胎中形成皮肤。
words.en: The outermost of the three primary germ layers of an embryo, from which the epidermis, nervous tissue, and, in vertebrates, sense organs develop.

words.tr: n. [医] 异位（器官等的位置异常，通常是先天性的）
words.ex: The baby has ectopia in the heart.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿的心脏有异位。
words.en: The abnormal position of an organ or other part of the body.

words.tr: phrase. 异位妊娠；宫外孕（受精卵在子宫外着床发育）
words.ex: She was diagnosed with an ectopic pregnancy.
words.ex_cn: 她被诊断出宫外孕。
words.en: An ectopic pregnancy is a complication of pregnancy in which the embryo attaches outside the uterus.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes EGO

words.tr: adj. 自我中心的；利己的；
words.ex: He is egocentric and only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他以自我为中心，只谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egocentric, you mean that they are only concerned with their own needs and desires, and not with those of other people.

words.tr: n. 自大狂；极端利己；利己癖；自尊癖
words.ex: He has egomania and talks only about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他有自我中心狂，只谈论自己。
words.en: An obsessive preoccupation with oneself.

words.tr: adj. 自我本位的；任性的；自负的
words.ex: He is egotistical and always talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他很自我中心，总是谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egotistical, you disapprove of them because they behave as if they are more important or better than other people.

words.tr: n. 自我主义者；利己主义者
words.ex: He is an egoist who only thinks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他是个只为自己着想的利己主义者。
words.en: An egoist is someone who is excessively self-centered and selfish, often disregarding the needs and feelings of others.

words.ex: He listens to his super-ego when he makes moral choices.
words.ex_cn: 当他做出道德选择时，他会听从超我的声音。
words.en: In psychoanalysis, the super-ego is the part of a person's mind that acts as a self-critical conscience, reflecting social standards learned from parents and teachers.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ENDO-

words.tr: n. 内容矿物；胖型体质
words.ex: He is an endomorph who gains weight easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是个容易发胖的内胚型体型的人。
words.en: An endomorph is a person with a body type characterized by a tendency to store fat, a round physique, and a slow metabolism.

words.ex: The hormone is endogenous to the human body.
words.ex_cn: 这种激素是人体内源性的。
words.en: Originating or produced within an organism, tissue, or cell.

words.ex: The doctor uses an endoscope to see inside the body.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用内窥镜来观察身体内部。
words.en: An endoscope is a medical device consisting of a long, thin tube that has a light and a camera at one end, which is used to look inside a person's body in a non-invasive way.

words.tr: adj.[生态] 组织内寄生的，[生态] 生物内生的
words.ex: The endobiotic bacteria live inside the human body.
words.ex_cn: 内生菌生活在人体内部。
words.en: Living or occurring within a host organism.

words.tr: adj. 心内膜的；心脏内的
words.ex: The endocardial tissue helps the heart beat properly.
words.ex_cn: 心内膜组织帮助心脏正常跳动。
words.en: Relating to the endocardium, the innermost layer of tissue that lines the chambers of the heart.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes EPI-

words.ex: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin.
words.ex_cn: 表皮是皮肤的最外层。
words.en: The epidermis is the outer layer of the skin of an animal, which serves as a protective barrier against the environment.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: He feels pain in the epigastric area after eating.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完饭后感到上腹部疼痛。
words.en: Relating to the upper central region of the abdomen.

words.ex: The epitaph on his grave says, 'Beloved father and friend.'
words.ex_cn: 他墓碑上的墓志铭写着：‘受人爱戴的父亲和朋友。’
words.en: An epitaph is a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone.

words.ex: The earthquake started at the epicenter near the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震从城市附近的震中开始。
words.en: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes EQU

words.ex: The equator divides the Earth into two halves.
words.ex_cn: 赤道将地球分为两半。
words.en: The equator is an imaginary line around the Earth, equally distant from the North Pole and the South Pole, dividing the Earth into the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.

words.ex: The equation is easy to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这个方程式很容易解。
words.en: An equation is a mathematical statement that asserts the equality of two expressions.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.ex: He kept his equanimity during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他在风暴中保持了冷静。
words.en: If you face a difficult situation with equanimity, you remain calm and do not get upset or angry.

words.ex: The inequity in pay between men and women is wrong.
words.ex_cn: 男女薪酬之间的不公是错误的。
words.en: Inequity refers to a lack of fairness or justice in a situation or system.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ERG

words.tr: n. 寡头政治；寡头统治集团；寡头统治的国家
words.ex: The country is ruled by an oligarchy of wealthy businessmen.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家由一群富有的商人寡头统治。
words.en: A form of government in which all power is vested in a few persons or in a dominant class or clique; government by the few.

words.tr: n. 工效学；人类工程学
words.ex: The chair is designed for good ergonomics.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子的设计符合人体工学。
words.en: Ergonomics is the study of people's efficiency in their working environment, especially the science of designing equipment and systems that fit the human body, its movements, and its cognitive abilities.

words.tr: n. [物] 尔格（功和能的单位）
words.ex: He feels erg after working all day.
words.ex_cn: 他工作了一整天后感到疲惫。
words.en: An erg is a unit of work or energy in the centimeter-gram-second system of units, equal to the work done by a force of one dyne acting over a distance of one centimeter.

words.tr: n. 测功计；[医] 肌力描记器；疲劳记录计
words.ex: The doctor used an ergograph to measure his hand strength.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用测力计来测量他的手部力量。
words.en: An ergograph is an instrument for measuring and recording the work performed by a muscle or group of muscles.

words.ex: The synergic team worked well together.
words.ex_cn: 这个协作的团队合作得很好。
words.en: Involving interaction or cooperation between two or more organizations, substances, or other agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their separate effects.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ERR

words.tr: adj. 游历的；游离不定的；行为不当的；出轨的
words.ex: The errant knight traveled far across the land.
words.ex_cn: 这位游历的骑士穿越了广袤的土地。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as errant, you mean that they have strayed from the proper course or standards.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.ex: His answer was erroneous because he added wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案是错误的，因为他加错了。
words.en: If you describe someone's beliefs or opinions as erroneous, you mean that they are incorrect and based on false information.

words.ex: He made an error in his math homework.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学作业中犯了一个错误。
words.en: An error is a mistake.

words.tr: n. （印刷或书写中的）错误；排错；勘误表
words.ex: The book has an erratum on page 5.
words.ex_cn: 这本书第5页有一个更正。
words.en: An erratum is a mistake in a printed or written document that has been corrected in a subsequent edition or version.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ETH/ETHOS

words.ex: The school's ethos is respect for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的社會精神特质是尊重每一个人。
words.en: The fundamental character or spirit of a culture; the underlying sentiment that informs the beliefs, customs, or practices of a group or society.

words.ex: He is studying bioethics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习生物伦理学。
words.en: Bioethics is the study of the ethical issues emerging from advances in biology and medicine.

words.tr: n. 道德规范；伦理标准；
words.ex: The company follows a strong ethic of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司遵循诚实的道德规范。
words.en: An ethic is a moral principle or set of moral principles that guides the behavior of a person or group, especially in a professional context.

words.ex: Doctors must follow medical ethics.
words.ex_cn: 医生必须遵守医学道德规范。
words.en: Ethics are moral beliefs and rules about right and wrong.

words.ex: He studies ethology to understand animal behavior.
words.ex_cn: 他研究动物行为学以了解动物行为。
words.en: Ethology is the scientific and objective study of animal behaviour, usually with a focus on behaviour under natural conditions, and viewing behaviour as an evolutionarily adaptive trait.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes EU-

words.ex: He gave a eulogy for his grandmother.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的祖母致了悼词。
words.en: A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly, typically someone who has just died.

words.ex: He used a euphemism to say he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个委婉语来表示他失业了。
words.en: A euphemism is a polite word or expression that is used to refer to things which people may find upsetting or embarrassing to talk about.

words.ex: He studied eugenics in the 1920s.
words.ex_cn: 他在20世纪20年代研究优生学。
words.en: The study of how to arrange reproduction within a human population to increase the occurrence of heritable characteristics regarded as desirable.

words.tr: n. 精神欢快；兴高采烈
words.ex: He felt euphoria after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到无比兴奋。
words.en: A feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.

words.ex: The poem has great euphony.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗具有优美的音韵。
words.en: The quality of being pleasing to the ear, especially through a harmonious combination of words.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes EXTRA-/EXTRO-

words.ex: She has an extraordinary talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 她具有非凡的音乐天赋。
words.en: Something that is extraordinary is very unusual or remarkable.

words.ex: He joins extracurricular activities after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后参加课外活动。
words.en: Extracurricular activities are those that fall outside the realm of the normal curriculum of school or university education, performed by students. Extracurricular activities exist at all levels of education, from 4th-6th, junior high/high school, college and university education.

words.tr: adj. 地球外的；地外的；外星球的；
words.ex: The movie shows an extraterrestrial life form.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一种地球外的生命形式。
words.en: An extraterrestrial is a creature that comes from or exists outside the planet Earth.

words.ex: The extraneous noise made it hard to concentrate.
words.ex_cn: 那些无关的噪音让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: Something that is extraneous is not relevant or essential to the subject you are dealing with.

words.ex: He shows extroversion at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上表现出外向。
words.en: Extroversion is the quality of being outgoing and socially confident.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes FAC/FIC/FEC

words.ex: The beneficent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: A beneficent person or organization helps people or results in something good.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.tr: n. 甜食；糖果；调制；精美作品
words.ex: He bought a confection at the candy store.
words.ex_cn: 他在糖果店买了一颗糖果。
words.en: A confection is a sweet food or a delicacy made with sugar or other sweeteners.

words.tr:
adj. 催眠的；让人瞌睡的
n. 安眠药
