words.en: A theocracy is a form of government in which a deity is recognized as the supreme civil ruler, the deity's laws being interpreted by ecclesiastical authorities.

words.tr: n. 神学；宗教学；宗教信仰学
words.ex: He is studying theology at the university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习神学。
words.en: Theology is the study of the nature of God and religious belief.

words.tr: n. 鼎盛时期；（人生或事业的)巅峰；册封为神
words.ex: The artist's work reached apotheosis in his final masterpiece.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家的作品在他的最终杰作中达到了神化。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; culmination or climax.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes THERAP

words.ex: He is receiving therapy for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受治疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Therapy is the treatment of someone with mental or physical illness without the use of drugs or operations.

words.ex: The therapeutic massage helped her relax.
words.ex_cn: 这种治疗性的按摩帮助她放松了。
words.en: If something is therapeutic, it helps you to relax or to feel better about things, especially if you have been feeling worried or upset.

words.ex: The therapist helped him feel better after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 治疗专家在事故后帮助他感觉好些了。
words.en: A therapist is a person who is skilled in a particular type of therapy and treats people using it.

words.tr: n. 生物疗法；[临床] 生物制剂疗法
words.ex: Biotherapy is increasingly being used to treat various types of cancer.
words.ex_cn: 生物疗法越来越多地被用于治疗各种类型的癌症。
words.en: Biotherapy refers to the treatment of disease using living organisms or their products.

words.ex: He goes to physiotherapy after his surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后去做物理治疗。
words.en: Physiotherapy is the treatment of disease, injury, or deformity by physical methods such as massage, heat treatment, and exercise rather than by drugs or surgery.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes THERM/THERMO

words.ex: He is learning thermochemistry in chemistry class.
words.ex_cn: 他正在化学课上学习热化学。
words.en: Thermochemistry is the branch of chemistry concerned with the quantities of heat evolved or absorbed during chemical reactions.

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.ex: The thermoduric bacteria can survive in high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 耐热细菌能在高温下存活。
words.en: Thermoduric refers to organisms, especially bacteria, that are able to survive high temperatures, typically those used in pasteurization.

words.ex: The engine works on thermodynamic principles.
words.ex_cn: 这个发动机基于热力学原理工作。
words.en: Thermodynamic refers to the branch of physical science that deals with the relations between heat and other forms of energy (such as mechanical, electrical, or chemical energy), and, by extension, of the relationships between all forms of energy.

words.tr: adj. 受热即分解的；[生化][免疫] 不耐热的；感热的；热不稳定的
words.ex: Some enzymes are thermolabile and lose their activity when heated.
words.ex_cn: 一些酶是不耐热的，加热后会失去活性。
words.en: A substance that is thermolabile is easily destroyed or altered by heat.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes TOM/TOME/TOMY

words.tr: n. 大部头的书；大册书
words.ex: He read a large tome about ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于古代历史的厚书。
words.en: A tome is a large, heavy book, especially one dealing with a serious topic.

words.ex: The doctor mapped the dermatome on his arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生绘制了他手臂上的皮节图。
words.en: A dermatome is an area of skin that is mainly supplied by a single spinal nerve. It is also a surgical instrument used to produce thin slices of skin from a donor area, for use in skin grafts.

words.tr: n. 显微镜用薄片切片机
words.ex: The lab technician uses a microtome to cut thin slices of tissue.
words.ex_cn: 实验室技术员使用切片机切割薄薄的组织切片。
words.en: A microtome is an instrument used to cut extremely thin slices of material, known as sections, for examination under a microscope.

words.ex: The doctor performed a gastrotomy to remove the object.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了胃切开术以取出异物。
words.en: A surgical operation in which an incision is made into the stomach.

words.tr: n. [泌尿] 输精管切除术
words.ex: He had a vasectomy last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年做了输精管切除术。
words.en: A vasectomy is a surgical procedure for male sterilization or permanent contraception.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes TOP/TOPO

words.ex: The map shows the topography of the mountain area.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山区的地形。
words.en: The topography of an area is the physical features of its surface, such as hills, valleys, and rivers, especially the representation of these features on maps.

words.ex: He is learning topology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习拓扑学。
words.en: Topology is the branch of mathematics concerned with the properties of space that are preserved under continuous transformations, such as stretching and bending, but not tearing or gluing.

words.tr: n. 地名，以地名命名者；部位名称
words.ex: The toponym 'London' comes from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 地名‘伦敦’源自古代。
words.en: A toponym is the name of a place, especially a geographical locality or a feature of the landscape.

words.ex: He has topophobia and avoids high places.
words.ex_cn: 他有恐高症，避免去高处。
words.en: Topophobia is a fear of certain places or a fear of going to certain places.

words.tr: n. （修辞学上的）惯用语句；（文学创作的）传统的主题
words.ex: He uses a topos in his math paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学论文中使用了一个拓扑斯。
words.en: A traditional theme or motif, especially in literature or art.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes TORS/TORT/TORQU

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.ex: The wire shows torsion when twisted.
words.ex_cn: 当电线被扭转时，会出现扭转。
words.en: Torsion is the action of twisting or the state of being twisted, especially of one end of an object relative to the other.

words.ex: He contorts his face to make the kids laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他扭曲面部表情来逗孩子们笑。
words.en: If someone's face or body contorts or is contorted, it moves into an unnatural and unattractive shape or position.

words.ex: The engine produces a lot of torque.
words.ex_cn: 发动机产生很大的扭矩。
words.en: Torque is a twisting force that causes rotation.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes TRACT

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.ex: The farmer drives a tractor in the field.
words.ex_cn: 农夫在田里开拖拉机。
words.en: A tractor is a powerful motor vehicle with large rear wheels, used chiefly on farms for hauling equipment and trailers.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.ex: He tries to protract the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他试图延长会议。
words.en: To protract something means to make it last longer than usual or necessary, often in a way that is annoying or inconvenient.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes TRAN-/TRANS-

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.ex: The wizard can transmute lead into gold.
words.ex_cn: 巫师可以把铅变成金子。
words.en: To change something completely, especially into something different and better.

words.ex: He committed a transgression by stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了过错。
words.en: A transgression is an act that goes against a law, rule, or code of conduct; an offense.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.tr: v. 使变形；使完全改变性质
words.ex: The witch can transmogrify a frog into a prince.
words.ex_cn: 女巫可以把青蛙变成王子。
words.en: To change or alter greatly and often with grotesque or humorous effect.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes TREM/TREMU

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.tr: adj. 颤抖的；战栗的；畏缩的
words.ex: Her voice was tremulous when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时声音颤抖。
words.en: If someone's voice, smile, or actions are tremulous, they are unsteady because the person is uncertain, afraid, or upset.

words.tr:
v. 发抖；打颤；战栗；焦虑
n. 震颤；发抖；战栗
words.ex: The old man tremble in the cold wind.
words.ex_cn: 老人在寒风中发抖。
words.en: If you tremble, you shake slightly because you are frightened or cold.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a strong tremor in the building.
words.ex_cn: 地震使大楼发生了强烈的震动。
words.en: A tremor is a small earthquake or a shaking or vibrating movement, especially one caused by fear or nervousness.

words.ex: The violinist plays with a fast tremolo.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴手用快速的颤音演奏。
words.en: A tremolo is a musical effect consisting of a rapid repetition of the same note or a rapid alternation between two notes.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes TURB

words.tr: adj. 浑浊的；污浊不清的；
words.ex: The river water looks turbid after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后河水看起来浑浊。
words.en: If you describe something as turbid, you mean that it is cloudy, dirty, or muddy.

words.ex: The wind turbine spins to make electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风力涡轮机旋转以发电。
words.en: A turbine is a machine or engine which uses a stream of air, gas, water, or steam to turn a wheel and produce power.

words.ex: The plane uses a turbojet engine to fly fast.
words.ex_cn: 这架飞机使用涡轮喷气发动机高速飞行。
words.en: A turbojet is a type of jet engine that compresses air with a turbine and then mixes it with fuel and ignites it to produce thrust.

words.tr: adj. 狂暴的；骚动的；动荡的；汹涌的
words.ex: The turbulent sea made the boat shake.
words.ex_cn: 汹涌的海让船摇晃。
words.en: A turbulent situation, time, or relationship is one in which there is a lot of change, confusion, and often conflict.

words.ex: The noise from the construction caused a disturbance.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的噪音造成了干扰。
words.en: A disturbance is an event or situation in which people behave in a noisy or violent way, or something that interrupts what you are doing.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes TYP/TYPE

words.ex: The typal pattern of the house is very common in this town.
words.ex_cn: 这种房子的典型模式在这个镇上很常见。
words.en: Typal refers to something that is characteristic or representative of a particular type or category.

words.tr: adj. 典型的；有代表性的；
words.ex: This is a typical example of a sunny day.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个晴天的典型例子。
words.en: You use typical to describe someone or something that shows the most usual characteristics of a particular type of person or thing, and is therefore a good example of that type.

words.tr: v. 作为…的典型；代表；象征
words.ex: He typifies a true leader.
words.ex_cn: 他代表了一位真正的领导者。
words.en: If something or someone typifies a situation or type of behavior, they have all the usual characteristics of it and are a typical example of it.

words.ex: He wrote a paper on the typology of ancient tools.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于古代工具分类的论文。
words.en: The study or systematic classification of types that have characteristics or traits in common.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ULTRA-

words.ex: The doctor used ultrasonic waves to check the baby.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用超声波来检查婴儿。
words.en: Ultrasonic refers to sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper limit of human hearing.

words.ex: He lives in an ultramodern house with smart windows.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个带有智能窗户的超现代房子里。
words.en: Ultramodern refers to something that is extremely modern, often incorporating the latest technology or design.

words.tr: adj. 极端保守主义的; n. 极端保守主义者
words.ex: He is an ultraconservative who opposes all changes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个极端保守的人，反对所有改变。
words.en: If you describe someone as ultraconservative, you are emphasizing that they are extremely conservative in their beliefs, attitudes, or policies.

words.ex: He supports ultranationalism and rejects foreign influence.
words.ex_cn: 他支持极端民族主义，拒绝外来影响。
words.en: Ultranationalism is an extreme form of nationalism, especially when it promotes the interests of one state or people above all others.

words.tr: adj. 世界之外的；太阳系之外的；超俗的
words.ex: He dreams of ultramundane worlds beyond the sky.
words.ex_cn: 他梦想着天空之外的超凡世界。
words.en: Beyond the world or the material universe; spiritual or supernatural.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes UN-

words.ex: He showed unfeigned joy when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 当他赢得奖品时，他表现出真诚的喜悦。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or actions as unfeigned, you mean that they are genuine and not pretended.

words.tr: adj. 难以捍卫的；站不住脚的；不堪一击的
words.ex: His excuse was untenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口站不住脚。
words.en: If an argument, theory, or position is untenable, it cannot be defended or supported against criticism.

words.tr: adj. 不屈的；不屈服的；坚硬的
words.ex: He is unyielding in his decision.
words.ex_cn: 他在决定上毫不退让。
words.en: If you describe someone as unyielding, you mean that they are very determined and not likely to change their mind.

words.tr: adj. 毫不含糊的；清楚明白的
words.ex: His answer was unequivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答是明确无误的。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude as unequivocal, you mean that it is completely clear and very firm.

words.tr: v. 解开脚链；解除束缚
words.ex: He unfettered the dog from the chain.
words.ex_cn: 他把狗从链子上解开了。
words.en: To release from restraints or inhibitions.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes UNI-

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: This rule is universal for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则对所有学生都是普遍适用的。
words.en: Something that is universal affects or relates to every part of the world or the universe.

words.tr: adj. 单极的；单尾的（神经细胞等）
words.ex: The country has a unipolar political system.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个单极的政治体系。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by a single pole or extremity; especially : having or involving a single magnetic pole.

words.ex: The little girl drew a unicorn in her notebook.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩在笔记本上画了一只独角兽。
words.en: A unicorn is a mythical creature typically represented as a horse with a single straight horn projecting from its forehead.

words.tr: n. 一致同意；全体赞同
words.ex: The team showed unanimity in voting for the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队在投票支持新计划时意见一致。
words.en: Unanimity is complete agreement among all members of a group.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes URB

words.ex: The urban area has many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市地区有许多高楼。
words.en: relating to a city or town

words.ex: They live in a quiet suburb outside the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市外一个安静的市郊。
words.en: A suburb is a residential district located on the outskirts of a city.

words.tr: adj. 温文儒雅的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: He is an urbane man who speaks politely.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个举止文雅、说话有礼貌的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as urbane, you mean that they are polite, confident, and comfortable in social situations.

words.ex: The urbanite walks to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市居民每天步行上班。
words.en: An urbanite is a person who lives in a city or town.

words.tr: n. 都市学家；都市问题专家
words.ex: He is an urbanologist who studies city life.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位研究城市生活的城市学家。
words.en: An urbanologist is an expert in the study of urban development, planning, and the problems associated with city life.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes US/UT

words.ex: The usage of this machine is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器的使用非常简单。
words.en: The way in which something is used or the fact of being used.

words.ex: He tried to usurp the throne from his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从他兄弟手中篡夺王位。
words.en: If you say that someone usurps a job, role, title, or position, they take it from someone when they have no right to do this.

words.ex: He paid high usury on his loan.
words.ex_cn: 他支付了高额的高利贷。
words.en: The practice of lending money at an exorbitant interest rate.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.ex: This tool is utile for fixing the chair.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具对修理椅子很有用。
words.en: If something is utile, it is useful.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VAC/VACA/VACU

words.ex: Please vacate the room by noon.
words.ex_cn: 请在中午前腾出房间。
words.en: To vacate a place or position means to leave it or give it up, making it available for other people.

words.tr:
n. 真空；空虚；
v. 用真空吸尘器打扫；
words.ex: The vacuum in space keeps no air.
words.ex_cn: 太空中的真空没有空气。
words.en: A vacuum is a space that contains no air or other gas, or a space from which most of the air or gas has been removed. It can also refer to a device that cleans floors and surfaces by sucking up dirt and dust.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: His speech was full of vacuity.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满空洞。
words.en: If you refer to the vacuity of something or someone, you are critical of them because they lack intelligent thought or ideas.

words.ex: The plant cell has a large vacuole.
words.ex_cn: 植物细胞有一个大的液泡。
words.en: A vacuole is a space or vesicle within the cytoplasm of a cell, enclosed by a membrane and typically containing fluid.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VEH/VECT

words.tr: adj. 车辆的；作为媒介的；用车辆运载的
words.ex: The accident involved a vehicular crash.
words.ex_cn: 这起事故涉及一辆车的碰撞。
words.en: Relating to or designed for vehicles, especially cars.

words.tr: adv. 激烈地；猛烈地；强烈地
words.ex: She vehemently denied the accusation.
words.ex_cn: 她强烈否认了这项指控。
words.en: If you say or do something vehemently, you do it with great energy or passion because you feel very strongly about it.

words.tr: n. 向量；矢量；带菌媒介；航向
words.ex: He drew a vector to show the direction of the wind.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个向量来表示风的方向。
words.en: In physics and mathematics, a vector is a quantity that has both magnitude and direction, represented by an arrow whose direction is the same as that of the quantity and whose length is proportional to the quantity's magnitude.

words.tr: v. 引导（飞机），（为飞机）定向（vector的现在分词）; n. 确定航向
words.ex: The drone is vectoring toward the target.
words.ex_cn: 无人机正在朝目标方向飞行。
words.en: The process of directing or guiding something, especially an aircraft, in a particular direction.

words.ex: Heat rises through convection in the room.
words.ex_cn: 热量通过空气对流在房间中上升。
words.en: Convection is the process by which heat is transferred by the movement of a fluid, such as air or water, due to the difference in density caused by temperature differences.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VEN/VENT

words.ex: He invented a new machine to clean the house.
words.ex_cn: 他发明了一台新机器来打扫房子。
words.en: To invent something means to design or create it, especially something that has never been made before.

words.ex: Handwashing is a simple prevention of disease.
words.ex_cn: 洗手是预防疾病的一种简单方法。
words.en: The act of stopping something from happening or arising.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.ex: He contravenes the school rules by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: To contravene a law or rule means to do something that is forbidden by it.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VER/VERAC/VERI

words.tr: adj. 真实的；确实的；真正的
words.ex: It was a veritable treasure trove of old books.
words.ex_cn: 那是一个真正的旧书宝库。
words.en: You use veritable to emphasize the size, amount, or nature of something.

words.ex: The verity of his story was proven by the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他故事的真实性被证据证明了。
words.en: Verity refers to the quality or state of being true or real.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

words.ex: The movie has verisimilitude because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有逼真性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: the quality of seeming to be true or real

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VERB

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VERS/VERT

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VIA

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VICT/VINC/VANQ

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VID/VIS

words.tr:
n. 视频；录像；
adj. 视频的；录像的；
words.ex: I watched a short video on YouTube.
words.ex_cn: 我看了一个YouTube上的短视频。
words.en: A recording of moving visual images made digitally or on videotape.

words.ex: The stars are visible at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚可以看到星星。
words.en: If something is visible, it can be seen.

words.ex: The supervisor checked the workers' progress.
words.ex_cn: 主管检查了工人们的进展。
words.en: A supervisor is a person who oversees and directs the work of others.

words.ex: The hikers enjoyed a beautiful vista from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者们从山顶欣赏到了美丽的景色。
words.en: A vista is a pleasing view, especially one seen through a long, narrow opening.

words.ex: His visage showed deep sadness.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出深深的悲伤。
words.en: The appearance of the face or facial expression of a person.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VIR

words.tr: adj. 有男子气概的；阳刚的；强有力的
words.ex: He is a virile man who works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的男子，每天努力工作。
words.en: If you describe a man as virile, you mean that he has the qualities that a man is traditionally expected to have, such as strength and sexual power.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.ex: The virago shouted loudly at the driver.
words.ex_cn: 那个泼妇对司机大喊大叫。
words.en: A virago is a woman who is very aggressive or domineering.

words.tr: n. 男子气概；生殖力；活力
words.ex: He shows his virility by lifting heavy weights.
words.ex_cn: 他通过举重物展示自己的阳刚之气。
words.en: Virility refers to the qualities or characteristics traditionally associated with men, such as strength, vigor, and sexual potency.

words.tr: n. [生理] 男性化；[医] 男性化现象
words.ex: He shows signs of virilism at an early age.
words.ex_cn: 他在很小的时候就表现出男性化特征。
words.en: A condition in which a female develops male physical characteristics, such as a deep voice and increased body hair, due to an excess of male hormones.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VIT

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.tr: v. 给予 ... 生命力； 激发
words.ex: The new paint will vitalize the old house.
words.ex_cn: 新油漆会让这栋老房子焕然一新。
words.en: To give life or energy to something, making it more active or successful.

words.ex: He sent his curriculum vitae to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他把简历发给了公司。
words.en: A curriculum vitae is a written account of your education and the jobs you have done, which you send when you are applying for a job.

words.ex: Eating fruits gives you vitamin C.
words.ex_cn: 吃水果可以给你维生素C。
words.en: A vitamin is one of a group of organic substances which are essential in small quantities to the nutrition of most animals and some plants, and which are present in natural foodstuffs or sometimes produced within the body.

words.ex: The child shows great vitality while playing.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩耍时充满活力。
words.en: Vitality refers to the state of being strong and active; energy.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VIV/VIVA

words.tr: v. 幸存；生存；存活；艰难挺过；
words.ex: He survived the accident with minor injuries.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中幸存下来，只有轻微受伤。
words.en: If you survive in a dangerous situation, you continue to live or exist in spite of it.

words.ex: She is a vivacious girl who laughs loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个活泼的女孩，笑得很响亮。
words.en: If you describe someone as vivacious, you mean that they are lively, exciting, and attractive.

words.ex: The conviviality at the party made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 派对上的友好气氛让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: Conviviality is the quality of being friendly and making people feel happy and welcome.

words.ex: The children visit the vivarium to see live snakes.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们去活体动物馆看活蛇。
words.en: A vivarium is an area, usually enclosed, for keeping and raising animals or plants for observation or research.

words.ex: He opposes vivisection because it hurts animals.
words.ex_cn: 他反对活体解剖，因为这会伤害动物。
words.en: The practice of performing operations on live animals for the purpose of experimentation or scientific research (often considered to be cruel).

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VOC/VOKE

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.tr: adj. 无法改变的；不能取消的
words.ex: The decision was irrevocable.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是不可撤销的。
words.en: If a decision, action, or process is irrevocable, it cannot be changed or reversed.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VOL/VOLI

words.ex: He did voluntary work at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院做志愿工作。
words.en: If something is voluntary, you do it because you choose to, and not because you have to.

words.tr: n. 意志力；自愿选择；自行决断
words.ex: He did it of his own volition.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于自己的意愿做的。
words.en: The power to make your own decisions or choices.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VOLV/VOLU

words.tr: n. 意志力；自愿选择；自行决断
words.ex: He did it of his own volition.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于自己的意愿做的。
words.en: The power to make your own decisions or choices.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes VOR/VORAC

words.tr: n. 意志力；自愿选择；自行决断
words.ex: He did it of his own volition.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于自己的意愿做的。
words.en: The power to make your own decisions or choices.

words.ex: Bears are omnivorous animals.
words.ex_cn: 熊是杂食动物。
words.en: An omnivorous animal or person eats both plants and meat.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes XEN/XENO

words.tr: n. 排外的人；对陌生人或外国人恐惧或憎恨的人
words.ex: He is a xenophobe who hates foreigners.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个讨厌外国人的排外者。
words.en: A xenophobe is a person who has a strong dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.tr: n. 喜欢外国人（或国外事物）者
words.ex: He is a xenophile who loves trying food from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喜爱外国文化的人，喜欢尝试其他国家的食物。
words.en: A xenophile is a person who is attracted to foreign peoples, cultures, or customs.

words.tr: adj. 异型生物质的; n. （药物、杀虫剂、致癌物等）异型生物质
words.ex: The body breaks down xenobiotic chemicals quickly.
words.ex_cn: 身体会迅速分解外来化学物质。
words.en: A xenobiotic is a chemical substance found within an organism that is not naturally produced or expected to be present within the organism. It can also cover substances that are present in much higher concentrations than are usual.

words.ex: The rock contains a xenocryst from deep underground.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石中包含一个来自地下的捕虏晶。
words.en: A xenocryst is a crystal foreign to the igneous rock in which it is found, having been picked up by the magma as it rose through the crust.

words.tr: n. 世代交替；自然发生
words.ex: The book describes xenogenesis as a strange way life can change.
words.ex_cn: 这本书将异种发生描述为生命可能发生的一种奇怪方式。
words.en: The production of offspring markedly different from either parent.

chapters.name: 300 High-Frequency Word Roots and Prefixes ZO/ZOO

words.ex: He loves zoology and studies animals in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱动物学，研究野外的动物。
words.en: Zoology is the scientific study of animals.

words.ex: Some ancient cultures practiced zoolatry by worshipping animals as gods.
words.ex_cn: 一些古代文化通过崇拜动物作为神灵来实践动物崇拜。
words.en: The worship of animals, especially as gods or deities.

words.tr: adj. 动物传染的；来自动物的（等于 zoogenous）
words.ex: The poison is zoogenic and comes from animals.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒液是动物来源的，来自动物。
words.en: Relating to or resulting from the activities of animals.

words.tr: n. 动物病；[动] 动物传染病
words.ex: Some zoonosis can spread from dogs to humans.
words.ex_cn: 一些人畜共患疾病可以从狗传播给人类。
words.en: A zoonosis is any disease or infection that is naturally transmissible from vertebrate animals to humans.

words.ex: He was arrested for zoophilia.
words.ex_cn: 他因恋兽癖被逮捕。
words.en: Zoophilia is a paraphilia involving sexual attraction to animals.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -able,-ible:

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.tr:
adj. 不可挽救的；屡教不改的；不可救药的
n. 无可救药的人
words.ex: He is an incorrigible liar.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个无可救药的骗子。
words.en: If you describe someone as incorrigible, you mean that they have faults which they seem unable or unwilling to correct, even though they are aware of them.

words.tr: adj. 无可辩驳的；不能否认的
words.ex: The evidence is irrefutable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If you describe something such as evidence or a fact as irrefutable, you mean that it cannot be denied or disproved.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 谦恭有礼的；和蔼可亲的
words.ex: He is an affable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is affable is pleasant and friendly.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.ex: His laudable effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得赞美的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Deserving praise and commendation.

words.tr: adj. 应受谴责的；应受指责的；
words.ex: His lying to the teacher was reprehensible.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师撒谎是应受谴责的。
words.en: If you think that someone's behavior is reprehensible, you think that it is very bad or unacceptable.

words.ex: He is culpable for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他对这起事故负有责任。
words.en: If someone is culpable, they are responsible for something wrong or bad that has happened.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ac:

words.tr: n. 氨树胶；氨草胶; adj. 氨的；含氨的
words.ex: The smell of ammoniac is strong in the lab.
words.ex_cn: 实验室里氨水的味道很浓。
words.en: Relating to or containing ammonia; a salt of ammonia.

words.ex: He cannot eat bread because he is celiac.
words.ex_cn: 他不能吃面包，因为他有乳糜泻。
words.en: Celiac refers to something related to the abdomen or the celiac disease, an autoimmune disorder where the ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine.

words.tr:
n. 疯子；狂人；狂热分子
adj. 疯狂的；狂热的
words.ex: The maniac screamed loudly in the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯子在街上大声喊叫。
words.en: A maniac is a person who has a very strong interest in something or behaves in a very wild or violent way.

words.ex: The cardiac patient needs to rest daily.
words.ex_cn: 这位心脏病人需要每天休息。
words.en: Cardiac means relating to the heart.

words.tr:
n. 疑病症患者
adj. 患疑病症的
words.ex: He is a hypochondriac who thinks he is sick every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是个疑病症患者，每天都觉得自己生病了。
words.en: A hypochondriac is a person who is excessively anxious about their health and often believes they are suffering from a serious illness despite having no or only mild symptoms.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -age:

words.ex: He doesn't know his parentage.
words.ex_cn: 他不知道自己的身世。
words.en: The identity or origins of one's parents.

words.ex: He felt trapped in bondage.
words.ex_cn: 他感到被困在束缚中。
words.en: Bondage refers to the state of being a slave or being under the control of another person.

words.ex: The war caused terrible carnage on both sides.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争在双方都造成了惨烈的大屠杀。
words.en: The killing of a large number of people, especially in a violent way.

words.ex: The ship stopped at the anchorage to wait for the tide.
words.ex_cn: 船在停泊处停靠，等待涨潮。
words.en: An anchorage is a place where boats or ships can anchor safely.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -al,-ial:

words.tr: adj. 逻辑上的；合乎逻辑的；
words.ex: His argument is logical and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点合乎逻辑，容易理解。
words.en: In accordance with the principles of logic; reasonable.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.ex: The glacial landscape was covered in snow.
words.ex_cn: 冰河地貌被雪覆盖着。
words.en: relating to, resulting from, or denoting the presence or agency of ice, especially in the form of glaciers.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.tr: adj. 辩论的；引起争论的；争议的
words.ex: His polemical article sparked strong debates.
words.ex_cn: 他那篇有争议的文章引发了激烈争论。
words.en: A polemical piece of writing or speech is one that strongly argues against or in favor of a particular opinion, person, or idea, often in a way that is intended to provoke controversy.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.ex: The provincial government opened a new school.
words.ex_cn: 省政府开设了一所新学校。
words.en: Relating to a province or provinces; having the manners, viewpoints, etc., considered characteristic of unsophisticated inhabitants of a province; narrow-minded.

words.tr: adj. 修辞性的；词藻华丽的；反问的
words.ex: He asked a rhetorical question to make a point.
words.ex_cn: 他问了一个修辞性的问题来阐明观点。
words.en: A rhetorical question is one which is asked in order to make a statement rather than to get an answer.

words.ex: The cartoon is satirical and makes fun of politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画是讽刺性的，嘲笑政客。
words.en: A satirical piece of writing or speech uses satire to criticize people or ideas.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

words.ex: His denial of the mistake made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他否认错误，让所有人都生气了。
words.en: A denial is a statement that something is not true or does not exist.

words.ex: The actors had a rehearsal before the play.
words.ex_cn: 演出前，演员们进行了一次排练。
words.en: A rehearsal of a play, dance, or piece of music is a practice of it in preparation for a performance.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -an,-ian:

words.ex: He bought a Canadian maple syrup.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一瓶加拿大的枫糖浆。
words.en: Of or relating to Canada or its people, culture, or language.

words.tr:
adj. 弗洛伊德的
n. 弗洛伊德学的信奉者
words.ex: The psychologist used a Freudian approach to analyze the patient's dreams.
words.ex_cn: 心理学家使用佛洛伊德学派的方法来分析病人的梦境。
words.en: Relating to or influenced by Sigmund Freud or his methods of psychoanalysis.

words.ex: The dragon had a reptilian skin.
words.ex_cn: 这条龙有像爬行动物一样的皮肤。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of reptiles; resembling or suggestive of a reptile.

words.ex: The civilian population stayed safe during the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 平民在冲突期间保持安全。
words.en: A civilian is a person who is not a member of the military or of a police or firefighting force.

words.tr:
adj. （《圣经》中所说的大洪水前的）古老的；过时的
n.  年迈的人；不合时宜的人
words.ex: He uses an antediluvian typewriter to write letters.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台远古的打字机写信。
words.en: Belonging to the time before the biblical Flood; very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: The subterranean tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接着两栋大楼。
words.en: Existing, occurring, or done under the earth's surface.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ance,-ence:

words.ex: The subterranean tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接着两栋大楼。
words.en: Existing, occurring, or done under the earth's surface.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ant,-ent:

words.tr:
n. 文件；公文；文献；
v. 记录；为…提供证明；
words.ex: He submitted the document to the office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件提交给了办公室。
words.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；丑恶可耻的；公然的
words.ex: He made a flagrant mistake during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中犯了一个明显的错误。
words.en: If you describe an action as flagrant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way and is intended to shock or offend people.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；优厚的； 大方的
words.ex: He gave a munificent donation to the school.
words.ex_cn: 他向学校捐赠了一笔慷慨的款项。
words.en: If you describe someone as munificent, you mean that they are very generous, often in the form of giving money or gifts.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.ex: The virulent virus spread quickly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种剧毒的病毒迅速在小镇上传播。
words.en: A virulent disease or poison is extremely powerful and dangerous.

words.ex: The contestant won the singing competition.
words.ex_cn: 这位竞争者赢得了歌唱比赛。
words.en: A contestant is someone who takes part in a competition or contest.

words.tr: n. 迂腐之人；书呆子；学究
words.ex: He is a pedant who corrects every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑剔的书呆子，会纠正每一个小错误。
words.en: A pedant is a person who is excessively concerned with minor details and rules or with displaying academic learning.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ar,-ary:

words.ex: The solar panel collects energy from the sun.
words.ex_cn: 太阳能板从太阳收集能量。
words.en: Solar means relating to the sun or using the energy from the sun to produce electricity.

words.ex: The polar bear lives in the Arctic.
words.ex_cn: 北极熊生活在北极。
words.en: relating to the North or South Pole or to the region around it; having opposite extremes or characteristics.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；爱开玩笑的；滑稽的
words.ex: He is jocular during breaks, making everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他在休息时很幽默，让大家笑个不停。
words.en: If you say that someone has a jocular manner, you mean that they are cheerful and often make jokes or try to make people laugh.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.tr: n. 一百周年纪念；一百年；
words.ex: The town held a party for the centenary of its founding.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇为建镇一百周年纪念举行了派对。
words.en: A centenary is the one hundredth anniversary of a significant event.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ate:

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.tr: v. 对…表示极不赞成；强烈反对；轻视
words.ex: They deprecate old software.
words.ex_cn: 他们不推荐使用旧软件。
words.en: If you deprecate something, you criticize it or express your disapproval of it.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.ex: He helped extricate the car from the mud.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助把车从泥里解脱出来。
words.en: If you extricate someone or something from a place where they are trapped or caught, you succeed in freeing them.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.ex: The ornate ceiling had gold patterns and flowers.
words.ex_cn: 华丽的天花板上有金色的图案和花朵。
words.en: Something that is ornate is highly decorated with complex patterns.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -cy:

words.tr: n. 优势；支配地位；支配力量
words.ex: The king's ascendancy lasted for twenty years.
words.ex_cn: 国王的统治持续了二十年。
words.en: If one group has ascendancy over another group, it has more power or influence than the other group.

words.tr: n. 破产；倒闭；无偿付能力
words.ex: The company filed for bankruptcy last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年申请了破产。
words.en: Bankruptcy is a legal status of a person or other entity that cannot repay the debts it owes to creditors.

words.tr: n. 精神失常；疯狂；极蠢
words.ex: His idea to jump from the roof was pure lunacy.
words.ex_cn: 他从屋顶跳下去的主意简直是疯了。
words.en: Lunacy is behavior that is stupid, dangerous, or insane.

words.ex: The small country has a dependency on foreign aid.
words.ex_cn: 这个小国依赖外国援助。
words.en: A dependency is a situation in which someone or something relies on someone or something else for support or existence.

words.ex: His complacency made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的自满让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: A feeling of smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -dom:

words.tr: n. 封地，采邑（等于 fief）
words.ex: The company CEO's assistant had created a fiefdom in his department.
words.ex_cn: 公司CEO的助理在他部门里建立了一个小王国。
words.en: A fiefdom is a piece of land that was given to someone by a king or queen in the past, in return for their loyalty or services.

words.ex: He felt boredom during the long meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在漫长的会议中感到无聊。
words.en: Boredom is the state of feeling bored.

words.ex: The history of the church is filled with tales of martyrdom.
words.ex_cn: 教会的历史充满了殉道的传说。
words.en: The death or suffering of a martyr.

words.tr: n. 官场；官员（总称）；官僚作风
words.ex: He was frustrated by the inefficiencies of officialdom.
words.ex_cn: 他对官场的低效率感到沮丧。
words.en: The officials or bureaucrats considered as a group or class.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -eer,-er,-or:

words.ex: The auctioneer sold the painting for $10,000.
words.ex_cn: 拍卖师以一万美元卖出了这幅画。
words.en: An auctioneer is a person who conducts auctions by accepting bids and declaring goods sold.

words.ex: He is an engineer who builds bridges.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名建造桥梁的工程师。
words.en: An engineer is a person who designs, builds, or maintains engines, machines, or public works.

words.ex: He is a strong contender for the championship.
words.ex_cn: 他是冠军的有力竞争者。
words.en: A contender is someone who takes part in a competition or tries to win something.

words.ex: The director of the school gave a speech.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主任发表了一次演讲。
words.en: A director is a person who is in charge of something, especially a film, play, or organization.

words.tr: n. 遗嘱执行人；执行器；执行者
words.ex: The executor paid the bills after the man died.
words.ex_cn: 执行人在那人去世后支付了账单。
words.en: An executor is a person who carries out some task or someone who is appointed to carry out the terms of a will.

words.tr: n. 演说者；演讲者；雄辩家；
words.ex: He is a famous orator who speaks at large events.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在大型活动中演讲的著名演说者。
words.en: An orator is a person who delivers speeches or lectures, especially one who is skilled at doing so.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ery:

words.ex: I bought fresh bread from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 我从面包房买了新鲜面包。
words.en: A bakery is a place where bread, cakes, and pastries are made or sold.

words.ex: He went to jail for bribery.
words.ex_cn: 他因贿赂而入狱。
words.en: Bribery is the act of offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting something of value for the purpose of influencing the action of an official in the discharge of his or her public or legal duties.

words.ex: He resorted to chicanery to win the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠狡辩赢得了争论。
words.en: The use of trickery to achieve a political, financial, or legal purpose.

words.ex: He learned about slavery in history class.
words.ex_cn: 他在历史课上学到了奴隶制。
words.en: Slavery is the system by which people are owned by other people as slaves.

words.ex: He showed snobbery when he laughed at her old shoes.
words.ex_cn: 当他嘲笑她的旧鞋子时，表现出了势利。
words.en: Snobbery is the attitude or behavior of someone who thinks they are better than other people because they are more intelligent, more cultured, or of a higher social class than others.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -(esc)ent:

words.ex: The moon looks like a crescent tonight.
words.ex_cn: 今晚的月亮像一弯新月。
words.en: A crescent is a curved shape that is wider in the middle and pointed at the ends, like the shape of the moon in its first or last quarter.

words.ex: The nascent industry is growing quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个新生的产业正在迅速发展。
words.en: Nascent things or processes are just beginning, and are expected to become stronger or to grow bigger.

words.tr: adj. 很快消失的；渐消散的；短暂的
words.ex: The evanescent mist disappeared at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 那消散的薄雾在日出时消失了。
words.en: Something that is evanescent quickly disappears or fades away.

words.tr: adj. [昆] 发出磷光的；磷光性的
words.ex: The phosphorescent paint glowed in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 磷光涂料在黑暗中发光。
words.en: A phosphorescent substance or object emits light without becoming hot, after it has been exposed to light or another form of radiation.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ferous:

words.ex: The forest has many coniferous trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林有很多针叶树。
words.en: Coniferous refers to trees that produce cones and have needle-shaped leaves, typically evergreen.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.tr: adj. 含水的；[地质] 蓄水的
words.ex: The aquiferous layer in the soil helps in groundwater recharge.
words.ex_cn: 土壤中的含水层有助于地下水补给。
words.en: Containing or conveying water; especially : relating to or being a rock stratum or formation that is water-bearing.

words.tr: adj. 含钙的；[生物] 含碳酸钙的
words.ex: The shells of these marine organisms are calciferous.
words.ex_cn: 这些海洋生物的壳是含钙的。
words.en: Containing or producing calcium.

words.ex: The coal deposits in this region are from the Carboniferous period.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区的煤炭沉积来自石炭纪。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the fifth period of the Paleozoic era, between the Devonian and Permian periods, or the system of rocks deposited during it.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -fic:

words.ex: The concert was terrific!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something or someone as terrific, you are very pleased with them or very impressed by them.

words.tr: adj. 恐怖的；令人震惊的
words.ex: The accident was horrific.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故非常可怕。
words.en: If you say that something is horrific, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant and shocking.

words.tr: adj. 快乐安详的；幸福的
words.ex: She had a beatific smile after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祈祷后，她脸上带着宁静幸福的微笑。
words.en: A beatific expression, smile, or vision shows great happiness and calmness.

words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.tr:
adj. 催眠的；让人瞌睡的
n. 安眠药
words.ex: The monotonous lecture was so soporific that I couldn't keep my eyes open.
words.ex_cn: 那个单调乏味的讲座让我昏昏欲睡，眼睛都睁不开了。
words.en: A soporific substance or activity makes you feel sleepy.

words.ex: The benefic effects of exercise are well-documented.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼的有益效果有据可查。
words.en: Having a good or helpful effect; doing good.

words.ex: The malefic influence of the full moon can cause erratic behavior.
words.ex_cn: 满月的有害影响会导致行为异常。
words.en: Having or exerting a harmful influence; causing harm or destruction.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -fy:

words.ex: He tried to falsify the report.
words.ex_cn: 他试图篡改报告。
words.en: To falsify means to change something in order to deceive people, or to make a false statement.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.ex: The storm personifies anger with loud thunder.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴用雷声拟人化了愤怒。
words.en: To represent a thing or abstraction as a person; to embody in a person.

words.ex: The machine purifies water by removing dirt.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器通过去除杂质来净化水。
words.en: To purify something means to make it clean and pure by removing dirty or harmful substances from it.

words.ex: He was mortified when he forgot his lines on stage.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记舞台上的台词时，他感到非常羞愧。
words.en: To mortify someone means to cause them to feel very embarrassed or ashamed. To mortify a part of your body means to discipline it by denying it things that it wants or needs.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ia:

words.ex: He has anorexia and eats very little food.
words.ex_cn: 他患有厌食症，吃得很少。
words.en: Anorexia is a psychological disorder characterized by an obsessive desire to lose weight by refusing to eat.

words.ex: Toxemia is a serious condition that can occur during pregnancy.
words.ex_cn: 毒血症是怀孕期间可能发生的一种严重病症。
words.en: Toxemia is a condition in which the blood contains toxins produced by body cells at a local source of infection or derived from the growth of microorganisms.

words.ex: Septicemia can lead to organ failure if not treated promptly.
words.ex_cn: 败血症如果不及时治疗可能导致器官衰竭。
words.en: Septicemia, also known as blood poisoning, is a serious bloodstream infection. It occurs when a bacterial infection elsewhere in the body, such as in the lungs or skin, enters the bloodstream.

words.ex: He collected memorabilia from the World Cup.
words.ex_cn: 他收集了世界杯的大事记。
words.en: Memorabilia are objects that are kept because they are connected with a memorable event or person.

words.ex: She carefully organized her personalia before the move.
words.ex_cn: 她在搬家前仔细整理了她的个人用品。
words.en: Personal details or information about someone, especially when considered as a collection.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ial:

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.ex: The glacial landscape was covered in snow.
words.ex_cn: 冰河地貌被雪覆盖着。
words.en: relating to, resulting from, or denoting the presence or agency of ice, especially in the form of glaciers.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.

words.tr: adj. 不重要的；无关紧要的
words.ex: His comment was inconsequential to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论对决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as inconsequential, you mean that it is not important.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

chapters.name: Common Suffixes ic:

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.tr: adj. 快乐主义者的；快乐论的；快乐主义的
words.ex: He leads a hedonistic life, always seeking pleasure.
words.ex_cn: 他过着快乐主义的生活，总是追求快乐。
words.en: If you describe someone as hedonistic, you mean that they are devoted to the pursuit of pleasure.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；苛性的；尖酸刻薄的
n. 腐蚀剂
words.ex: The caustic liquid burned through the metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种腐蚀性的液体腐蚀了金属。
words.en: A caustic substance is able to burn or destroy organic tissue by chemical action. Caustic remarks are extremely critical, sarcastic, or bitter.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.ex: He gave his last dollar to the homeless man, showing an altruistic heart.
words.ex_cn: 他把最后一美元给了那个无家可归的人，表现出一颗无私的心。
words.en: If you describe someone as altruistic, you mean that they show unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

words.ex: The word 'thou' is archaic in modern English.
words.ex_cn: ‘thou’这个词在现代英语中是过时的。
words.en: Very old or old-fashioned.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.tr: adj. 夸大的；言过其实的
words.ex: He gave a bombastic speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as bombastic, you are criticizing them for trying to impress other people by saying things that sound impressive but have little meaning.

words.tr: adj. 隐秘的；秘密的；隐晦的
words.ex: He gave a cryptic answer and left.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个神秘的回答，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something as cryptic, you mean that it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 教条的；武断的；固执己见的
words.ex: He is dogmatic about his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念非常固执。
words.en: If you say that someone is dogmatic, you are critical of them because they are convinced that they are right, and refuse to consider that other opinions might also be justified.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.ex: It's ironic that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: If you say that it is ironic that something happens, you mean that it is odd or amusing because it involves a contrast or is the opposite of what you would expect.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.ex: The lunatic was taken to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯人被送到了医院。
words.en: A lunatic is someone who behaves in a crazy or very foolish way.

words.ex: He was called a heretic for his strange beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 因为他奇怪的信仰，他被称为异端。
words.en: A heretic is someone whose beliefs or actions are considered wrong by most people, because they disagree with beliefs that are generally accepted.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ide:

words.ex: Diglycerides are used as emulsifiers in processed foods.
words.ex_cn: 甘油二酯被用作加工食品中的乳化剂。
words.en: A diglyceride is an ester formed from glycerol and two fatty acids, used as an emulsifier in food products.

words.ex: Glucose is a monosaccharide.
words.ex_cn: 葡萄糖是一种单糖。
words.en: A monosaccharide is the simplest form of carbohydrate and cannot be hydrolyzed to give a simpler sugar.

words.ex: Salt contains sodium chloride.
words.ex_cn: 盐含有氯化钠。
words.en: A chloride is a chemical compound of chlorine with another element or group, especially a salt of the anion Cl− or any compound containing chlorine in which the latter is more electronegative than the other element.

words.ex: Bananas have a lot of potassium.
words.ex_cn: 香蕉含有大量的钾。
words.en: A soft silver-white reactive metal of the alkali metal group, occurring principally in the form of salts in seawater and in minerals such as sylvite and carnallite.

words.tr: n. 溴化物；溴化物镇静剂；陈腔滥调
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a bromide for his anxiety.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了一种溴化物来治疗焦虑。
words.en: A bromide is a chemical compound containing bromine, or a remark or statement that is unoriginal and used too often.

words.ex: Titanium boride is used in high-temperature applications.
words.ex_cn: 钛硼化物用于高温应用。
words.en: A boride is a compound between boron and a less electronegative element, for example, a metal. Borides are hard, high-melting materials and are used in abrasives and as refractory materials.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -il,-ile:

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: His puerile jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puerile, you mean that they are silly and childish.

words.tr: adj. 可延展的；易于塑造的
words.ex: The gold is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 金具有延展性，可以拉成细丝。
words.en: A ductile material is one that can be stretched into a wire or hammered into a thin sheet without breaking.

words.tr: adj. 婴儿的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: The infantile smile made everyone feel warm.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿般的微笑让每个人都感到温暖。
words.en: Infantile behavior or illnesses are typical of very young children.

words.tr: adj. 年老的；衰老的；老糊涂的
words.ex: The senile man forgot his son's name.
words.ex_cn: 这位年老的男子忘记了他儿子的名字。
words.en: If someone is senile, they are behaving in a confused or strange way, and unable to remember things, because they are old.

words.tr: adj. 屈从的；奴隶的；逢迎的
words.ex: He gave a servile answer to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他向老板给出了卑躬屈膝的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as servile, you disapprove of them because they are too eager to obey someone or do things for them.

words.ex: The rope has high tensile strength.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子有很高的抗拉强度。
words.en: relating to tension; capable of being stretched or drawn out

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ine:

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.tr:
adj. 猫（科）的
n. 猫科动物
words.ex: The feline slept on the windowsill.
words.ex_cn: 那只猫在窗台上睡觉。
words.en: A feline is an animal that belongs to the cat family, including lions, tigers, and domestic cats. Feline can also describe something that is like a cat in appearance or behavior.

words.ex: The marine birds fly over the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这些海鸟在海面上飞翔。
words.en: Marine is used to describe things relating to the sea or to the ships and boats which sail on it.

words.ex: His leonine mane of hair made him look powerful and regal.
words.ex_cn: 他那狮子般的浓密头发使他看起来既强大又威严。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a lion.

words.tr: adj. 忧郁的；乖戾的；严肃的
words.ex: He has a saturnine mood and rarely smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他情绪阴郁，很少微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as saturnine, you mean that they are serious and unfriendly.

words.tr: n. 乳白色；乳白玻璃; adj. 蛋白石的，蛋白石状的；发乳光的；乳白色的
words.ex: The opaline glass vase caught the light beautifully.
words.ex_cn: 乳白玻璃花瓶在灯光下显得格外美丽。
words.en: Resembling opal in appearance; having a milky or pearly luster.

words.ex: The sugar formed a crystalline structure.
words.ex_cn: 糖形成了晶状结构。
words.en: Something that is crystalline is clear and transparent like crystal, or is made up of crystals.

words.ex: The tourmaline gemstone is known for its vibrant colors.
words.ex_cn: 电气石宝石以其鲜艳的颜色而闻名。
words.en: Tourmaline is a crystalline mineral that can be found in a variety of colors and is often used as a gemstone in jewelry.

words.tr: n. 鲜红色，深粉红色; adj. 鲜红色的，深粉红色的; v. （使）呈鲜红色；染红
words.ex: The sunset painted the sky in incarnadine hues.
words.ex_cn: 夕阳将天空染成了鲜红色。
words.en: Of a blood-red or pinkish-red color.

words.ex: He buys gasoline for his car every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周为他的汽车买汽油。
words.en: Gasoline is a volatile, flammable liquid obtained from petroleum and used as fuel in internal combustion engines.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ion,-tion,-ation:

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.ex: He fell into oblivion after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，他被遗忘了。
words.en: A state of being forgotten or unknown.

words.ex: The limitation of the phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的限制是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A limitation is a rule or situation that restricts what you can do or what can happen.

words.ex: He felt uncomfortable with the adulation from his fans.
words.ex_cn: 他对于粉丝们的盲目崇拜感到不舒服。
words.en: Excessive admiration or praise.

words.ex: He gave her a loud affirmation.
words.ex_cn: 他给了她一个大声的肯定。
words.en: An affirmation is a statement or sign that something is true.

words.ex: He felt apprehension before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到焦虑。
words.en: Anxiety or fear that something bad or unpleasant will happen; understanding; the action of arresting someone.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: The pollution caused the degradation of the river.
words.ex_cn: 污染导致了河流的恶化。
words.en: The process by which something is reduced in quality, value, or status.

words.ex: He has a disinclination to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意在公众场合讲话。
words.en: A disinclination to do something is a feeling of not wanting to do it.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ise,-ize:

words.tr:
v. 臆测；猜想
n. 臆测；猜度
words.ex: He surmises that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you surmise that something is true, you guess it from the available evidence, although you do not know for certain.

words.tr: v. 使增加至最大限度；最大化；
words.ex: He tries to maximize his profit by selling more.
words.ex_cn: 他通过多卖东西来使利润达到最大。
words.en: To maximize something means to make it as great in amount, size, or importance as possible.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

words.ex: The sun vaporizes water from the lake.
words.ex_cn: 太阳把湖里的水蒸发了。
words.en: To convert or be converted into vapor.

words.ex: Scientists hypothesize that water once existed on Mars.
words.ex_cn: 科学家假设火星上曾经存在水。
words.en: To hypothesize means to suggest a possible explanation for something, which has not yet been proved to be true.

words.ex: The doctor cauterized the wound to stop the bleeding.
words.ex_cn: 医生烧灼伤口以止血。
words.en: To burn the skin or wound with a hot instrument or caustic substance to stop bleeding or prevent infection.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ism:

words.tr: n. 民族优越感；本国中心主义
words.ex: Ethnocentrism often leads to misunderstandings and conflicts between different cultures.
words.ex_cn: 民族优越感常常导致不同文化之间的误解和冲突。
words.en: The belief in the inherent superiority of one's own ethnic group or culture.

words.tr: n. 自我主义；利己主义
words.ex: His egotism makes him talk only about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他的自我中心让他只谈论自己。
words.en: Egotism is the practice of talking and thinking about oneself excessively because of an undue sense of self-importance.

words.ex: His fanaticism for the team made him miss work.
words.ex_cn: 他对球队的狂热让他错过了工作。
words.en: Fanaticism is the quality of being fanatical, which means having very extreme and often unreasonable beliefs, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: He received criticism for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而受到批评。
words.en: Criticism is the act of expressing disapproval of someone or something and of the faults they have or the mistakes they have made.

words.tr: n. 俏皮话；妙语；诙谐语
words.ex: His speech was filled with witticisms that kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了妙语，让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A witticism is a clever and amusing remark.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ist:

words.tr:
n. 机会主义者
adj. 机会主义的；投机的；见风转舵的
words.ex: He was criticized as an opportunist who would do anything for personal gain.
words.ex_cn: 他因投机取巧、为个人利益不择手段而受到批评。
words.en: An opportunist is someone who takes advantage of any opportunity to achieve an end, often with little regard for principles or consequences.

words.tr: n. 漫画家；动画片画家；
words.ex: The cartoonist draws funny animals for children's magazines.
words.ex_cn: 这位漫画家为儿童杂志画有趣的小动物。
words.en: A cartoonist is an artist who draws cartoons, especially for newspapers or magazines.

words.tr: n. 口技表演者；腹语表演者；
words.ex: The ventriloquist made his doll talk funny.
words.ex_cn: 这位口技表演者让他的玩偶说起了滑稽的话。
words.en: A ventriloquist is someone who can speak without moving their lips and who entertains people by making it seem as if a puppet is talking.

words.tr: n. 利他主义者；爱他主义者
words.ex: He was known as an altruist who always put others' needs before his own.
words.ex_cn: 他以利他主义者著称，总是把别人的需要放在自己之前。
words.en: An altruist is someone who shows unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

words.tr:
n. 和平主义者；反战主义者
adj. 非战主义的
words.ex: He is a pacifist and refuses to fight in wars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名和平主义者，拒绝参与战争。
words.en: A pacifist is someone who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable and that disputes should be settled by peaceful means.

words.ex: The nihilist rejected all forms of organized religion.
words.ex_cn: 那个虚无主义者拒绝了一切形式的宗教组织。
words.en: A nihilist is someone who believes that life has no inherent meaning, value, or purpose.

words.ex: The prohibitionist movement gained momentum in the early 20th century.
words.ex_cn: 禁酒主义运动在20世纪早期获得了动力。
words.en: A prohibitionist is someone who advocates for the prohibition of something, especially alcoholic beverages.

words.tr: n. 通晓数国语言的人；语言学家；
words.ex: He is a linguist who speaks five languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位通晓五种语言的人。
words.en: A linguist is someone who studies language or languages, especially a person who studies linguistics.

words.ex: The geologist studied rocks in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这位地质学家研究了山里的岩石。
words.en: A geologist is a scientist who studies the solid, liquid, and gaseous matter that constitutes the Earth and other terrestrial planets, as well as the processes that shape them.

words.tr: n. 精神病学家；精神科医生
words.ex: He visits a psychiatrist every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周去看一次精神科医生。
words.en: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental illnesses and emotional disorders.

words.ex: The scientist studies stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家研究夜空中的恒星。
words.en: A scientist is someone who has studied science and whose job is to teach or do research in science.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ite:

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.tr: n. 以色列人；古以色列的居民
words.ex: The ancient israelite people lived in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 古代的以色列人生活在沙漠中。
words.en: An Israelite is a member of the ancient Hebrew nation, especially in the period from the Exodus to the Babylonian Captivity.

words.tr: n. 勒德分子；反对使用新技术的人；
words.ex: He is a luddite who refuses to use smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 他是个拒绝使用智能手机的勒德分子。
words.en: A Luddite is someone who is opposed to the introduction of new working methods, especially new machines.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -itis:

words.ex: He has dermatitis on his arms.
words.ex_cn: 他的胳膊上有皮炎。
words.en: Dermatitis is a condition in which the skin becomes red, swollen, and sore, sometimes with small blisters, resulting from direct irritation of the skin by an external agent or an allergic reaction to it.

words.ex: The doctor diagnosed phlebitis in her leg.
words.ex_cn: 医生诊断出她的腿患有静脉炎。
words.en: Phlebitis is the inflammation of a vein, usually in the legs.

words.ex: He has appendicitis and needs surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他得了阑尾炎，需要手术。
words.en: Appendicitis is a medical condition in which the appendix becomes inflamed and painful, often requiring surgery to remove the appendix.

words.ex: He has tendonitis in his wrist from playing tennis.
words.ex_cn: 他因为打网球得了手腕肌腱炎。
words.en: Inflammation of a tendon, most commonly from overuse but also from infection or rheumatic disease.

words.ex: Osteoarthritis is a common joint disorder that primarily affects cartilage.
words.ex_cn: 骨关节炎是一种常见的关节疾病，主要影响软骨。
words.en: A type of arthritis that occurs when flexible tissue at the ends of bones wears down.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ity,-ty:

words.ex: He felt animosity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对邻居感到敌意。
words.en: Animosity is a strong feeling of dislike and anger towards someone.

words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.ex: The movie shows a fantasy, not reality.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示的是幻想，而不是现实。
words.en: Reality is the state of things as they actually exist, rather than as they may appear or might be imagined.

words.ex: The rules show uniformity in all schools.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则在所有学校中都保持一致。
words.en: The state or quality of being uniform; consistency.

words.ex: The similarity between the two paintings is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这两幅画的相似点很明显。
words.en: The quality or state of being similar; likeness or resemblance.

words.ex: He felt enmity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对他邻居怀有敌意。
words.en: Enmity is a feeling of hostility or ill will towards someone or something.

words.tr: n. 奸诈；欺骗；口是心非
words.ex: He showed duplicity by lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他通过对朋友撒谎表现出虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of duplicity, you mean that they are deceitful.

words.tr: n. 堕落；道德败坏；腐化
words.ex: The depravity of his crimes shocked the community.
words.ex_cn: 他罪行的堕落程度震惊了整个社区。
words.en: Depravity is the state of being morally bad or evil.

words.ex: The insularity of Japan affects its cultural traditions.
words.ex_cn: 日本的岛国特性影响了它的文化传统。
words.en: The state of being isolated or detached from others, often resulting in a narrow or limited perspective.

words.tr: n. 恶名；坏名声；声名狼藉
words.ex: The criminal gained notoriety for his bold robberies.
words.ex_cn: 这名罪犯因大胆的抢劫而声名狼藉。
words.en: Notoriety is the state of being famous or well known for something bad.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.tr: n. 男子气概；生殖力；活力
words.ex: He shows his virility by lifting heavy weights.
words.ex_cn: 他通过举重物展示自己的阳刚之气。
words.en: Virility refers to the qualities or characteristics traditionally associated with men, such as strength, vigor, and sexual potency.

words.ex: His tenacity helped him finish the marathon despite the pain.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚韧让他即使疼痛也完成了马拉松。
words.en: The quality or fact of being able to grip something firmly; the quality or fact of being very determined and not giving up easily.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

chapters.name: Common Suffixes -ive:

words.ex: He is argumentative in class and always disagrees with the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上爱争辩，总是不同意老师的意见。
words.en: Someone who is argumentative is always ready to disagree or start arguing with other people.

words.ex: He is introspective and often thinks about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他善于内省，经常思考自己的感受。
words.en: If you describe someone as introspective, you mean that they spend a lot of time examining their own thoughts, ideas, and feelings.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.
