words.ex: We arrived at the opportune moment, just as the meeting was starting.
words.ex_cn: 我们到达得很及时，正好会议刚开始。
words.en: If something happens at an opportune time or is opportune, it happens at the time that is most convenient for someone or most likely to lead to success.

words.tr:
n. 机会主义者
adj. 机会主义的；投机的；见风转舵的
words.ex: He was criticized as an opportunist who would do anything for personal gain.
words.ex_cn: 他因投机取巧、为个人利益不择手段而受到批评。
words.en: An opportunist is someone who takes advantage of any opportunity to achieve an end, often with little regard for principles or consequences.

words.ex: He faced opprobrium for lying to the public.
words.ex_cn: 他因对公众撒谎而遭到谴责。
words.en: Opprobrium is harsh criticism or censure; public disgrace arising from shameful conduct.

words.tr: n. 眼镜商；验光师；眼镜商店
words.ex: He visited the optician to get new glasses.
words.ex_cn: 他去眼镜店配了新眼镜。
words.en: A person who makes or sells eyeglasses and other optical instruments.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.tr: adj. 可选择的；非强制的；
words.ex: The field trip is optional.
words.ex_cn: 这次郊游是可选的。
words.en: If something is optional, you can choose whether or not you do it or have it.

words.ex: The optometrist checked my eyes last week.
words.ex_cn: 验光师上周检查了我的眼睛。
words.en: An optometrist is a person whose job is to examine people's eyes and to recommend and sell glasses.

words.ex: The palace showed opulence with golden walls and silk curtains.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿以金墙和丝绸窗帘展现了富裕。
words.en: Opulence is great wealth or luxuriousness.

words.tr: n. 编号作品；乐曲；艺术作品
words.ex: The composer's latest opus has received critical acclaim.
words.ex_cn: 这位作曲家的最新作品获得了评论界的好评。
words.en: An opus is a creative work, especially a musical composition or set of compositions numbered in order of publication.

words.ex: His oracular words confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他那神秘莫测的话语让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as oracular, you mean that it is like an oracle, especially because it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.tr: n. 演说者；演讲者；雄辩家；
words.ex: He is a famous orator who speaks at large events.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在大型活动中演讲的著名演说者。
words.en: An orator is a person who delivers speeches or lectures, especially one who is skilled at doing so.

words.ex: The oratorio was performed by a large choir.
words.ex_cn: 清唱剧由一个大合唱团表演。
words.en: An oratorio is a large musical composition for orchestra, choir, and soloists. Like an opera, an oratorio includes the use of a choir, soloists, an ensemble, various distinguishable characters, and arias. However, opera is musical theatre, while oratorio is strictly a concert piece.

words.tr: v. 授予圣职；命令；注定
words.ex: The priest will ordain the new pastor next Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 神父将在下个星期日任命这位新牧师。
words.en: To ordain someone as a priest or minister means to officially make them a priest or minister, usually in a religious ceremony. To ordain something means to order or command it officially.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.ex: The city passed an ordinance to stop littering.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过了一项禁止乱扔垃圾的法令。
words.en: An ordinance is an authoritative rule, law, decree, or command.

words.tr: n. 圣职授任；授任圣职典礼
words.ex: The ordination of the new bishop was a grand ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 新主教的任命仪式非常隆重。
words.en: The act of ordaining or conferring holy orders on someone.

words.ex: The party turned into an orgy of drinking and dancing.
words.ex_cn: 派对变成了饮酒跳舞的狂欢。
words.en: An orgy is a wild party or gathering where people behave in an unrestrained way, often involving excessive drinking, eating, or sexual activity.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words P

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.tr: adj. 宫殿般的；宏伟的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: He lives in a palatial house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边一座宏伟的房子里。
words.en: If you describe a building or a place as palatial, you mean that it is very large, impressive, or luxurious, like a palace.

words.ex: He loves paleontology and finds dinosaur bones.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱古生物学，寻找恐龙骨头。
words.en: The branch of science concerned with fossil animals and plants.

words.ex: The painter arranged his colors on the palette.
words.ex_cn: 画家把颜色放在调色板上。
words.en: A palette is a flat piece of wood, plastic, etc., on which an artist mixes paints.

words.tr: n. 重写羊皮纸；仍然能看出痕迹的东西
words.ex: The manuscript is a palimpsest, with earlier texts visible beneath the more recent writing.
words.ex_cn: 这手稿是一个重写本，较早的文本在较新的书写之下依然可见。
words.en: A palimpsest is a manuscript or piece of writing material on which the original writing has been effaced to make room for later writing but of which traces remain.

words.tr:
n. 柩衣；棺罩；帷幕；遮盖物
v. 使人厌倦；变得枯躁无味
words.ex: The pall of smoke from the factory hung over the town.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟幕笼罩着整个城镇。
words.en: A pall is a dark cloud of smoke, dust, or similar, or a feeling of fear, sadness, or depression.

words.tr: n. 托盘；（运货用的）托台；（睡觉用的）草垫子
words.ex: The goods were packed onto pallets for easy transportation.
words.ex_cn: 货物被装在托盘上以便于运输。
words.en: A pallet is a flat wooden or metal platform on which goods are stacked so that they can be lifted and moved easily, for example by a forklift truck.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medication to palliate the patient's pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了药来减轻病人的疼痛。
words.en: To palliate means to make something less severe or intense without actually solving the cause of it. It can refer to the easing of physical pain or the attempt to make a fault or crime seem less serious.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；暗淡的；无生气的
words.ex: Her face was pallid after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 久病之后，她的脸色变得苍白。
words.en: If you describe something such as a performance or a piece of writing as pallid, you mean that it is weak and not at all exciting or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: Her heart palpitated with excitement.
words.ex_cn: 她的心脏因兴奋而悸动。
words.en: If your heart palpitates, it beats very fast and in an irregular way, usually because you are anxious or frightened.

words.ex: He gave a paltry amount of money to charity.
words.ex_cn: 他捐给慈善机构的钱微不足道。
words.en: If you describe an amount of money as paltry, you mean that it is very small.

words.ex: He put the bread in the pan.
words.ex_cn: 他把面包放进平底锅里。
words.en: A pan is a round metal container with a long handle, which is used for cooking things in, usually on top of a stove.

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.ex: He wore the hat with panache.
words.ex_cn: 他戴着那顶帽子，显得很夸耀。
words.en: If you do something with panache, you do it in a confident, stylish, and elegant way.

words.ex: The pandemic caused many schools to close.
words.ex_cn: 这场流行病导致许多学校关闭。
words.en: A pandemic is an occurrence of a disease that affects many people over a wide area.

words.tr: n. 喧嚣；大混乱；大吵大闹
words.ex: The crowd created pandemonium when the winner was announced.
words.ex_cn: 当获胜者被宣布时，人群陷入了混乱。
words.en: Pandemonium is a situation in which there is a lot of noise and confusion because people are excited, angry, or frightened.

words.ex: The show pandered to children's tastes.
words.ex_cn: 这个节目迎合了孩子们的口味。
words.en: If you pander to someone or to their wishes, you do everything that they want, often to get some advantage for yourself.

words.ex: The speech was a panegyric to the retiring chairman.
words.ex_cn: 这场演讲是对即将退休的主席的赞颂。
words.en: A panegyric is a formal public speech, or written verse, delivered in high praise of a person or thing, a eulogy.

words.ex: The view from the hill is panoramic.
words.ex_cn: 从山上望去，景色一览无余。
words.en: A panoramic view or picture is one that shows a wide area of land or sea.

words.tr:
n. 哑剧；（英）圣诞童话剧
v. 打手势；演哑剧
words.ex: The children laughed at the clown's pantomime.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们笑了，因为小丑的哑剧表演。
words.en: Pantomime is a type of entertainment where performers express a story or represent characters through gestures and body movements without using speech.

words.ex: Ancient Egyptians wrote on papyrus.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人在纸莎草纸上写字。
words.en: Papyrus is a material similar to thick paper that was used in ancient times as a writing surface. It was made from the pith of the papyrus plant, Cyperus papyrus, a wetland sedge.

words.ex: The parable of the Good Samaritan teaches compassion and kindness.
words.ex_cn: 好撒玛利亚人的寓言教导了同情和善良。
words.en: A simple story used to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson, as told by Jesus in the Gospels.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.ex: The parallelism between the two events is striking.
words.ex_cn: 这两件事之间的相似之处非常明显。
words.en: Parallelism is the state of being parallel or of corresponding in some way.

words.ex: The teacher changed the parameter to make the test easier.
words.ex_cn: 老师更改了参数，使测试更容易。
words.en: A parameter is a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.ex: She kept her paramour a secret from her husband.
words.ex_cn: 她对丈夫隐瞒了她的情人。
words.en: A paramour is someone with whom one is having a romantic or sexual relationship outside of marriage.

words.ex: His paranoia made him believe that everyone was out to get him.
words.ex_cn: 他的多疑让他相信每个人都在算计他。
words.en: Paranoia is the unreasonable feeling that you are being threatened in some way, or that people are trying to harm you, without any evidence.

words.ex: He packed his paraphernalia before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 他在旅行前收拾好了随身用具。
words.en: The equipment, apparatus, or furnishing used in or necessary for a particular activity.

words.ex: He paraphrased the poem in simple words.
words.ex_cn: 他用简单的语言意译了这首诗。
words.en: To paraphrase means to express the meaning of something written or spoken using different words, especially to achieve greater clarity.

words.tr: n. 寄生虫；寄生生物；依赖他人过活者；
words.ex: The parasite lives inside the host's body.
words.ex_cn: 这种寄生虫生活在宿主的体内。
words.en: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host organism and gets its food from or at the expense of its host.

words.tr: adj. 焦干的；干渴的； v. “parch”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The parched earth cracked under the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 焦干的土地在烈日下开裂了。
words.en: If something is parched, it is extremely dry, especially because of hot weather.

words.tr: n. 被社会遗弃者；贱民；底层民众
words.ex: He felt like a pariah in the community after the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 丑闻之后，他在社区里感觉像个贱民。
words.en: A pariah is someone who is not accepted by a particular group, especially because they are believed to have done something wrong or unacceptable.

words.ex: The parity of the numbers is important in this game.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的奇偶性在这个游戏中很重要。
words.en: If there is parity between two things, they are equal to each other.

words.ex: In everyday parlance, people call it a phone.
words.ex_cn: 在日常用语中，人们称它为电话。
words.en: A particular way of speaking or using words, especially a way common to those with a particular job or interest.

words.tr:
v. 会谈；谈判
n. 会谈；谈判
words.ex: The two sides agreed to parley in order to resolve their differences.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意进行会谈以解决分歧。
words.en: A parley is a discussion between two opposing sides in a conflict, especially a discussion of terms for a truce.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.tr:
n. 拙劣的模仿（作品）
v. 拙劣模仿
words.ex: The film is a parody of classic horror movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对经典恐怖电影的滑稽模仿。
words.en: A parody is a humorous or satirical imitation of a serious piece of literature or writing.

words.tr: n. 突然发作；激发；阵发
words.ex: She experienced a paroxysm of coughing during the night.
words.ex_cn: 她在夜里经历了一次剧烈的咳嗽发作。
words.en: A paroxysm is a sudden attack or outburst of a particular emotion or activity.

words.tr: n. 拼花地板；镶木地板
words.ex: The floor was covered with a beautiful parquet.
words.ex_cn: 地板上铺着漂亮的镶木地板。
words.en: Parquet is a type of flooring made by arranging small blocks of wood in a geometric pattern, often used in ballrooms and theaters.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；避开；回避
n. 挡开；闪避
words.ex: He parries the punch with his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他用胳膊格挡了这一拳。
words.en: If you parry a question or argument, you cleverly avoid answering it or dealing with it. In fencing, if you parry a blow, you defend yourself against it by pushing it away with your weapon.

words.tr: n. 吝啬；小气；过度节俭
words.ex: His parsimony led to a reputation for stinginess.
words.ex_cn: 他的吝啬导致了他被认为是个小气鬼。
words.en: Parsimony is the quality of being very unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: He only read the partial report.
words.ex_cn: 他只读了部分报告。
words.en: If you describe something as partial, you mean that it is not complete or whole.

words.ex: He showed partiality toward his favorite student.
words.ex_cn: 他对最喜欢的学生表现出偏袒。
words.en: If you have a partiality for something, you like it very much.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.tr:
n. 划分；隔离物；分割
v. 分开；隔开
words.ex: The partition of the room made it more private.
words.ex_cn: 房间的隔断让它更私密了。
words.en: A partition is a wall, screen, or divider that separates one part of a room, vehicle, or other space from another.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；已过盛年的
words.ex: The fashion styles of the 1980s are now considered passé.
words.ex_cn: 20世纪80年代的时尚风格现在被认为已经过时了。
words.en: No longer fashionable or in vogue; out of date.

words.ex: He remained passive during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持被动。
words.en: Accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

words.tr: n. 模仿作品；风格拼凑的艺术作品
words.ex: The movie is a pastiche of various genres.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是各种类型的混成曲。
words.en: A pastiche is a work of art, literature, or music that imitates the style of someone else's work or is a mixture of different styles.

words.ex: The pastoral man tends his sheep on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧人在山上照看他的羊。
words.en: Relating to the countryside or to the work of a shepherd; idyllically rural.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.tr: adj. 病理学的；病理的；病态的
words.ex: The doctor found a pathological change in the tissue.
words.ex_cn: 医生在组织中发现了一种病理性的变化。
words.en: Pathological means relating to pathology, which is the study of diseases, or it can describe a behavior or condition that is extreme and not normal, often in a way that is harmful or undesirable.

words.tr: n. 怜悯；悲情；哀婉；凄楚
words.ex: The movie filled us with pathos.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让我们充满感动。
words.en: Pathos is a quality in a work of art or literature that evokes feelings of pity or sadness.

words.tr: n. 铜绿锈；（金属表面的）绿锈；（旧木器等表面）年久而产生的光泽；（有点儿…的）样子
words.ex: The patina on the old bronze statue added to its charm.
words.ex_cn: 旧青铜雕像上的铜绿增添了它的魅力。
words.en: A patina is a thin layer that forms on the surface of something, especially metal, often as a result of age or exposure to the air, and that is usually green or brown.

words.tr: n. 方言，土语；行话；（Patois）帕图瓦（人名）
words.ex: The villagers spoke a patois that was difficult to understand.
words.ex_cn: 村民们说一种难以理解的方言。
words.en: A patois is a form of language that is considered nonstandard, although it is sometimes used in literature and in the theater, and is often used in informal speech.

words.ex: The patriarch leads his large family with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 这位族长以智慧领导他的大家庭。
words.en: A patriarch is a man who is the head of a family or tribe, or a highly respected man in a particular field.

words.tr:
n. （古罗马的）贵族；名门望族；有教养的人；罗马帝国的地方官
adj. 贵族的；贵族似的；上流社会的
words.ex: She was born into a patrician family.
words.ex_cn: 她出生在一个贵族家庭。
words.en: A patrician is a person of high birth or noble status, especially in ancient Rome.

words.tr: v. 惠顾；资助；屈尊俯就
words.ex: He often patronizes the local bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他经常光顾这家本地面包店。
words.en: If someone patronizes you, they speak or behave towards you in a way which seems friendly, but which shows that they think they are superior to you in some way.

words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.ex: The pauper lived in a small hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个穷人住在一间小屋里。
words.en: A pauper is someone who is extremely poor and has very little money or possessions.

words.ex: He committed a peccadillo by arriving a few minutes late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到几分钟而犯了一个小错误。
words.en: A peccadillo is a small, unimportant fault or sin.

words.ex: He lost his pecuniary support after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了经济支持。
words.en: Pecuniary means relating to money, especially in terms of financial gain or loss.

words.tr: n. 施教者；好为人师的人；卖弄学问者
words.ex: The pedagogue taught children to read and write.
words.ex_cn: 这位教师教孩子们读书写字。
words.en: A pedagogue is a teacher, especially one who is strict or old-fashioned in their methods.

words.ex: The teacher learned new pedagogy from the workshop.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师从研讨会中学到了新的教学法。
words.en: The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept.

words.tr: n. 迂腐之人；书呆子；学究
words.ex: He is a pedant who corrects every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑剔的书呆子，会纠正每一个小错误。
words.en: A pedant is a person who is excessively concerned with minor details and rules or with displaying academic learning.

words.ex: He gave a pedantic answer about grammar rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对语法规则给出了一个迂腐的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as pedantic, you mean that they are too concerned with unimportant details or traditional rules, especially in connection with academic subjects.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: The pediatrician checks the child's health every month.
words.ex_cn: 儿科医生每个月检查孩子的健康状况。
words.en: A pediatrician is a doctor who specializes in the care of children and their diseases.

words.tr: adj. 无可匹敌的；盖世无双的
words.ex: Her singing is peerless.
words.ex_cn: 她的歌唱无人能及。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peerless, you mean that they are better than any other person or thing of the same type.

words.tr:
adj. 贬损的；轻蔑的
n. 贬损语
words.ex: He used a pejorative word to describe his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个贬义词来描述他的邻居。
words.en: A pejorative word or expression is one that expresses criticism or disapproval.

words.tr:
adj.  胡乱的；匆忙的
adv. 乱糟糟地；匆忙地
words.ex: The students rushed pell-mell into the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 学生们慌乱地冲进教室。
words.en: If people move or act pell-mell, they move or act in a hurried, disorganized way, often because they are excited or frightened.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；易懂的
words.ex: The water in the mountain stream was so pellucid that we could see the fish swimming.
words.ex_cn: 山间溪流中的水如此清澈，我们可以看到鱼儿在游动。
words.en: If something is pellucid, it is very clear and easy to understand.

words.tr:
n. （赎罪的）苦行；苦修；忏悔
v. 使...以苦行赎罪
words.ex: He performed penance for his sins.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的罪行忏悔。
words.en: Penance is the act of doing something to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done, especially in some religions.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.tr:
n. 垂饰；悬挂物
adj. 吊着的；悬垂的；悬而未决的
words.ex: She wears a silver pendant around her neck.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条银色吊坠在脖子上。
words.en: A pendant is a piece of jewelry that hangs from a chain worn around the neck.

words.tr: adj. 松垂的；悬垂摆动的
words.ex: The pendulous branches swayed in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 垂下的枝条在风中摇曳。
words.en: Something that is pendulous hangs or swings freely.

words.tr:
adj. 忏悔的；悔过的
n. 忏悔者；悔罪者
words.ex: He sat in the church, a penitent man seeking forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在教堂里，一个忏悔的人寻求宽恕。
words.en: Feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong; repentant.

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.ex: The penumbra of the eclipse was visible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 日食的半影可以用肉眼看到。
words.en: The partially shaded outer region of the shadow cast by an opaque object.

words.ex: He lives in penury after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Penury is the state of being extremely poor.

words.tr: n. 日工；劳工；雇农；被强制劳役以还债的工人; n. （Peon）人名；（俄、葡）佩翁
words.ex: The peon worked long hours in the fields.
words.ex_cn: 这名劳工在田里长时间工作。
words.en: A peon is a person who does hard physical work, especially in a job that does not require much skill and is not well paid.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.ex: He plays the drum, a type of percussion.
words.ex_cn: 他演奏鼓，一种打击乐器。
words.en: Percussion refers to musical instruments that are played by being struck or shaken, such as drums, cymbals, or tambourines. It can also refer to the act of striking or hitting something.

words.ex: He feared perdition for his wicked deeds.
words.ex_cn: 他因自己的恶行而害怕堕入地狱。
words.en: Perdition is a state of eternal punishment and damnation into which a sinful and unrepentant person is believed to pass after death.

words.ex: His peregrinations through Europe were filled with adventure and discovery.
words.ex_cn: 他在欧洲的游历充满了冒险和发现。
words.en: A long journey, especially one made on foot.

words.tr: adj. 断然的；不容置辩的；专横的
words.ex: He gave a peremptory order to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他下达了一个不容置疑的离开命令。
words.en: If someone's manner or behavior is peremptory, they are so confident and sure of their authority that they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.ex: The machine can perforate the paper quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器可以快速地在纸上打孔。
words.en: To make a hole or holes through something, especially by piercing or drilling.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something that is done as perfunctory, you mean that it is done as a duty or a formality, without much care or interest.

words.ex: The satellite is at perigee today.
words.ex_cn: 今天卫星处于近地点。
words.en: The point in the orbit of the moon or a satellite at which it is nearest to the earth.

words.ex: The fence marks the perimeter of the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏标出了花园的边界。
words.en: The perimeter of an area or object is the total length of its sides or outer boundary.

words.tr: adj. 巡游的；到处走的；兼职的
words.ex: He is a peripatetic teacher who moves from town to town.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位四处奔波的老师，从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: If you have a peripatetic job or way of life, you travel around a lot, living or working in different places for short periods of time.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.ex: The small village lies on the periphery of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄位于城市的外围。
words.en: The outer limits or edge of an area or object.

words.ex: He was charged with perjury after lying in court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后被控伪证罪。
words.en: The crime of telling a lie in a court of law after having sworn to tell the truth.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr: n. 结尾；总结；冗长乏味的演说
words.ex: The speaker's peroration was filled with grandiose promises.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者的结束语充满了夸张的承诺。
words.en: The concluding part of a speech, typically intended to inspire enthusiasm in the audience.

words.ex: He was arrested for perpetrating a fraud.
words.ex_cn: 他因实施诈骗而被逮捕。
words.en: If someone perpetrates a crime or any other immoral or harmful act, they do it.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr: adj. 风度好的；个性或外表宜人的；英俊的；貌美的；有魅力的
words.ex: He was a personable young man, always ready to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品貌兼优的年轻人，总是乐于助人。
words.en: If you describe someone as personable, you mean that they are pleasant and attractive in appearance and character.

words.tr: adj. 颖悟的；敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perspicacious and notices small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 她很敏锐，能注意到细小的错误。
words.en: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things.

words.tr: n. （文章语言表达等的）明晰；简明
words.ex: The perspicuity of her writing made it easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 她写作的明晰性使得文章易于理解。
words.en: The quality of being clear and easy to understand.

words.tr: adj. 明白易懂的；表达清楚的
words.ex: The instructions were written in a perspicuous manner.
words.ex_cn: 说明书写得清晰易懂。
words.en: If you describe something such as an argument or explanation as perspicuous, you mean that it is clear and easy to understand.

words.tr: adj. 别致的；时髦的；小巧玲珑的；活泼的；无礼的；唐突的
words.ex: She gave a pert reply to the interviewer's question.
words.ex_cn: 她对采访者的问题给出了无礼的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as pert, you mean that they are lively and confident, and perhaps slightly disrespectful.

words.ex: He is pertinacious about finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is pertinacious continues trying to do something in a very determined way, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.tr: v. 使焦虑；使不安；扰乱
words.ex: The noise perturbs the baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让婴儿不安。
words.en: If something perturbs you, it makes you feel anxious or worried.

words.ex: He peruses the newspaper every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上浏览报纸。
words.en: To read or examine something carefully or thoroughly.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；任性的；乖张的；故意作对的；悖理的
words.ex: He gave a perverse answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个反常的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as perverse, you mean that they deliberately behave in an unreasonable way, especially by doing the opposite of what is expected or wanted.

words.tr: n. 颠倒；歪曲；堕落；性欲倒错；（性）变态
words.ex: The perversion of justice led to widespread public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 司法的颠倒导致了公众的广泛愤怒。
words.en: A perversion of something is a change to it that makes it unnatural, wrong, or unacceptable.

words.ex: His pessimism made him expect the worst.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲观主义让他总是预期最坏的结果。
words.en: Pessimism is the belief that bad things are going to happen or that something is going to turn out badly.

words.tr: adj. 致死的；有害的；传染的
words.ex: The pestilential conditions in the refugee camp led to a rapid spread of disease.
words.ex_cn: 难民营中引起瘟疫的条件导致了疾病的迅速传播。
words.en: Pestilential is used to describe something that is harmful or destructive, especially in a way that is difficult to control or stop.

words.tr:
n. 杵；碾槌
v. 用槌磨；用杵捣
words.ex: She used a pestle to grind the herbs into a fine powder.
words.ex_cn: 她用杵把草药捣成细粉。
words.en: A pestle is a heavy tool with a rounded end, used for crushing and grinding substances such as spices or drugs, usually in a mortar.

words.tr: v. 使石化；使僵化；吓呆
words.ex: The lightning petrified the tree into stone.
words.ex_cn: 闪电把树变成了石头。
words.en: To petrify means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.

words.tr: adj. 琐碎的；微不足道的；心胸狭窄的
words.ex: He got angry over a petty mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个微不足道的错误生气了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.

words.ex: The child's petulant behavior was a result of his frustration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子暴躁的行为是因他的沮丧所致。
words.en: If you describe someone as petulant, you mean that they get angry or annoyed in a childish or unreasonable way.

words.tr: adj. 伪善的；遵守表面虚礼的
words.ex: His pharisaical attitude towards others was deeply resented.
words.ex_cn: 他对别人的伪善态度令人深恶痛绝。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as pharisaical, you are criticizing them for being hypocritical and self-righteous.

words.ex: His physiological response to stress is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 他对压力的生理反应非常强烈。
words.en: Physiological refers to the normal functions of living organisms and their parts, or to the branch of biology that deals with these functions.

words.ex: The piebald horse trotted gracefully across the meadow.
words.ex_cn: 那匹花斑马优雅地小跑穿过草地。
words.en: A piebald animal has patches of black and white on it.

words.tr:
adj. 零碎的；
adv. 零碎地；
words.ex: He fixed the car piecemeal, one part at a time.
words.ex_cn: 他一点一点地修理汽车，一次修一个零件。
words.en: If you describe a change or process as piecemeal, you disapprove of it because it happens gradually, usually at irregular intervals, and is probably not satisfactory.

words.ex: The pied butterfly fluttered among the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 那只杂色蝴蝶在花丛中翩翩起舞。
words.en: Having patches of two or more colors, typically black and white.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.ex: The pigment in leaves changes color in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 叶子中的色素在秋天会变色。
words.en: A pigment is a substance that gives something a particular color.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺；抢劫；掠夺物
v. 抢劫；掠夺
words.ex: The soldiers committed pillage after winning the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在赢得战斗后进行了掠夺。
words.en: If a group of people pillage a place, they steal a lot of things from it and often cause a lot of damage, especially in a war.

words.tr:
n. 颈手枷
v. 给…上颈手枷；使惹人嘲笑；示众；公开批评
words.ex: The newspaper did not hesitate to pillory the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸毫不犹豫地公开谴责那位腐败的政客。
words.en: A pillory is a wooden framework with holes for the head and hands, in which offenders were formerly locked and exposed to public abuse or ridicule. As a verb, to pillory means to expose someone to public scorn, ridicule, or abuse.

words.ex: The pine grows tall in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 松树在森林里长得很高。
words.en: A pine is a type of evergreen tree which has long thin leaves called needles and produces cones. As a verb, to pine means to feel a deep longing or desire for something or someone.

words.tr:
n. 小齿轮；翼
v. 缚住（双臂）
words.ex: The mechanic replaced the damaged pinion in the gearbox.
words.ex_cn: 机械师更换了变速箱中损坏的小齿轮。
words.en: A pinion is a small gear or the outer part of a bird's wing including the flight feathers.

words.tr:
n. 尖塔；尖顶；尖峰；尖岩石；顶点；顶峰
v. 造小尖塔；把...放在极高处
words.ex: The pinnacle of the church reached high into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔高耸入云。
words.en: The pinnacle of something is the highest point or level that it can reach, especially when it is very good.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；信神的；伪善的
words.ex: He is a pious man who prays every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天祈祷的虔诚的人。
words.en: Someone who is pious is very religious and moral.

words.tr: adj. 开胃的；辛辣的；刺激的；迷人的；兴奋的
words.ex: The sauce has a piquant flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种酱汁味道辛辣可口。
words.en: Something that is piquant is pleasantly strong and sharp in taste or smell.

words.tr:
v. 激怒；使生气；激起
n. 怨恨；愤恨
words.ex: His rude comment piqued her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论激怒了她。
words.en: If something piques your interest or curiosity, it makes you interested or curious.

words.ex: The town is famous for its piscatorial activities.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇以其渔业活动而闻名。
words.en: Relating to fish or fishing.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.tr:
n. （木）髓；（柑橘等）外皮下的海绵层；精髓；核心
v. 除去木髓
words.ex: The pith of the essay is its call for social change.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章的核心是其呼吁社会变革。
words.en: The essential or most vital part of some idea or experience.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；精练的
words.ex: He gave a pithy answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简洁有力的回答。
words.en: A pithy statement or piece of writing is short, clear, and full of meaning.

words.tr: n. 微薄的工资；极少的报酬
words.ex: He lived on a pittance during his early career.
words.ex_cn: 他在职业生涯初期靠微薄的收入生活。
words.en: A very small or inadequate amount of money paid to someone as an allowance or wage.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a placebo to see if his pain would go away.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一个安慰剂，看看他的疼痛是否会消失。
words.en: A substance that has no therapeutic effect, used as a control in testing new drugs, or given for its psychological effect to a patient who believes it to be a medicine.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；温和的；
words.ex: The lake was placid in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的阳光下，湖面平静无波。
words.en: A placid person or animal is calm and does not easily become excited, angry, or upset.

words.ex: He plagiarized the essay from the internet.
words.ex_cn: 他从网上抄袭了这篇论文。
words.en: To plagiarize means to use someone else's ideas or work and pretend that it is your own.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.tr: adj. 柏拉图式的（指不含性爱）
words.ex: They had a platonic relationship, with no romantic involvement.
words.ex_cn: 他们的关系是纯精神的，没有任何浪漫的牵扯。
words.en: Platonic describes a relationship or love that is intimate and affectionate but not sexual.

words.ex: The actor received a plaudit for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而获得赞誉。
words.en: Plaudit refers to an expression of praise or approval, often given in the form of applause or enthusiastic commendation.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.tr:
adj. 平民的；粗俗的
n. 平民；下层人；老百姓
words.ex: The speech was criticized for its plebeian language.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲因其粗俗的语言而受到批评。
words.en: A plebeian is a member of the general populace, especially one of the common people of ancient Rome. As an adjective, it describes something that is common, ordinary, or vulgar.

words.tr:
adj. 全体参加的；无限的；完全的
n. 全会；全体会议
words.ex: The plenary session started at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 全体会议在上午九点开始。
words.en: A plenary session or meeting is one that is attended by everyone who has the right to attend.

words.ex: The garden was in a state of plenitude, with flowers blooming everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 花园里繁花似锦，处处充满生机。
words.en: The state of being full or complete; abundance.

words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.ex: The willow branch is pliant and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 柳枝柔软，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliant person or thing is easily influenced or controlled by others.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.tr:
v. 摘；拔；猛拉；拨弹
n. 胆识；胆量；快而猛地拉
words.ex: He plucked a flower from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他从花园里摘了一朵花。
words.en: To pluck means to pull something quickly to remove it or to play a musical instrument by pulling the strings with your fingers. As a noun, it refers to the quality of being brave and determined.

words.ex: The bird's plumage was a vibrant mix of colors.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟的羽毛色彩鲜艳。
words.en: The feathers covering the body of a bird.

words.ex: The builder used a plumb to check if the wall was straight.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工人用铅锤检查墙是否垂直。
words.en: To measure the depth of water with a plumb line; to explore or understand something deeply; exactly vertical; completely or directly.

words.ex: The apple plummeted from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上垂直落下。
words.en: If an amount, rate, or price plummets, it decreases quickly by a large amount.

words.tr: n. 富豪；财阀；财阀政治；富豪统治
words.ex: The country is often criticized for being a plutocracy where wealth determines political power.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经常因为财富决定政治权力的富豪统治而受到批评。
words.en: A plutocracy is a society or system that is ruled or controlled by people of great wealth or income.

words.ex: He visited a podiatrist for his sore feet.
words.ex_cn: 他因为脚疼去看足病医生。
words.en: A podiatrist is a medical professional devoted to the study and medical treatment of disorders of the foot, ankle, and lower extremity.

words.ex: He stood on the podium to receive the gold medal.
words.ex_cn: 他站在领奖台上领取金牌。
words.en: A podium is a small platform on which someone stands to give a speech or conduct an orchestra, or on which a medal winner stands during a prize-giving ceremony.

words.ex: The poignancy of the moment was not lost on anyone.
words.ex_cn: 那一刻的辛酸没有被任何人忽略。
words.en: The quality of evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret.

words.ex: The issue polarized the community into two opposing groups.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题使社区分裂成了两个对立的群体。
words.en: To polarize means to cause something, especially a group or an issue, to divide into two sharply contrasting groups or sets of opinions or beliefs.

words.ex: His article was a polemic against government corruption.
words.ex_cn: 他的文章是对政府腐败的抨击。
words.en: A polemic is a very strong written or spoken attack on, or defence of, a particular belief or opinion.

words.tr: adj. 辩论的；引起争论的；争议的
words.ex: His polemical article sparked strong debates.
words.ex_cn: 他那篇有争议的文章引发了激烈争论。
words.en: A polemical piece of writing or speech is one that strongly argues against or in favor of a particular opinion, person, or idea, often in a way that is intended to provoke controversy.

words.tr: adj. 有智虑的；精明的；有策略的
words.ex: It was politic to stay silent during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 在会议上保持沉默是明智的。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as politic, you mean that it is sensible and likely to achieve what you want.

words.tr: n. 政体；国体；有组织的社会团体
words.ex: The small island has a stable polity.
words.ex_cn: 这个小岛有一个稳定的政体。
words.en: A polity is a society or country considered as a political entity, or the form of government or constitution of such an entity.

words.tr: n. 多配偶论者；多配偶的人
words.ex: The polygamist lifestyle is often misunderstood by those outside the community.
words.ex_cn: 多配偶的生活方式常常被社区外的人误解。
words.en: A polygamist is a person who practices polygamy; that is, having more than one spouse at the same time.

words.tr:
adj. 多种语言的；通晓数种语言的
n. 通晓数种语言的人
words.ex: He is a polyglot who speaks five languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位会说五种语言的多语者。
words.en: A polyglot is a person who knows and is able to use several languages.

words.tr: n.  浮华；虚夸；炫耀；自负
words.ex: His pomposity often alienated his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的自大使他经常疏远同事。
words.en: Pomposity is the quality of being pompous; self-importance.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；笨重的；沉闷的
words.ex: He carried a ponderous box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他搬着一个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: Something that is ponderous is very heavy or is very slow and clumsy because of its weight or size.

words.tr: adj. 教皇的；武断的；傲慢的
words.ex: He wore a pontifical robe during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上穿了一件教皇式的长袍。
words.en: Relating to the Pope or to the office or authority of the Pope; having the pomp or dignity associated with high ecclesiastical office.

words.tr:
n. 毛孔；小孔
v. 细看；钻研；凝视
words.ex: Sweat comes out through the pores of the skin.
words.ex_cn: 汗水通过皮肤上的毛孔排出。
words.en: A pore is a tiny opening in a surface that allows liquids or gases to pass through. As a verb, to pore means to read or study something very carefully.

words.ex: The sponge is porous and absorbs water easily.
words.ex_cn: 海绵是多孔的，容易吸水。
words.en: If something is porous, it has a lot of tiny holes in it that allow water or air to pass through slowly.

words.ex: Dark clouds portend a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something portends something else, it indicates that it is likely to happen in the future.

words.tr: n. 异兆；凶兆；不祥之兆
words.ex: The dark clouds were a portent of the coming storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是即将到来的风暴的前兆。
words.en: A portent is an event or sign that is considered to indicate what is going to happen in the future, especially something very good or very bad.

words.ex: The portly man walks slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位胖胖的男人拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: If you describe someone as portly, you mean that they are fat in a dignified way.

words.tr: n. 装模作样的人；装腔作势的人
words.ex: He was always seen as a poseur, trying too hard to fit in with the cool crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他总是被视为一个装模作样的人，过于努力地想融入酷酷的群体。
words.en: A poseur is someone who behaves in an artificial way in order to impress other people.

words.ex: He wrote the book for posterity.
words.ex_cn: 他写这本书是为了留给后人。
words.en: All future generations of people.

words.tr: adj. 死后的；死后出版的；遗腹的
words.ex: He received a posthumous award for his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢而被追授了奖项。
words.en: Posthumous means occurring, awarded, or appearing after the death of the originator.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.tr: adj. 可饮用的；适于饮用的
words.ex: The water is potable.
words.ex_cn: 这水可以饮用。
words.en: Potable water is safe to drink.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.ex: The potentate ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 这位统治者以铁腕统治。
words.en: A potentate is a ruler who has great power, especially one who rules over a large area or empire.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.ex: The witch stirred a magic potion.
words.ex_cn: 女巫搅拌了一瓶魔药。
words.en: A potion is a liquid that is believed to have magical or medicinal properties.

words.tr: n. 百花香；混杂物；集锦
words.ex: The book is a potpourri of various literary styles.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是各种文学风格的混合体。
words.en: A potpourri is a mixture of dried petals and leaves from various flowers and plants that is used to make a room smell pleasant. It can also refer to a mixture of things, especially musical or literary pieces, that are varied and not connected with each other.

words.ex: The doctor recommended applying a poultice to the wound.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议在伤口上敷膏药。
words.en: A poultice is a soft, moist mass of material, typically of plant origin, applied to the body to relieve soreness and inflammation and kept in place with a cloth.

words.ex: This plan is practicable.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的。
words.en: If a task, plan, or idea is practicable, it can be successfully done or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；实际的；实践的；
words.ex: This tool is practical for everyday use.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具日常使用很实用。
words.en: relating to what is real rather than to what is possible or imagined; likely to succeed or be effective in real circumstances; involving or concerned with experience or actual use; not theoretical

words.tr: adj. 务实的；实事求是的；
words.ex: He took a pragmatic approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他采取了务实的方法来解决问题。
words.en: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.

words.ex: He is a pragmatist who solves problems with real solutions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个注重实际解决方案的实用主义者。
words.en: A pragmatist is someone who is pragmatic, that is, someone who is practical and focused on reaching a goal. Pragmatists are results-oriented and often have a no-nonsense approach to solving problems.

words.tr:
v. 胡扯；唠叨；喋喋不休
n. 唠叨；喋喋不休
words.ex: He likes to prate about his trips.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢喋喋不休地谈论他的旅行。
words.en: To talk excessively and pointlessly; chatter.

words.tr:
v. 说孩子气的话；说半截话；闲扯；多嘴多舌
n. 孩子般颠三倒四的话；连续而无意义的声音；废话
words.ex: She prattled on about her new dress.
words.ex_cn: 她喋喋不休地谈论她的新裙子。
words.en: If someone prattles on about something, they talk for a long time in a boring or silly way because they keep talking about unimportant things.

words.ex: The preamble explains the purpose of the law.
words.ex_cn: 序言解释了法律的目的。
words.en: A preamble is an introduction to a speech or piece of writing, especially one that explains what follows.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.ex: The court followed the precedent set in 1995.
words.ex_cn: 法院遵循了1995年确立的先例。
words.en: A precedent is an action or decision that is used as an example when someone wants to do a similar thing in the future.

words.tr: n. (尤指道德方面的)戒律；准则
words.ex: He follows the precept to be kind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循要善良的教诲。
words.en: A precept is a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought.

words.ex: The hiker stood at the precipice, afraid to move.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者站在悬崖边，不敢动。
words.en: A very steep or overhanging place on a cliff or mountain; a situation of great peril.

words.ex: Her precipitant decision led to many regrets later.
words.ex_cn: 她轻率的决定导致了后来的许多遗憾。
words.en: A precipitant action or decision is done without careful consideration, often leading to sudden or unexpected results.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.ex: The car took a precipitous turn on the mountain road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在山路上急转弯。
words.en: A precipitous slope or cliff is very steep and often dangerous.

words.tr:
n. 摘要；大纲
v. 为…写摘要；概括…的大意
words.ex: He wrote a précis of the long report for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他为会议写了一份长报告的摘要。
words.en: A précis is a short summary of a larger work, capturing the main points and essence of the original material.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.tr: n. 掠夺者；捕食性动物；食肉动物；
words.ex: The lion is a predator that hunts deer.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种捕食鹿的掠夺者。
words.en: A predator is an animal that naturally preys on others.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.ex: He predetermines the outcome before the game starts.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛开始前就决定了结果。
words.en: To decide or settle (something) in advance.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.tr: v. 使预先有倾向；使易接受；使易于患（病）
words.ex: Genes can predispose a person to diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 基因可能使人更容易患糖尿病。
words.en: If something predisposes you to think or behave in a particular way, it makes it likely that you will think or behave in that way.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.ex: The company preempted its rivals by launching the product early.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司通过提前推出产品抢先行动。
words.en: To preempt something means to do or say something before someone else does, especially to prevent them from doing or saying it.

words.tr: v. 用喙整理羽毛；精心打扮；感觉良好
words.ex: The bird preens its feathers every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟每天早上梳理它的羽毛。
words.en: If a bird preens or preens itself, it cleans and arranges its feathers using its beak.

words.ex: The book begins with a prefatory note from the author.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以作者的前言开始。
words.en: Serving as an introduction or preface; introductory.

words.tr: adj. 可盘卷的；能抓住的；有理解能力的；贪婪的
words.ex: The monkey has a prehensile tail to grab trees.
words.ex_cn: 这只猴子有一条能抓握的尾巴来抓住树木。
words.en: A prehensile tail or limb is adapted for grasping or holding.

words.tr: n. .高级教士；职位甚高的教士
words.ex: The prelate delivered a sermon on the importance of charity.
words.ex_cn: 这位高级教士在布道中讲述了慈善的重要性。
words.en: A prelate is a high-ranking member of the clergy, such as a bishop, who has authority over other clergy and often over a specific area.

words.ex: The quiet music was a prelude to the loud concert.
words.ex_cn: 轻柔的音乐是盛大音乐会的前奏。
words.en: A prelude is an introductory piece of music, event, or action that comes before a more important one.

words.ex: He did not premeditate the crime; it happened in the moment.
words.ex_cn: 他没有预谋犯罪；那是当场发生的。
words.en: If you premeditate an action, especially a crime, you plan it or think about it before you do it.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.ex: She had a premonition that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A premonition is a feeling that something, especially something unpleasant, is going to happen.

words.ex: She had a premonitory feeling that something bad was about to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得有不好的事情即将发生。
words.en: Serving as a warning or indication of a future event.

words.ex: The preponderance of evidence shows he is guilty.
words.ex_cn: 大多数证据表明他有罪。
words.en: If there is a preponderance of one type of thing or person in a group, there are more of that type than of any other.

words.ex: It's preposterous to think cats can drive cars.
words.ex_cn: 认为猫会开车是极其荒谬的。
words.en: If you describe something as preposterous, you mean that it is extremely unreasonable and foolish.

words.ex: It is the president's prerogative to make final decisions.
words.ex_cn: 做最终决定是总统的特权。
words.en: A prerogative is a right or privilege exclusive to a particular individual or class.

words.tr:
n. 预示；前兆；预感
v. 预示；预兆
words.ex: The dark clouds presage a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something presages a situation or event, it is considered to be a warning or sign of what is about to happen.

words.ex: He showed prescience by predicting the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他通过预测风暴展现了先见之明。
words.en: The ability to know or predict what will happen in the future.

words.ex: She had a presentiment that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A presentiment is a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.tr: adj. 放肆的；冒昧的；自以为是的
words.ex: He was presumptuous to ask for a raise after just one week.
words.ex_cn: 他才工作一周就要求加薪，太自以为是了。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as presumptuous, you disapprove of them because they are doing something that they have no right or authority to do.

words.tr: adj. 自命不凡的；自负的；矫饰的
words.ex: He wore a fancy hat to seem pretentious.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶华丽的帽子，显得自命不凡。
words.en: If you describe something as pretentious, you mean that it is intended to seem important or significant, but you think it is not.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；超自然的；难以解释的
words.ex: The psychic claimed to have preternatural abilities.
words.ex_cn: 这位通灵者声称自己拥有超自然的能力。
words.en: Beyond what is normal or natural; supernatural.

words.ex: He used a pretext to leave the meeting early.
words.ex_cn: 他找了个借口提前离开了会议。
words.en: A pretext is a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.ex: He prevaricates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他回避回答。
words.en: If you prevaricate, you avoid giving a direct answer or making a firm decision.

words.tr:
n. 猎物；受害者；受骗者；
v. 捕食；坑害；折磨；
words.ex: The lion chased its prey across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在平原上追逐它的猎物。
words.en: An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.tr: n. 长子身份；长子继承权
words.ex: In many historical societies, primogeniture dictated that the eldest son would inherit the family estate.
words.ex_cn: 在许多历史社会中，长子继承权规定长子将继承家族的地产。
words.en: The system by which the eldest son in a family inherits all his parents' property.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；远古的；最初的
words.ex: The primordial soup formed the first life on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 原始汤形成了地球上的最初生命。
words.en: Primordial means existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval.

words.tr: v. 打扮；装饰；精心打扮
words.ex: She spent hours primping before the big event.
words.ex_cn: 她在重大活动前花了几个小时精心打扮。
words.en: To spend time making small adjustments to one's appearance, especially in front of a mirror.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.ex: The family endured years of privation during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭在战争期间经历了多年的贫困。
words.en: Privation is a situation in which you do not have the things that are essential for a comfortable life, such as enough food, clothing, or shelter.

words.tr: adj. 私下参与的；私下的；秘密的
words.ex: He is privy to the secret plan.
words.ex_cn: 他知道这个秘密计划。
words.en: If you are privy to something secret, you have been allowed to know about it.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.ex: The new policy is problematic for small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对小企业来说成问题。
words.en: If something is problematic, it involves problems and is difficult to deal with or solve.

words.ex: He has a proclivity for solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有解决数学问题的倾向。
words.en: A proclivity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way or to like a particular thing.

words.ex: He always procrastinates doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他总是拖延做作业。
words.en: If you procrastinate, you keep leaving things you should do until later, often because you do not want to do them.

words.tr: n. （为军队或其他组织的）采购
words.ex: The army's procurement of food and fuel takes months.
words.ex_cn: 军队的食品和燃料采购需要数月时间。
words.en: Procurement is the act of obtaining or buying goods and services, often for a business or government.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；激励；督促
n. 戳；刺；催促
words.ex: He prodded the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke or jab someone or something, often with a finger or a pointed object, in order to get their attention or to encourage them to do something.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.ex: The boy is a piano prodigy at age six.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩六岁时就是一位钢琴奇才。
words.en: A prodigy is someone who is unusually young and has a great natural ability in a particular area.

words.tr:
adj. 亵渎的；不敬神的；世俗的
v. 亵渎神灵；亵圣
words.ex: He used profane words during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵中说了脏话。
words.en: If someone uses profane language, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, especially because it refers to sex or other bodily functions in a way that is considered inappropriate.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍无度的；行为不检点的；放荡的
n. 放荡的人；恣意挥霍的人
words.ex: His profligate lifestyle led to his financial ruin.
words.ex_cn: 他放荡的生活方式导致了他经济上的破产。
words.en: Someone who is profligate spends too much money or uses too much of something.

words.ex: His words had a profound effect on her life.
words.ex_cn: 他的话对她的生活产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe something as profound, you mean that it is very great or intense.

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.ex: The ancient hunter is the progenitor of our family.
words.ex_cn: 这位古代猎人是我们家族的祖先。
words.en: A progenitor is a direct ancestor of someone or the originator of a particular idea or movement.

words.ex: The old tree produced many progeny.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树生了许多后代。
words.en: The offspring or descendants considered as a group.

words.tr: n. 预断病情；预后；预测
words.ex: The prognosis for patients with this disease is generally poor.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病的患者预后通常不佳。
words.en: A prognosis is an estimate of the future course and outcome of a disease, especially of the chances of recovery.

words.ex: He tries to prognosticate the weather tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他试图预测明天的天气。
words.en: To prognosticate means to foretell or predict something based on present signs or symptoms.

words.ex: The price of the phone is prohibitive for most students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了。
words.en: If the cost of something is prohibitive, it is so high that it prevents people from buying it or doing it.

words.tr:
n. 抛射物；射弹；发射物；自动推进武器
adj. 发射的；射弹的；推进的
words.ex: The boy threw a projectile into the air.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把一个抛射物扔向空中。
words.en: A projectile is an object that is thrown or shot forwards, such as a bullet fired from a gun.

words.tr: adj. 无产阶级的；n. 无产者
words.ex: The proletarian worked long hours in the factory.
words.ex_cn: 普罗在工厂里长时间工作。
words.en: A proletarian is a member of the proletariat, the class of wage-earners in a capitalist society whose only possession of significant material value is their labor-power.

words.ex: Rabbits proliferate quickly in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在野外繁殖得很快。
words.en: If something proliferates, it increases in number or spreads quickly.

words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.ex: The judge criticized the lawyer for his prolixity in the court.
words.ex_cn: 法官批评了律师在法庭上的冗长发言。
words.en: Prolixity refers to the use of too many words to express an idea, making speech or writing tediously lengthy.

words.ex: The book begins with a short prologue.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一个简短的序言开始。
words.en: A prologue is an introduction to a book, play, or other written work that sets the scene or provides background information.

words.ex: They decided to prolong the meeting by one hour.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定将会议延长一小时。
words.en: To prolong something means to make it last longer.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: adj. 淫乱的；滥交的；杂乱的
words.ex: He was criticized for his promiscuous behavior.
words.ex_cn: 他因淫乱的行为而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe someone as promiscuous, you disapprove of them because they have sexual relationships with many people. In a more general sense, promiscuous can describe something that is not selective or is mixed without order.

words.ex: The lighthouse stands on a promontory overlooking the sea.
words.ex_cn: 灯塔建在俯瞰大海的岬角上。
words.en: A promontory is a high point of land or rock projecting into a body of water; a headland.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.ex: The virus can propagate quickly among people.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以在人群中迅速传播。
words.en: To propagate something means to spread it and encourage more people to believe in it or support it.

words.tr: n. 推进剂；发射药；火箭燃料
words.ex: The rocket uses a strong propellant to fly.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用一种强大的推进剂来飞行。
words.en: A propellant is a substance that is used to move something forward, especially a rocket or a bullet, by creating a force that pushes it.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.tr: adj. 预言的；预示的；先知的
words.ex: His words were prophetic when the storm came.
words.ex_cn: 当风暴来临时，他的话应验了。
words.en: If something was prophetic, it described or suggested something that did actually happen later.

words.tr:
adj. 预防性的
n. 预防剂；避孕用品
words.ex: He took a prophylactic pill before traveling.
words.ex_cn: 他旅行前吃了一颗预防药。
words.en: A prophylactic is a measure taken to prevent disease or another unwanted outcome.

words.tr: n. 邻近；接近；（血统上的）近亲
words.ex: The propinquity of the two houses made it easy to visit.
words.ex_cn: 这两所房子的邻近使拜访变得容易。
words.en: Propinquity refers to the state of being close to someone or something, either in a physical sense or in terms of a relationship.

words.tr: v. 劝慰；使息怒；谋求好感
words.ex: He brought flowers to propitiate his angry wife.
words.ex_cn: 他带了花去劝慰他生气的妻子。
words.en: To propitiate someone means to make them less angry or hostile by doing something to please them.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.tr: v. 提出；提议；提出…供考虑
words.ex: He propound a new theory in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上提出了一种新理论。
words.en: To propound means to suggest or put forward an idea, theory, or point of view for consideration.

words.ex: He always follows social propriety.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵守社交礼仪。
words.en: Propriety is the quality of being proper, suitable, or appropriate in behavior or conduct.

words.ex: The rocket has a propulsive engine.
words.ex_cn: 这枚火箭有一个推进引擎。
words.en: Relating to or capable of propelling or driving forward.

words.tr: adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；平淡无奇的
words.ex: His prosaic speech bored everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他平淡无奇的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as prosaic, you mean that it is ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.ex: The actors stood on the proscenium to begin the play.
words.ex_cn: 演员们站在台口开始演出。
words.en: The part of a theater stage in front of the curtain.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.tr: v. 使改变宗教（或政治）信仰
words.ex: He tries to proselytize his friends about his new religion.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让他的朋友信奉他的新宗教。
words.en: To proselytize means to try to persuade someone to change their religious or political beliefs or way of living to your own.

words.tr: n. 韵律学；作诗法；诗体学
words.ex: He studied the prosody of ancient poems.
words.ex_cn: 他研究了古代诗歌的韵律。
words.en: Prosody is the patterns of rhythm and sound used in poetry.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.tr:
adj. 俯卧的；平卧的；给（悲伤等）压倒的
v. 使俯伏；使拜倒
words.ex: He fell prostrate on the ground after the race.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，他瘫倒在了地上。
words.en: If you prostrate yourself, you lie down flat on the ground, usually in front of someone, as a way of showing respect or submission. It can also mean to be extremely tired or emotionally drained.

words.tr: adj. 变化多端的；千变万化的
words.ex: He is protean in his interests, changing often.
words.ex_cn: 他对兴趣变化多端，经常改变。
words.en: Able to change frequently or easily; versatile.

words.ex: The famous artist took her young protege under her wing.
words.ex_cn: 这位著名艺术家收这位年轻后辈为徒。
words.en: A protégé is a person who is guided and supported by an older and more experienced or influential person.

words.ex: The two countries signed a protocol to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项停止战争的协议。
words.en: A protocol is a set of rules or a system of rules about the correct way to act in formal situations.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: He tries to protract the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他试图延长会议。
words.en: To protract something means to make it last longer than usual or necessary, often in a way that is annoying or inconvenient.

words.ex: The nail protrudes from the wood.
words.ex_cn: 钉子从木头里凸出来。
words.en: If something protrudes from somewhere, it sticks out.

words.tr: n. 凸起物；突出部分；结节；瘤
words.ex: The rock has a small protuberance on top.
words.ex_cn: 这块石头顶部有一个小突起。
words.en: A protuberance is a part that sticks out from the surface of something.

words.ex: The provenance of this ancient vase is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个古花瓶的起源未知。
words.en: The place of origin or earliest known history of something.

words.ex: The farmer gives provender to his cows every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上给他的奶牛喂饲料。
words.en: Provender refers to food or provisions, especially dry food for livestock.

words.tr: adj. 有先见之明的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He is a provident man who saves money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有远见的人，会为未来存钱。
words.en: Making provision for the future; exercising foresight or forethought.

words.ex: The provincial government opened a new school.
words.ex_cn: 省政府开设了一所新学校。
words.en: Relating to a province or provinces; having the manners, viewpoints, etc., considered characteristic of unsophisticated inhabitants of a province; narrow-minded.

words.ex: He took a provisional job until he found a better one.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到更好的工作之前做了一份临时工作。
words.en: Something that is provisional is temporary and likely to be changed or replaced in the future.

words.ex: The contract has a proviso that payments must be made on time.
words.ex_cn: 合同中有一项限制条款，要求付款必须按时进行。
words.en: A proviso is a condition or stipulation in a legal document, agreement, or law that must be fulfilled or adhered to.

words.ex: His provocative words made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他挑衅的话让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you describe something as provocative, you mean that it is intended to make people react angrily or argue against it.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.tr: n. 代理人；代表；代理权；代理服务器
words.ex: He gave his friend a proxy to vote for him.
words.ex_cn: 他让朋友当他的代理人替他投票。
words.en: A proxy is a person or thing that is authorized to act on behalf of another, especially in voting or representing someone in a meeting.

words.tr: n. 故作守礼的人；假正经的人
words.ex: She is a prude who won't wear short skirts.
words.ex_cn: 她是个拘谨的人，不愿意穿短裙。
words.en: A prude is a person who is easily shocked by matters relating to sex or nudity.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: She ate a prune for a healthy snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一颗梅干作为健康零食。
words.en: To prune means to cut off some of the branches of a tree or bush to make it grow better. It can also mean to reduce the extent of something by removing superfluous or unwanted parts.

words.ex: The movie had prurient scenes that upset many viewers.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有令人不适的色情场面。
words.en: Having or encouraging an excessive interest in sexual matters.

words.tr:
n. 窥探；杠杆；爱打探的人
v. 打听；窥探；用杠杆撬开
words.ex: His pry into my private messages made me angry.
words.ex_cn: 他窥探我的私信让我很生气。
words.en: To try to find out private information about someone or something in a way that is annoying or rude.

words.ex: He writes books under a pseudonym.
words.ex_cn: 他用笔名写书。
words.en: A pseudonym is a name that someone, especially a writer, uses instead of their real name.

words.ex: The child's psyche was affected by the loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的心灵受到了嘈杂声音的影响。
words.en: The human soul, mind, or spirit.

words.tr: n. 精神病学家；精神科医生
words.ex: He visits a psychiatrist every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周去看一次精神科医生。
words.en: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental illnesses and emotional disorders.

words.ex: The man showed psychopathic behavior toward others.
words.ex_cn: 这个人对他人表现出精神病态的行为。
words.en: Psychopathic refers to someone who behaves in a way that is morally or socially unacceptable and shows no guilt or remorse for their actions. It is often associated with a lack of empathy and manipulative behavior.

words.tr: n. 精神病；精神错乱；思觉失调
words.ex: He showed signs of psychosis after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他表现出精神病的症状。
words.en: A severe mental disorder in which thought and emotions are so impaired that contact is lost with external reality.

words.ex: The boy saw a pterodactyl in the dinosaur book.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在恐龙书中看到了翼手龙。
words.en: A pterodactyl is an extinct flying reptile of the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods, which had a long, pointed beak, a short tail, and a wingspan of up to 12 meters.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: His puerile jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puerile, you mean that they are silly and childish.

words.ex: The pugilist trained every day for the match.
words.ex_cn: 这位拳击手每天都为比赛训练。
words.en: A pugilist is someone who fights with their fists, especially a professional boxer.

words.ex: His pugnacity made him argue with everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的好斗性格让他和每个人争论。
words.en: Pugnacity is the quality of being eager or quick to argue, quarrel, or fight.

words.tr: adj. 强有力的；强盛的；有势力的
words.ex: The puissant ruler commanded respect from all his subjects.
words.ex_cn: 这位强大的统治者赢得了所有臣民的尊敬。
words.en: Having great power or influence; potent.

words.ex: Her pulchritude was the talk of the town.
words.ex_cn: 她的美貌是全镇的话题。
words.en: Physical beauty, especially of a woman.

words.tr: adj. 肺的；肺部的；与肺有关的
words.ex: He has a pulmonary infection.
words.ex_cn: 他患有肺部感染。
words.en: Relating to the lungs.

words.ex: The light pulsates slowly in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 灯在黑暗中缓慢地脉动。
words.en: If something pulsates, it beats, moves in and out, or shakes with strong, regular movements.

words.tr: v. 粉碎；磨成粉；彻底击败；摧毁
words.ex: The machine will pulverize the rocks into dust.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会把岩石碾成粉末。
words.en: To pulverize something means to crush it into a fine powder or to defeat someone or something completely.

words.tr: v. 连续猛击；反复拳打；捶打
words.ex: The boxer pummels his opponent with fast punches.
words.ex_cn: 拳击手用快速的拳击击打他的对手。
words.en: To pummel someone or something means to hit them many times using your fists.

words.tr: adj. 谨小慎微的；一丝不苟的
words.ex: He is punctilious about following every rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对遵守每一条规则都谨小慎微。
words.en: If someone is punctilious, they are very careful to behave correctly and to follow the details of rules or customs.

words.tr: n. 权威人士；专家；评论员
words.ex: The pundit said the team will win tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这位专家说球队明天会赢。
words.en: A pundit is a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is often asked to give their opinions to the public.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.ex: The court imposed a punitive fine for the violation.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这一违规行为处以惩罚性罚款。
words.en: Punitive actions, laws, or measures are intended to punish someone.

words.ex: He is puny and can't lift the box.
words.ex_cn: 他很瘦弱，举不起那个箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puny, you mean that they are small and weak.

words.tr:
n. 购买；采购；
v. 购买；采购；
words.ex: The purchase of a new car took all his savings.
words.ex_cn: 买一辆新车花光了他所有的积蓄。
words.en: To purchase something means to buy it. It can also refer to something that has been bought.

words.tr: n. 炼狱；受难的处所（或状态）；折磨
words.ex: He felt like he was in purgatory while waiting for the results.
words.ex_cn: 他在等待结果时感觉自己身处炼狱。
