words.en: Purgatory is a place or state of suffering inhabited by the souls of sinners who are expiating their sins before going to heaven.

words.tr:
v. 净化；清除；清洗；整肃
n. 净化；清除；泻药
words.ex: The company purged its outdated systems.
words.ex_cn: 公司净化了其过时的系统。
words.en: To purge an organization or place of something or someone means to remove them from it because they are considered undesirable or harmful.

words.tr:
v. 声称；意指；意味着
n. 意义；要旨；主要意思
words.ex: The letter purports to be from the president.
words.ex_cn: 这封信声称是总统写的。
words.en: If something purports to be a particular thing or to do a particular thing, it claims or appears to be that thing or to do that thing, even though this may not be the case.

words.tr:
adj. 据称的；传言的
v. 声称；意指；意味着；“purport”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The purported owner of the car was not the real one.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的所谓主人并不是真正的主人。
words.en: If you say that something purports to be true or to have a particular quality, you mean that it claims to be true or to have that quality, although it may not be.

words.tr: n. 女用小包；钱包；资金；
words.ex: She put her keys in her purse.
words.ex_cn: 她把钥匙放进她的女用小包里。
words.en: A purse is a small bag used especially by women to carry everyday personal items.

words.tr: n. 办伙食者；提供者；供应商；承办商
words.ex: The purveyor brings food to the school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 办伙食者每天早上给学校送饭。
words.en: A purveyor is a person or company that supplies or provides something, especially food or information.

words.ex: His pusillanimous behavior in the face of danger was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前的懦弱行为令人失望。
words.en: If you say that someone is pusillanimous, you mean that they are timid or afraid, especially in a way that you find irritating or disappointing.

words.tr: adj. 推定的；假定的；一般认为的
words.ex: The putative father was asked to take a DNA test.
words.ex_cn: 被推定的父亲被要求做DNA测试。
words.en: Generally believed to be or to exist, but not proved to be so.

words.ex: The putrid meat smelled awful.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂的肉闻起来很臭。
words.en: Something that is putrid has decayed and smells very unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 指示塔；高压电线铁塔
words.ex: The pylon holds up the power lines.
words.ex_cn: 电线杆支撑着输电线路。
words.en: A pylon is a tall structure, especially one that is part of a building or that is used to support something such as a bridge or a road.

words.tr: n. （术语）纵火狂患者；（非正式）爱玩火（或看火）的人
words.ex: He is a pyromaniac who loves setting fires.
words.ex_cn: 他是个纵火狂，喜欢放火。
words.en: A pyromaniac is a person who has an uncontrollable desire to set fire to things.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words Q

words.tr:
n. 嘎嘎叫声；庸医；冒充内行的人
v. 嘎嘎地叫；大声闲谈；冒充内行
words.ex: The duck made a loud quack.
words.ex_cn: 鸭子发出了响亮的嘎嘎叫声。
words.en: A quack is someone who pretends to have medical skills that they do not really possess. It can also refer to the sound a duck makes.

words.tr:
n. 四足动物
adj. 有四足的；四足动物的
words.ex: The dog is a quadruped.
words.ex_cn: 狗是四足动物。
words.en: A quadruped is an animal that walks on four legs.

words.tr: v. 豪饮；痛饮；开怀畅饮
words.ex: He quaffed the cold drink quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝下了那杯冷饮。
words.en: To drink (a beverage) heartily and with gusto.

words.ex: The hikers got stuck in a quagmire near the river.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在河边陷入了一片沼泽地。
words.en: A quagmire is a difficult, complicated, or unpleasant situation that is hard to escape from.

words.tr:
n. 鹌鹑；鹌鹑肉 
v. 畏缩；胆怯
words.ex: The farmer raised quail for their eggs.
words.ex_cn: 农夫饲养鹌鹑来获取它们的蛋。
words.en: If someone quails, they feel or show fear or hesitation.

words.ex: The village has a quaint old church.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄有一座古色古香的古老教堂。
words.en: Something that is quaint is attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的； v. 取得资格；“qualify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a qualified teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有资格的老师。
words.en: Having the necessary qualifications for a particular job or task.

words.tr: n. 不安；良心之谴责；疑虑；“qualm”的复数
words.ex: He had no qualms about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎毫无愧疚。
words.en: If you have no qualms about doing something, you are not worried that it may be wrong in some way.

words.tr: n. 困境；窘境；困惑之境；进退两难
words.ex: He is in a quandary about what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他对于该做什么感到困惑。
words.en: A situation in which you are unsure or confused about what to do.

words.ex: He stayed in quarantine for 14 days.
words.ex_cn: 他隔离了14天。
words.en: A quarantine is a period of time during which an animal or person that might have a disease is kept away from other people or animals so that the disease cannot spread.

words.ex: The workers load stones from the quarry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从采石场装载石头。
words.en: A quarry is a place where stone, sand, etc., is dug out of the ground. It can also refer to an animal or person that is being hunted or chased.

words.ex: The court will quash the false order.
words.ex_cn: 法院将撤销这个虚假的命令。
words.en: If a court or someone in authority quashes a decision or judgment, they officially reject it and say that it is not valid.

words.ex: The boat docked at the quay.
words.ex_cn: 船停在了码头。
words.en: A quay is a long platform beside the sea or a river where boats can be tied up and loaded or unloaded.

words.tr: adj. 恶心的；欲吐的；稍感紧张的；略有不安的
words.ex: He feels queasy after eating too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多糖果后感到恶心。
words.en: If you feel queasy, you feel slightly sick or uncomfortable, especially because you are nervous or worried.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.tr: v. 熄灭；平息；抑制（欲望）；用水冷却
words.ex: He quenched the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水熄灭了火。
words.en: To satisfy one's thirst or to extinguish a fire or to suppress a feeling or desire.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.tr:
n. 询问；疑问；问号
v. 询问；怀疑
words.ex: He made a query about the bus schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了公交车的时刻表。
words.en: A query is a question, especially one that you ask in order to check that something is true or correct.

words.tr:
n. 长队；
v. 排队；
words.ex: There is a long queue at the ticket counter.
words.ex_cn: 售票处排着一条长队。
words.en: A queue is a line of people or vehicles waiting for something.

words.tr:
n. 遁词；狡辩；支吾以对；争论的小问题
v. 使用遁词；含糊其辞；吹毛求疵
words.ex: His excuse was just a quibble to avoid blame.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口只是逃避责任的遁词。
words.en: To argue or raise objections about a trivial matter or minor detail.

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.ex: The lake offers quietude at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 湖面在日出时带来宁静。
words.en: A state of stillness, calmness, and quiet in a place or person.

words.ex: She is the quintessence of grace.
words.ex_cn: 她是优雅的典范。
words.en: The quintessence of something is the most perfect or typical example of it.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 奇事；巧合；怪癖；奇行
words.ex: His habit of talking to his plants is a strange quirk.
words.ex_cn: 他跟植物说话的习惯是一个奇怪的奇事。
words.en: A quirk is a peculiar habit or aspect of a person's character, or an unexpected twist in a situation or story.

words.ex: He was called a quisling for helping the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为帮助敌人而被称为叛徒。
words.en: A quisling is a person who collaborates with an enemy occupying force, often serving in a puppet government or similar capacity.

words.tr:
v. 颤抖；颤动；发抖
n. 颤抖
words.ex: The leaf quivers in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树叶在风中颤抖。
words.en: To shake or tremble with a slight rapid motion; a case for carrying arrows.

words.tr: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；不切实际的
words.ex: He made a quixotic effort to fix the broken bridge with sticks and glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用树枝和胶水试图修复那座破桥，这真是异想天开。
words.en: If you describe someone's ideas or plans as quixotic, you mean that they are imaginative or hopeful but unrealistic.

words.tr: adj. 疑惑的；嘲弄的；揶揄的
words.ex: He gave a quizzical look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出困惑的表情。
words.en: If you give someone a quizzical look or smile, you look at them or smile at them in a way that shows that you are surprised or amused by their behavior.

words.ex: A quorum must be present to conduct official business.
words.ex_cn: 必须有法定人数在场才能进行正式业务。
words.en: A quorum is the minimum number of people that must be present at a meeting before it can officially begin and before official decisions can be taken.

words.tr: adj. 每日的；平凡的；平常的
words.ex: He drinks coffee every quotidian morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is quotidian occurs every day or is very common and ordinary.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words R

words.tr: adj. 患狂犬病的；狂暴的；疯狂的
words.ex: The rabid dog ran wildly through the street.
words.ex_cn: 那只狂犬在街上狂奔。
words.en: If you describe someone as rabid, you mean that they have very strong and unreasonable opinions or beliefs about a subject, especially in politics.

words.tr: n. 善于讲故事的人；健谈者
words.ex: He was known as a raconteur, always able to captivate an audience with his stories.
words.ex_cn: 他以健谈著称，总能用他的故事吸引听众。
words.en: A raconteur is someone who is good at telling stories in an interesting and amusing way.

words.ex: The ragamuffin played in the mud with no shoes.
words.ex_cn: 那个衣衫褴褛的孩子光着脚在泥里玩。
words.en: A ragamuffin is a child who is dressed in old, torn clothes and looks dirty, often because they are poor.

words.ex: The train runs on the rail.
words.ex_cn: 火车在铁轨上行驶。
words.en: A rail is a horizontal bar, typically made of metal or wood, used as a support or barrier; or a track made of steel rails along which trains run.

words.ex: He really loves his job.
words.ex_cn: 他真正地热爱他的工作。
words.en: You use really to emphasize that something is true or that it is the case.

words.tr: adj. 放荡的；肆无忌惮的；潇洒的
words.ex: He wore a rakish hat at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上戴了一顶歪斜的帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone as rakish, you mean that they are stylish and confident in a way that is slightly unconventional and possibly a little disreputable.

words.tr:
v. 集合起来；振作；复苏
n. 集会
words.ex: The crowd rallied to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集起来支持他们的球队。
words.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party or a sports team. It can also mean to come together again in order to continue fighting or arguing after a defeat or a period of confusion.

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

words.tr: n. 分支；支流；衍生物；后果
words.ex: The ramification of the tree spread wide.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的分支延伸得很广。
words.en: A ramification is a complex or unwelcome consequence of an action or decision.

words.ex: The decision will ramify into many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定将会引发许多问题。
words.en: To divide or spread out into branches or branchlike parts.

words.ex: The wheelchair goes up the ramp easily.
words.ex_cn: 轮椅可以轻松地走上坡道。
words.en: A ramp is a sloping surface connecting two levels, such as a road or a path.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: n. 防御土墙；城墙；壁垒
words.ex: The old castle had a high rampart around it.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡周围有一道高高的城墙。
words.en: A rampart is a wide, high wall of earth, stone, or other material built around a place to protect it from attack.

words.tr: adj. 摇摇欲坠的；破烂不堪的
words.ex: The old house was ramshackle and needed repair.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子摇摇欲坠，需要修理。
words.en: A ramshackle building or vehicle is in very bad condition and in danger of falling down.

words.ex: The milk turned rancid after being left out.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶被放在外面后变酸了。
words.en: If food is rancid, it tastes or smells bad because it is no longer fresh.

words.ex: He still feels rancor toward his old boss.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然对他的前老板怀有怨恨。
words.en: A feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.tr: v. 使人耿耿于怀；令人怀恨
words.ex: The unfair comment still rankles him.
words.ex_cn: 那句不公平的话仍让他耿耿于怀。
words.en: If something rankles, it continues to cause you irritation, bitterness, or pain, often because you think it was unfair.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；激昂地说
n. 喧闹的话；夸口话；叫喊
words.ex: He went on a rant about bad service.
words.ex_cn: 他大肆抱怨服务很差。
words.en: To speak or write in an angry or violent manner, often for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 贪婪的；贪得无厌的；劫掠的
words.ex: The rapacious wolf ate all the food.
words.ex_cn: 贪婪的狼吃掉了所有食物。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as rapacious, you disapprove of their greedy or selfish behaviour.

words.ex: They have good rapport with their students.
words.ex_cn: 他们与学生关系友好。
words.en: A friendly relationship in which people understand each other very well.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的；专心致志的
words.ex: The children were rapt during the story.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们全神贯注地听故事。
words.en: If someone is rapt, they are so interested in or fascinated by what they are seeing or hearing that they do not pay attention to anything else.

words.tr: adj. 高雅的； v. “rarefy”的过去式；
words.ex: He enjoys rarefied art and classical music.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢高雅的艺术和古典音乐。
words.en: Rarefied means made less dense or concentrated, especially in the context of air or gases. It can also refer to something that is elevated in character or nature, often in a way that is considered refined or exclusive.

words.ex: His voice sounds raspy after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他大喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: A raspy voice or sound is unpleasantly rough.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.ex: His ratiocination helped him solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他的推理帮助他解开了这个谜题。
words.en: The process of logical reasoning or argumentation.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.tr: v.  合理化； 使合理
words.ex: He tries to rationalize his bad choices.
words.ex_cn: 他试图为自己的错误选择找借口。
words.en: To rationalize something means to try to find reasons to explain or justify it, often when these reasons are not really good ones.

words.tr: adj. 沙哑的；粗声的；喧闹的
words.ex: His raucous voice made it hard to understand him.
words.ex_cn: 他沙哑的声音让他很难被听清楚。
words.en: A raucous sound is loud and harsh.

words.tr:
v. 毁坏；破坏；劫掠
n. 破坏；蹂躏
words.ex: The storm ravaged the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个小村庄。
words.en: To ravage means to cause severe and extensive damage to something.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.tr: v. 解开(~ sth. out)；使更复杂(~ sth. up)
words.ex: She raveled the tangled yarn out slowly.
words.ex_cn: 她慢慢地把缠绕的毛线解开。
words.en: To ravel means to tangle or untangle threads or fibers, or to become tangled or untangled. It can also refer to the process of separating the threads of a woven or knitted fabric, or to confuse or complicate a situation.

words.ex: He was ravenous after running five miles.
words.ex_cn: 跑了五英里后，他饿极了。
words.en: If you are ravenous, you are extremely hungry.

words.ex: The river flows through a deep ravine.
words.ex_cn: 河流流经一个深谷。
words.en: A ravine is a deep, narrow gorge with steep sides, often carved by a river or stream.

words.tr: v. 使夷为平地；彻底摧毁
words.ex: They will raze the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将把那座旧建筑夷为平地。
words.en: To raze a building, town, or forest means to completely destroy it, especially by knocking it down or burning it.

words.tr:
adj. 反动的；保守的
n. 反动派；保守人士
words.ex: The reactionary government banned free speech.
words.ex_cn: 这个反动政府禁止了言论自由。
words.en: A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country.

words.ex: This book is about the realm of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于人工智能领域的。
words.en: A realm is a country ruled by a king or queen, or an area of activity, interest, or knowledge.

words.tr: n. 收割者；收获者；收割机
words.ex: The reaper cuts wheat in the field.
words.ex_cn: 收割者在田里收割小麦。
words.en: A reaper is a person or machine that cuts and gathers crops at harvest.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；退款
v. 减少
words.ex: He got a rebate on his new TV.
words.ex_cn: 他买新电视时得到了一笔回扣。
words.en: A rebate is a partial refund to someone who has paid too much for tax, rent, or a utility.

words.tr:
v. 断然拒绝
n. 粗暴回绝；生硬的拒绝
words.ex: He rebuffed her offer with a shake of his head.
words.ex_cn: 他摇了摇头，拒绝了她的提议。
words.en: If you rebuff someone or rebuff a suggestion that they make, you refuse to do what they suggest.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.ex: The children enjoyed solving the rebus puzzles.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢解画谜。
words.en: A rebus is a puzzle in which words are represented by combinations of pictures and individual letters; for instance, 'i' might be represented by an eye.

words.ex: He gave a strong rebuttal to the claim.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个说法给出了有力的反驳。
words.en: A rebuttal is a statement or piece of evidence that contradicts or opposes a previous statement or evidence.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.tr: v. 撤回声明；放弃信仰
words.ex: He recanted his statement after seeing the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他在看到证据后撤回了他的话。
words.en: If you recant, you say publicly that you no longer hold a set of beliefs that you had in the past.

words.tr: v. 重述要点；简要回顾
words.ex: Can you recapitulate the main points of the lecture?
words.ex_cn: 你能重述一下讲座的主要要点吗？
words.en: If you recapitulate something, you say it again briefly, or you give a summary of it.

words.tr: v. 重铸；改写；更换（演员）
words.ex: The director decided to recast the play with a different set of actors.
words.ex_cn: 导演决定用另一组演员重新排演这出戏。
words.en: To recast something means to change it by organizing it in a different way or presenting it in a different form.

words.tr: adj. 善于接受的；能接纳的；
words.ex: He is receptive to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他善于接受新想法。
words.en: Willing to consider or accept new suggestions and ideas.

words.ex: Many people lost jobs during the recession.
words.ex_cn: 在经济不景气期间，许多人失去了工作。
words.en: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is not doing well, industrial production and business activity are at a low level, and many people are unemployed.

words.ex: He returned to prison because of recidivism.
words.ex_cn: 他因再犯而重返监狱。
words.en: Recidivism is the act of repeating an undesirable behavior after having experienced negative consequences of that behavior.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.ex: They have a reciprocal agreement to help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们有一个互相帮助的互惠协议。
words.en: A reciprocal action or agreement involves two people or groups who do the same thing to each other or agree to help each other in a similar way.

words.tr: v. 回报；报答；往复；来回
words.ex: She helped me, and I will reciprocate.
words.ex_cn: 她帮了我，我会回报她。
words.en: If your feelings or actions towards someone are reciprocated, the other person feels or behaves in the same way towards you as you have felt or behaved towards them.

words.tr: n. 隐居者；遁世者；隐士
words.ex: He lives as a recluse in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他住在树林里，过着隐居的生活。
words.en: A recluse is a person who lives alone and avoids other people.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.ex: The recondite math problem confused most students.
words.ex_cn: 这道深奥的数学题让大多数学生感到困惑。
words.en: Recondite knowledge or information is known and understood by very few people.

words.ex: The soldier did reconnaissance before the mission.
words.ex_cn: 士兵在任务前进行了侦察。
words.en: Reconnaissance is the military activity of obtaining information about an enemy's position, strength, or intentions by sending out small groups of soldiers or by using aircraft.

words.tr:
v. 细述；叙述
n. 叙述；重新计票
words.ex: He tried to recount the accident to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向警察重新叙述那场事故。
words.en: To recount means to tell someone about something that happened, often in detail; or to count something again to make sure the number is correct.

words.ex: He had no recourse but to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他别无依靠，只能求助。
words.en: If you have recourse to a particular course of action, you use it when you are in a difficult situation or when you need to achieve something.

words.ex: They shouted recrimination at each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此大声指责。
words.en: Recrimination is the act of accusing someone who has accused you of something.

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.ex: His rectitude in business dealings was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的正直是众所周知的。
words.en: Moral integrity; honesty and correctness of judgement or behaviour.

words.tr: adj. 斜躺的；斜靠的；侧卧的
words.ex: The old man sat in a recumbent chair.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人坐在一张躺椅上。
words.en: A recumbent position or posture is one in which a person is lying down or leaning back in a relaxed manner.

words.ex: He needs time to recuperate after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他需要时间在手术后恢复。
words.en: To recuperate means to recover from illness or exertion, or to regain or make up for something lost or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 反复出现的；再发生的；
words.ex: He has recurrent headaches every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都反复出现头痛。
words.en: Happening or appearing again or repeatedly.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.ex: The redoubtable warrior struck fear into the hearts of his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 那位令人敬畏的战士让敌人心生恐惧。
words.en: If you describe someone as redoubtable, you have great respect for their power and strength, and you may be afraid of them as well.

words.ex: The government must redress the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 政府必须纠正这部不公平的法律。
words.en: If you redress something such as a wrong or a complaint, you do something to correct it or to improve things for the person who has been wronged.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.tr:
v. 散发臭气；发出难闻的气味；洋溢；充满
n. 恶臭；难闻的气味
words.ex: The garbage reeks in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾在烈日下散发恶臭。
words.en: To reek of something means to smell very strongly of it, especially in an unpleasant way.

words.ex: The students eat lunch in the refectory.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在食堂吃午饭。
words.en: A refectory is a dining hall, especially in a monastery, college, or other institution.

words.ex: The refraction of light makes the straw look bent in water.
words.ex_cn: 光的折光使水中的吸管看起来弯曲了。
words.en: The change in direction of a wave, such as light or sound, when it passes from one medium into another of different density.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；难驾驭的；难以治愈的
words.ex: The refractory material can withstand high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 这种耐火材料能承受高温。
words.en: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control; difficult to melt or work; resistant to heat.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: The refulgent sun illuminated the entire room.
words.ex_cn: 灿烂的阳光照亮了整个房间。
words.en: Shining brightly; radiant.

words.tr: v. 重新刷新；翻新；整修
words.ex: They will refurbish the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新这栋老房子。
words.en: To refurbish something means to clean it, decorate it, and provide it with new equipment or facilities, especially so that it is more attractive or more useful.

words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.tr: adj. 皇家的；尊贵的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: The queen wore a regal crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着一顶威严的王冠。
words.en: If you describe something as regal, you mean that it is suitable for a king or queen, because it is very impressive or beautiful.

words.tr: v. 盛情招待；尽情吃喝；使欢悦
words.ex: He regaled us with stories of his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他给我们讲了他旅行的故事，让我们很开心。
words.en: To regale someone means to entertain them with stories or to provide them with a lot of enjoyable food and drink.

words.tr: n. 划船比赛；赛艇比赛
words.ex: The boys joined a regatta last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末，这些男孩参加了一场帆船比赛。
words.en: A regatta is a sporting event consisting of a series of boat or yacht races.

words.ex: The forest shows regeneration after the fire.
words.ex_cn: 森林在火灾后显示出再生。
words.en: The process of renewal, restoration, and growth that makes cells, organisms, and ecosystems resilient to natural fluctuations or events that cause disturbance or damage.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.ex: The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司会报销你的旅行费用。
words.en: If you reimburse someone for something, you pay them back the money that they have spent or lost because of it.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: He gave a quick rejoinder to her question.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的问题迅速做出了回应。
words.en: A rejoinder is a reply, especially a quick or witty one, to a question or remark.

words.tr: v. 使年轻； 使恢复精神； 使复原
words.ex: The new sleep routine helps rejuvenate her energy.
words.ex_cn: 新的睡眠习惯帮助她恢复精力。
words.en: To rejuvenate someone or something means to make them look or feel young, fresh, or lively again.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.tr: v. 发慈悲；动怜悯心；缓和
words.ex: The teacher finally relented and gave the students more time.
words.ex_cn: 老师终于发慈悲，给了学生们更多时间。
words.en: If you relent, you allow someone to do something that you had previously refused to allow them to do.

words.ex: This information is relevant to our project.
words.ex_cn: 这些信息与我们的项目相关。
words.en: Something that is relevant to a situation or person is important or significant in that situation or to that person.

words.ex: The old temple is a relic from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是来自古代的遗迹。
words.en: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.tr:
v. 喜欢；享受；从…获得乐趣
n. 享受；乐趣；调味品
words.ex: He relishes every bite of his favorite food.
words.ex_cn: 他享受着每一口他最喜欢的食物。
words.en: If you relish something, you enjoy it very much.

words.tr: adj. 可补救的；可挽救的；可矫正的
words.ex: The damage to the environment is remediable if we act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们迅速采取行动，对环境的破坏是可以补救的。
words.en: If something is remediable, it can be corrected or cured.

words.ex: He felt a warm reminiscence of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了对童年的温馨回忆。
words.en: The act or process of recalling past experiences, events, etc.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；怠慢的；不留心的
words.ex: It would be remiss of me not to mention the importance of regular exercise.
words.ex_cn: 不提及定期锻炼的重要性，我会感到疏忽。
words.en: If someone is remiss, they are careless and do not do the things they are expected to do.

words.tr: n. 宽恕；赦免；减轻；豁免
words.ex: The priest granted remission of his sins.
words.ex_cn: 神父宽恕了他的罪过。
words.en: If someone who has had a serious disease such as cancer is in remission or if the disease is in remission, the disease has been controlled so that they are not as ill as they were.

words.ex: The remnant of the old wall still stands.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙的残余部分仍然矗立着。
words.en: A remnant is a small remaining quantity of something.

words.ex: The committee issued a remonstrance against the proposed changes.
words.ex_cn: 委员会对拟议的变更提出了抗议。
words.en: A remonstrance is a formal statement of protest or complaint.

words.ex: He felt remorse after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到后悔。
words.en: Remorse is a strong feeling of sadness and regret about something wrong that you have done.

words.tr: adj. 有报酬的；有利益的；
words.ex: He took a remunerative job to support his family.
words.ex_cn: 他找了一份有报酬的工作来养家。
words.en: providing payment; profitable

words.tr: v. 撕碎；劈开；揪扯；割裂
words.ex: The storm rends the tree from its roots.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨将树从根部撕裂。
words.en: To tear or split something apart with great force.

words.ex: The rain rendered the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 雨水使道路变得滑溜。
words.en: To render something means to cause it to become or to provide it. It can also mean to express or translate something.

words.tr: n. 会合地点；约会；集会
words.ex: They will rendezvous at the park at 6 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 他们将在晚上6点在公园会合。
words.en: A rendezvous is a meeting that has been arranged between people, often secretly.

words.ex: The rendition of the song by the singer moved everyone.
words.ex_cn: 歌手对这首歌的演出打动了所有人。
words.en: A rendition of a play, poem, or piece of music is a performance of it.

words.tr:
n. 叛徒；变节者；叛教者
adj. 背叛的；变节的
v. 背叛
words.ex: He is a renegade who left the team suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个突然离开团队的叛徒。
words.en: A renegade is a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles.

words.ex: He reneged on his promise to help me.
words.ex_cn: 他背弃了帮助我的承诺。
words.en: If someone reneges on a promise or an agreement, they do not do what they have promised or agreed to do.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

words.ex: He is a scientist of great renown.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位享有盛誉的科学家。
words.en: Renown is the state of being known and talked about by many people because of your achievements, qualities, or actions.

words.tr: v. 租借；出租；“rend”的过去式和过去分词； n. 租金；
words.ex: They rent a small apartment in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们租了一间城市里的小公寓。
words.en: Rent refers to the payment made periodically by a tenant to a landlord for the use of property or land.

words.tr: adj. 可补救的；可补偿的
words.ex: The broken bike is reparable.
words.ex_cn: 这辆坏了的自行车可以修好。
words.en: If something is reparable, it is possible to fix or mend it.

words.ex: The preparation for the exam took two weeks.
words.ex_cn: 考试的准备花了两周时间。
words.en: Preparation is the process of getting something ready for use or for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 敏捷的回答；机智的回答
words.ex: The witty repartee between the two comedians kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 两位喜剧演员之间的机智对话让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A repartee is a quick, witty reply or a conversation full of such replies.

words.ex: They enjoyed a leisurely repast in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们在花园里享受了一顿悠闲的餐食。
words.en: A repast is a meal or the act of eating a meal.

words.ex: The repeal of the old law took effect last month.
words.ex_cn: 这项旧法律的废止上个月生效了。
words.en: If the government repeals a law, it officially ends it, so that it is no longer valid.

words.ex: The smell repels insects.
words.ex_cn: 这种气味能击退昆虫。
words.en: If something repels you, it is so unpleasant or offensive that you want to avoid it or push it away.

words.ex: We use a repellent to keep mosquitoes away.
words.ex_cn: 我们使用驱虫剂来驱赶蚊子。
words.en: A repellent is a substance that is used to keep insects or animals away from something. It can also refer to something that is extremely unpleasant or disgusting.

words.tr: n. 弹回；反响；后果；反射
words.ex: The ball showed a clear repercussion off the wall.
words.ex_cn: 球从墙上明显地弹回。
words.en: The effect that an action, event, or decision has on something, especially a bad effect.

words.ex: His repertoire includes singing, dancing, and acting.
words.ex_cn: 他的全部才能包括唱歌、跳舞和表演。
words.en: A repertoire is all the plays, songs, pieces of music, etc. that a performer or group knows and can perform.

words.tr:
n. 重复部分；再现
v. 重演；重奏
words.ex: The song ended with a short reprise of the chorus.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌以副歌的简短重复部分结束。
words.en: A reprise is a repetition of a piece of music or a performance. It can also refer to the act of repeating something.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

words.ex: He bought a replica of the ancient statue.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一件古代雕像的复制品。
words.en: A replica of something such as a statue, building, or weapon is an accurate copy of it.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.tr: n. 仓库；贮藏室；存放处；智囊
words.ex: He saves his code in a GitHub repository.
words.ex_cn: 他把代码保存在 GitHub 仓库中。
words.en: A repository is a place where something is stored or can be found.

words.tr: adj. 应受谴责的；应受指责的；
words.ex: His lying to the teacher was reprehensible.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师撒谎是应受谴责的。
words.en: If you think that someone's behavior is reprehensible, you think that it is very bad or unacceptable.

words.ex: He tried to repress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you repress a feeling, you deliberately do not express it, often because it is considered unacceptable or inappropriate.

words.tr:
v. 缓期执行；暂缓处刑
n. 缓刑；暂缓
words.ex: The judge gave him a reprieve until next month.
words.ex_cn: 法官给了他一个延期，直到下个月。
words.en: If someone who has been sentenced in a court is given a reprieve, their punishment is officially delayed or cancelled.

words.tr:
n. 申斥；谴责
v. 斥责；训斥
words.ex: The teacher gave him a reprimand for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而训斥了他。
words.en: A reprimand is a formal or official expression of disapproval, typically by a person in authority.

words.tr: n. 报复；报仇；报复性劫掠
words.ex: He feared reprisal after speaking out against the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因公开反对老板而害怕遭到报复。
words.en: An act of retaliation for a wrong or injury.

words.tr:
v. 责备；指责
n. 责备；指责
words.ex: She reproached him for being late.
words.ex_cn: 她责备他迟到了。
words.en: To express disapproval or disappointment towards someone because of their actions or behavior.

words.tr: n. 堕落的人；不道德的人
words.ex: The townspeople shunned the reprobate, fearing his influence.
words.ex_cn: 镇上的人们都避开那个堕落的人，害怕他的影响。
words.en: A reprobate is a person who behaves in a way that is morally wrong and who shows no regret or shame for their actions.

words.ex: The proposal faced widespread reprobation from the public.
words.ex_cn: 该提案遭到了公众的广泛反对。
words.en: Reprobation refers to the act of condemning or disapproving of someone or something strongly.

words.ex: The teacher reproved the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责骂了他。
words.en: If you reprove someone, you speak angrily or seriously to them because they have behaved in a wrong or foolish way.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.ex: She felt a strong repugnance towards the idea of eating insects.
words.ex_cn: 她对吃昆虫的想法感到非常反感。
words.en: A strong feeling of dislike or disgust towards something.

words.tr: n. 厌恶；嫌弃；排斥；斥力
words.ex: The sight filled her with repulsion.
words.ex_cn: 那景象让她感到厌恶。
words.en: A feeling of intense distaste or disgust.

words.tr: adj. 有声望的；声誉好的
words.ex: He works for a reputable company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家信誉良好的公司工作。
words.en: A reputable person or organization is considered to be good and trustworthy by most people.

words.tr:
adj. 据说的；号称的；有名气的
v. 认为；以为；“repute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a reputed doctor in this city.
words.ex_cn: 他是这座城市里有名的医生。
words.en: Generally believed to be a particular thing, although this might not be true.

words.ex: The choir performed a beautiful requiem in memory of the deceased.
words.ex_cn: 唱诗班为纪念逝者演唱了一首优美的安魂曲。
words.en: A requiem is a piece of music that is performed in a Catholic church in memory of someone who has died, or a piece of music that is similar to this and is performed in memory of someone who has died.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；必备的；必不可少的；
words.ex: A passport is a requisite for international travel.
words.ex_cn: 护照是国际旅行所必需的。
words.en: Something that is necessary for a particular purpose.

words.ex: She tried to requite his kindness with a thoughtful gift.
words.ex_cn: 她试图用一份贴心的礼物来回报他的好意。
words.en: To repay, return, or retaliate for something.

words.ex: The school will rescind the rule next month.
words.ex_cn: 学校下个月将撤销这项规定。
words.en: If a government or a group of people in power rescind a law or agreement, they officially withdraw it and state that it is no longer valid.

words.ex: He felt resentment after being ignored by his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他被朋友忽视后感到怨恨。
words.en: Resentment is a feeling of anger or bitterness about something that you believe is unfair.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.ex: The residue left in the cup was sugar.
words.ex_cn: 杯子里留下的残留物是糖。
words.en: A residue of something is a small amount that remains after the main part has gone or been taken or used.

words.ex: He handed in his resignation last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周递交了辞职信。
words.en: The act of giving up a job or position in a formal or official way; also refers to the acceptance of something undesirable but inevitable.

words.ex: The resilient child bounced back quickly after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这个适应力强的孩子在事故后很快恢复了。
words.en: Something that is resilient is strong and not easily damaged by being hit, stretched, or squeezed.

words.ex: The resolution of the conflict took many meetings.
words.ex_cn: 这个冲突的解决花了多次会议。
words.en: A resolution is a formal decision made at a meeting by the vote of the people who are there. It can also refer to a firm decision to do or not to do something.

words.ex: He resolved the problem with a simple plan.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的计划解决了问题。
words.en: If you resolve to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

words.tr: adj. 洪亮的；共振的；引起共鸣的；
words.ex: The bell has a resonant sound.
words.ex_cn: 这口钟的声音洪亮。
words.en: A sound that is resonant is deep, strong, and clear, often because it is produced in a space that echoes or amplifies it.

words.ex: Breathing deeply helps with respiration.
words.ex_cn: 深呼吸有助于呼吸。
words.en: The process of breathing, which involves inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide.

words.ex: The rain gave us a short respite from the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨为我们带来了短暂的凉爽缓解。
words.en: A respite is a short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: The queen was resplendent in her golden crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着金色王冠，光彩夺目。
words.en: Something that is resplendent is very bright and attractive, often because it is richly decorated or very colorful.

words.ex: The responsiveness of the touchscreen is very good.
words.ex_cn: 这个触摸屏的敏感性很好。
words.en: The quality of reacting quickly and positively.

words.tr: n. 归还；赔偿；恢复原状
words.ex: The court ordered restitution for the damaged property.
words.ex_cn: 法院命令对受损财产进行赔偿。
words.en: The act of restoring something to its original state or the act of compensating for loss or damage.

words.tr: adj. 不安宁的； 焦躁不安的；难驾驭的；倔强的
words.ex: The audience grew restive as the speaker droned on.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者喋喋不休，听众开始焦躁不安。
words.en: If you are restive, you are impatient or bored with a situation and you want it to change.

words.ex: He showed restraint when he stayed calm during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持冷静，表现出了克制。
words.en: Restraint is a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control or within limits.

words.tr: n. 恢复；重新开始；继续进行
words.ex: The resumption of classes was delayed by one week.
words.ex_cn: 课程的恢复被推迟了一周。
words.en: The act of starting something again after a pause or interruption.

words.ex: The idea of a resurgence in national pride began to take hold.
words.ex_cn: 民族自豪感复兴的想法开始深入人心。
words.en: If something resurges, it becomes stronger or more popular again after a period of being weak or not popular.

words.tr: v. （使）复活；（使）恢复知觉；（使）复兴
words.ex: The paramedics tried to resuscitate the man after he collapsed.
words.ex_cn: 当这位男子晕倒后，急救人员试图救活他。
words.en: To resuscitate someone means to bring them back to consciousness or to make them start breathing again after they have stopped.

words.ex: He retains his old photos in a box.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧照片保存在一个盒子里。
words.en: If you retain something, you keep it or continue to have it.

words.ex: He feared retaliation after speaking against the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因反对老板而害怕遭到报复。
words.en: Retaliation is the act of returning an injury or wrong, especially by inflicting harm in return for harm received.

words.tr: adj. 记性好的；有保持力的
words.ex: She has a very retentive memory.
words.ex_cn: 她有非常好的记忆力。
words.en: If you have a retentive memory, you are able to remember things easily.

words.tr: adj. 沉默寡言的；讳莫如深的
words.ex: He is reticent about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的感受很沉默。
words.en: If you are reticent about something, you are unwilling to talk about it or make your feelings known.

words.ex: The king was accompanied by a large retinue.
words.ex_cn: 国王由一大群随行人员陪同。
words.en: A retinue is a group of people who travel with an important person to help or protect them.

words.tr:
adj. 不爱交际的；离群索居的；即将退休的
v. 退休；退役；“retire”的现在分词
words.ex: She was a retiring woman, preferring to spend her evenings at home.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个不爱与人交往的女人，更喜欢在家度过晚上。
words.en: If someone is retiring, they are about to leave their job permanently, usually because of age.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.ex: The company must retrench to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司必须裁员以节省资金。
words.en: If a person or organization retrenches, they spend less money.

words.ex: He feared retribution for his actions.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕因自己的行为而受到报复。
words.en: Retribution is punishment for a crime, especially punishment that is carried out by someone other than the official authorities.

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

words.ex: The law is retroactive and covers last year.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律具有追溯效力，适用于去年。
words.en: If a decision, action, or law is retroactive, it is intended to take effect from a date before it was actually made.

words.tr:
adj. 倒退的；退化的；退步的
v. 逆行；倒退；堕落
words.ex: The company's retrograde policies led to a decline in productivity.
words.ex_cn: 公司倒退的政策导致了生产力的下降。
words.en: If you describe an action or idea as retrograde, you disapprove of it because it returns to old ideas or methods and does not take advantage of recent progress.

words.tr: adj. 回顾的；回想的；溯及既往的
words.ex: He made a retrospective look at his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回顾了自己的童年。
words.en: A retrospective is an exhibition or compilation showing the development of an artist's work over a period of time. It can also refer to a look back at past events or situations.

words.ex: The party was filled with revelry and laughter.
words.ex_cn: 派对上充满了狂欢和笑声。
words.en: Revelry is a situation in which people are enjoying themselves in a lively and noisy way, often while they are drinking alcohol.

words.ex: The sound reverberated in the empty hall.
words.ex_cn: 声音在空荡的大厅里回响。
words.en: If a sound reverberates, it continues to be heard as an echo, or it seems to be repeated many times.

words.ex: He spoke in a reverent tone as he described the ancient temple.
words.ex_cn: 他在描述这座古老寺庙时，语气恭敬。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as reverent, you mean that they are showing great respect for a person or thing.

words.ex: He sat by the window in reverie.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边，沉浸在遐想中。
words.en: A reverie is a state of imagining or thinking about pleasant things, often as a way of escaping from reality.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.ex: He was reviled by his opponents for his controversial views.
words.ex_cn: 由于他的有争议的观点，他受到了对手的辱骂。
words.en: To revile someone means to criticize them in an abusive or angrily insulting manner.

words.ex: The teacher will revoke his privilege to use the computer.
words.ex_cn: 老师将撤销他使用电脑的权限。
words.en: If someone in authority revokes something such as a law, license, or agreement, they cancel it.

words.ex: She felt revulsion when she saw the dirty food.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到那脏兮兮的食物时，感到非常厌恶。
words.en: A sudden and intense feeling of disgust or loathing.

words.tr: v. 狂热地描述；过分赞美；写作狂想诗文
words.ex: She loves to rhapsodize about her travels.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢热情地谈论她的旅行。
words.en: To rhapsodize means to speak or write about someone or something with great enthusiasm and delight.

words.tr: n. 修辞学；花言巧语；华丽的文辞；
words.ex: He studied rhetoric to improve his speaking skills.
words.ex_cn: 他学习修辞学以提高自己的演讲能力。
words.en: Rhetoric is the art or study of using language effectively and persuasively.

words.ex: His ribald jokes were inappropriate for a family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 他的下流笑话不适合家庭聚会。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as ribald, you mean that it refers to sex in a rude or humorous way.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.ex: The rider rode his horse quickly across the field.
words.ex_cn: 骑手快速骑马穿过田野。
words.en: A rider is someone who rides a horse, bicycle, or motorcycle, or a clause added to a document that provides additional information or conditions.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；充满…的
words.ex: Rumors are rife in the town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在镇上到处流传。
words.en: If you say that something, usually something bad, is rife in a place or that the place is rife with it, you mean that it is very common.

words.ex: There is a small rift in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: A rift is a major fault or break in the Earth's crust.

words.tr:
n. 索具装备；钻探设备；装备
v. 配备索具；操纵；舞弊
words.ex: He uses a rig to hold the camera steady.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个支架来固定相机。
words.en: To rig something means to arrange or set it up in a particular way, often in a temporary or makeshift manner. It can also refer to the equipment used in drilling for oil or gas, or the sails and ropes on a ship.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.ex: The math proof requires rigor.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学证明需要严谨。
words.en: Rigor is a situation in which people are made to follow rules in a very strict way.

words.ex: His comments about her appearance really riled her.
words.ex_cn: 他对她外貌的评论真的激怒了她。
words.en: To make someone annoyed or irritated.

words.tr:
adj. 吸引人的；引人入胜的
v. （用铆钉）固定；吸引住；“rivet”的现在分词
words.ex: The movie was riveting from start to finish.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影从头到尾都扣人心弦。
words.en: If you describe something as riveting, you mean that it is extremely interesting and exciting, and that it holds your attention completely.

words.ex: A small rivulet flows through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 一条小溪流过森林。
words.en: A very small stream.

words.tr: adj. 强健的；强壮的；结实的；
words.ex: The dog is robust and runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很强健，每天跑步。
words.en: Strong and healthy; vigorous. (of an object) sturdy in construction.

words.tr:
adj. 洛可可式的；旧式的；过分修饰的
n. 洛可可式
words.ex: The room has rococo decorations with lots of curves and gold.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有大量曲线和金色的洛可可装饰。
words.en: Rococo is a style of architecture, music, and art that emerged in France in the early 18th century, characterized by elaborate ornamentation and asymmetrical values.

words.ex: The news roiled the financial markets.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息搅乱了金融市场。
words.en: To make (a liquid) turbid or muddy by stirring up sediment; to disturb or irritate.

words.tr: adj. 玫瑰色的；红润的（皮肤）；美好的；有希望的（前途等）
words.ex: The sky turned rosy at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 日出时，天空变成了玫瑰色。
words.en: If you describe a situation as rosy, you mean that it seems to be full of hope and promise.

words.ex: The coach checks the roster before every game.
words.ex_cn: 教练在每场比赛前检查名单。
words.en: A roster is a list which gives details of the members of a team, organization, or group, and the times or order in which they are to perform a particular duty.

words.tr: n. 讲坛；指挥台；领奖台
words.ex: He stood on the rostrum to give a speech.
words.ex_cn: 他站在讲台上发表演讲。
words.en: A rostrum is a raised platform on which someone stands to make a public speech, receive an award or medal, or conduct an orchestra.

words.tr: n. 死记硬背；机械的做法；生搬硬套
words.ex: He learned the poem by rote.
words.ex_cn: 他通过死记硬背学会了这首诗。
words.en: Rote is the process of learning something by repeating it many times without thinking about it or understanding it.

words.tr: n. 圆形建筑；圆形大厅
words.ex: The rotunda at the museum was a popular meeting spot.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆的圆形大厅是一个受欢迎的集合地点。
words.en: A rotunda is a large round room or building, especially one with a dome.

words.ex: The rotundity of the marble ball made it roll smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 大理石球的球状使它滚动得很顺畅。
words.en: The quality or state of being round in shape.

words.tr:
adj. 激励的；充满活力（或激情）的；令人振奋的
v. 唤醒；觉醒；“rouse”的现在分词
words.ex: The speech was a rousing call to action.
words.ex_cn: 这次演讲是一次激动人心的行动号召。
words.en: Causing great excitement or enthusiasm; stirring.

words.ex: We took a different route to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们换了条路线以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A route is a way from one place to another, or the path that something follows to reach a destination.

words.ex: The children played on the rubble after the building fell.
words.ex_cn: 建筑物倒塌后，孩子们在碎石上玩耍。
words.en: Rubble is the broken pieces of stone, brick, etc., that are left when a building falls down or is destroyed.

words.tr: n. 红字标题；说明；规定；题目；类目
words.ex: The rubric at the top of the page said 'Exam Instructions'.
words.ex_cn: 页面顶部的红字标题写着‘考试须知’。
words.en: A rubric is a set of instructions or rules.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；红的；淡红色
words.ex: Her complexion was ruddy from the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的脸色因寒冷的天气而变得红润。
words.en: Having a healthy red color, especially in the face.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；真的；正确的；
words.ex: The story is true.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是真实的。
words.en: in accordance with fact or reality

words.ex: The ruffian shouted at the old man.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍对老人大喊大叫。
words.en: A ruffian is a violent, lawless person.

words.ex: He sits quietly to ruminate on his choices.
words.ex_cn: 他静静地坐着沉思自己的选择。
words.en: To ruminate means to think deeply about something or to chew the cud, as a cow does.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；翻找；乱翻
n. 翻箱倒柜的寻找
words.ex: He rummaged through his drawer to find the keys.
words.ex_cn: 他翻找抽屉找钥匙。
words.en: If you rummage through something, you search for something you want by moving things around in a careless or hurried way.

words.tr: adj. 北欧古字的；卢恩文的；神秘的
words.ex: He found an old stone with runic letters.
words.ex_cn: 他发现了一块刻有如尼文字的古老石头。
words.en: Runic refers to the ancient alphabets used by Germanic peoples before the adoption of the Latin alphabet, or something resembling these alphabets.

words.ex: He used a clever ruse to escape from the prison.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个巧妙的计策从监狱逃脱。
words.en: A ruse is a trick or plan that is used to deceive someone.

words.tr:
adj. 乡村的；纯朴的；土气的
n. 乡下人；乡巴佬
words.ex: They live in a rustic cabin near the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一间乡村小屋里。
words.en: Rustic is used to describe things that are typical of the countryside rather than the town, or things that are simple and old-fashioned in a way that is considered typical of the countryside.

words.tr: v. （尤指在牛津、剑桥）罚（大学生）暂时停学；下乡；（使）成粗面石工；退归林下
words.ex: He was rusticated for a year due to his involvement in a campus protest.
words.ex_cn: 他因参与校园抗议而被停学一年。
words.en: To rusticate means to send someone to live in the country, or to make something appear more rural or simple. It can also refer to the act of suspending a student from a university as a form of punishment.

words.tr: adj. 无情的；冷酷的；残忍的；
words.ex: The ruthless boss fired employees without warning.
words.ex_cn: 这位无情的老板未经警告就解雇了员工。
words.en: If you say that someone is ruthless, you mean that you disapprove of them because they are very harsh or cruel, and will do anything that is necessary to achieve what they want.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words S

words.tr: n. 蓄意破坏者；破坏分子
words.ex: The saboteur tried to disrupt the operation by cutting the power lines.
words.ex_cn: 破坏者试图通过切断电源线来破坏运营。
words.en: A saboteur is a person who deliberately destroys or damages something, especially for political or military advantage.

words.tr: adj. 极甜的；过分甜的；故作多情的；奉承的；过于亲近的
words.ex: The cake tasted too saccharine.
words.ex_cn: 这块蛋糕尝起来太甜了。
words.en: Excessively sweet or sentimental.

words.tr: adj. 亵渎神圣的；大不敬的
words.ex: He made a sacrilegious joke about the church.
words.ex_cn: 他开了一个关于教堂的亵渎神明的玩笑。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or actions are sacrilegious, they show great disrespect towards something holy or something that people think should be respected.

words.tr: adj. 极神圣的；神圣不可侵犯的
words.ex: The church's rules were considered sacrosanct and unchangeable.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的规定被认为是神圣不可侵犯的，不可改变的。
words.en: If you describe something as sacrosanct, you mean that it is considered to be special and should not be changed or interfered with.

words.tr: adj. 虐待狂的；残酷成性的
words.ex: The sadistic man laughed when the dog cried.
words.ex_cn: 那个残忍的人当狗叫时笑了。
words.en: Deriving pleasure from inflicting pain, suffering, or humiliation on others.

words.ex: He told a long saga about his grandfather's adventures.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他祖父冒险的漫长故事。
words.en: A long, detailed story of connected events, especially one that is passed from one generation to the next.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.ex: She added sage to the stuffing for Thanksgiving dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她在感恩节晚餐的填料中加入了鼠尾草。
words.en: A sage is a person who is regarded as being very wise, especially someone who is known for their good judgment and deep understanding of life.

words.tr: adj. 猥亵的；淫秽的；诲淫的；好色的
words.ex: The novel was criticized for its salacious content.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说因其淫秽内容而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something such as a book or joke as salacious, you think that it deals with sexual matters in an unnecessarily detailed way.

words.ex: The salient point in the report is the cost increase.
words.ex_cn: 报告中最显著的要点是成本上升。
words.en: The most noticeable or important.

words.ex: The wound was cleaned with saline water.
words.ex_cn: 伤口用盐水清洗。
words.en: Saline is used to describe something that contains salt or is related to salt.

words.tr:
adj. 灰黄的；蜡黄的
n. 黄华柳；阔叶柳
v. （使）成灰黄色
words.ex: His face looks sallow after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他久病之后脸色发黄。
words.en: If someone is sallow, their skin, especially on their face, is a pale-yellowish color and looks unhealthy.

words.tr: adj. 有益健康的；环境宜人的
words.ex: The air in the mountains is salubrious.
words.ex_cn: 山里的空气有益健康。
words.en: A salubrious place is pleasant, healthy, and good for you.

words.ex: The experience was a salutary lesson in the importance of preparation.
words.ex_cn: 这次经历是一个关于准备重要性的有益教训。
words.en: A salutary experience or warning is one that has a good effect or influence, especially by showing you the bad results of a particular action or behaviour.

words.tr:
n. 抢救；
v. 打捞；挽救；抢救；
words.ex: The salvage of the ship took three days.
words.ex_cn: 对这艘船的抢救花了三天时间。
words.en: To salvage something means to retrieve or preserve it from loss or destruction, especially from a shipwreck or fire. It can also refer to the act of saving or rescuing something from a difficult situation.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr: n. 避难所；庇护所；庇护；
words.ex: The birds found sanctuary in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在森林里找到了避难所。
words.en: A sanctuary is a place where people or animals are protected from danger or trouble.

words.tr: adj. 血淋淋的；嗜杀的；残暴的
words.ex: The battle was known for its sanguinary nature.
words.ex_cn: 这场战斗因其血腥的性质而闻名。
words.en: Involving or causing much bloodshed; marked by great slaughter.

words.tr: adj. 乐天的；自信的；红润的
words.ex: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the future.
words.ex_cn: 尽管遭遇挫折，他对未来仍然充满希望。
words.en: If you are sanguine about something, you are cheerful and confident that things will happen in the way that you want them to.

words.tr:
n. 树液；
v. 使逐渐耗竭；使削弱；
words.ex: The tree releases sap in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在春天流出树液。
words.en: Sap is the watery fluid that circulates in the vascular system of a plant, carrying nutrients and sugars. It can also refer to the vitality or energy of a person or thing.

words.ex: He said it with sarcasm, even though he seemed happy.
words.ex_cn: 他说这话时带着讽刺，尽管他看起来很高兴。
words.en: Sarcasm is a sharp, bitter, or cutting expression or remark; a bitter gibe or taunt.

words.ex: He gave a sardonic smile when she told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当她说出真相时，他露出了讽刺的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as sardonic, you mean they are mocking or scornful in a humorous way.

words.ex: He has a sartorial style that impresses everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种令人印象深刻的服装风格。
words.en: Sartorial relates to tailoring, clothes, or style of dress.

words.tr: v. 充分满足，使饱享； 使厌腻
words.ex: The rich food sated her hunger.
words.ex_cn: 丰盛的食物满足了她的饥饿感。
words.en: To satisfy a desire or an appetite to the full.

words.ex: The satellite sends pictures from space.
words.ex_cn: 卫星从太空发送图片。
words.en: A satellite is an object which has been sent into space in order to collect information or to be part of a communications system. Satellites move continually round the earth or around another planet.

words.tr: v. 使饱足；使厌腻；充分满足
words.ex: The big meal satiated his hunger.
words.ex_cn: 这顿丰盛的饭填饱了他的肚子。
words.en: To satisfy a desire or need fully.

words.ex: The movie is a satire about politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部关于政治家的讽刺作品。
words.en: A way of criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way, especially in order to make a political point, or a piece of writing that uses this style.

words.ex: The cartoon is satirical and makes fun of politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画是讽刺性的，嘲笑政客。
words.en: A satirical piece of writing or speech uses satire to criticize people or ideas.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.tr: adj. 忧郁的；乖戾的；严肃的
words.ex: He has a saturnine mood and rarely smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他情绪阴郁，很少微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as saturnine, you mean that they are serious and unfriendly.

words.tr: n. 萨梯；好色之徒；性欲极强的男人
words.ex: The satyr was depicted as a creature with the body of a man and the legs of a goat.
words.ex_cn: 萨梯被描绘成一个拥有人类身体和山羊腿的生物。
words.en: In Greek mythology, a satyr is a creature that is part man and part goat, known for its association with Dionysus and its love of wine, music, and pleasure.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 闲逛；漫步
words.ex: We decided to saunter along the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定沿着海滩漫步。
words.en: If you saunter somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr: n. 博学之士；大文豪；大学者
words.ex: He is a savant who can solve math problems instantly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位天才，能立即解决数学问题。
words.en: A savant is a person of profound or extensive learning; learned scholar.

words.tr:
v. 品味；细品；享用；体会
n. 风味；滋味
words.ex: He savord the taste of the chocolate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地品味着巧克力的味道。
words.en: To enjoy or appreciate (something) completely.

words.tr:
adj. 咸的；辛辣的；好吃的；好闻的
n. 咸味小吃
words.ex: The savory snack made her thirsty.
words.ex_cn: 这道咸味小吃让她口渴了。
words.en: Savory food is pleasantly salty or spicy and not sweet in taste.

words.ex: He carefully slid the sword into its scabbard.
words.ex_cn: 他小心地把剑插回鞘中。
words.en: A scabbard is a sheath for a sword, dagger, or other similar blade.

words.ex: He caught a scad while fishing at the pier.
words.ex_cn: 他在码头钓鱼时捕到一条竹荚鱼。
words.en: A large number or amount of something.

words.ex: The workers are climbing the scaffold to paint the building.
words.ex_cn: 工人们正在爬脚手架去粉刷大楼。
words.en: A scaffold is a temporary structure erected to support workers and materials during the construction, repair, or cleaning of a building or other large structure. It can also refer to a raised wooden platform used formerly for the public execution of criminals.

words.tr:
n. 规模；等级；比例（尺）；刻度；秤；
v. 改变…大小；
words.ex: The scale of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的规模让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.

words.tr: adj. 欠缺的；过小的；少量的
words.ex: He had scanty food for the whole day.
words.ex_cn: 他一整天的食物很少。
words.en: If something is scanty, there is not enough of it or it is too small in amount.

words.tr:
n. 替罪羊；代人受过者
v. 使…成为替罪羊
words.ex: He was made the scapegoat for the company's financial failures.
words.ex_cn: 他被当作公司财务失败的替罪羊。
words.en: A scapegoat is a person who is blamed for something that someone else has done.

words.tr: v. （在废物中）寻觅；食腐肉；拾荒
words.ex: Dogs scavenge for food in the streets.
words.ex_cn: 狗在街上翻找食物。
words.en: To scavenge means to search for and collect anything usable from discarded waste.

words.tr: n. 可能发生的情况；设想；
words.ex: It's a possible scenario that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天会下雨是一个可能发生的情况。
words.en: A scenario is a description of a possible course of action or events.

words.ex: He drew a simple schematic of the circuit.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个电路的简单示意图。
words.en: A schematic diagram or representation is a simple drawing that uses symbols to show the parts of something and how they are connected.

words.ex: The schism divided the church into two groups.
words.ex_cn: 这个分裂使教会分成了两个群体。
words.en: A schism is a division between people, usually belonging to an organization, movement, or religious denomination, due to a difference in opinion or belief.

words.ex: There was not a scintilla of evidence to support his claim.
words.ex_cn: 没有一丝证据支持他的主张。
words.en: A scintilla is a very small amount or trace of something.

words.tr: v. 闪烁；发火花；焕发才智
words.ex: The diamonds on her necklace scintillated under the light.
words.ex_cn: 她项链上的钻石在灯光下闪闪发光。
words.en: To emit sparks or to sparkle; to twinkle; to be brilliant or lively in conversation or performance.

words.tr:
n. 嘲笑；嘲弄
v. 嘲笑；狼吞虎咽
words.ex: His joke received a scoff from the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话引来了人群的嘲笑。
words.en: If you scoff at something, you speak about it in a way that shows you think it is ridiculous or inadequate.

words.ex: The police scotched the plan to rob the bank.
words.ex_cn: 警察阻止了抢劫银行的计划。
words.en: To scotch something means to stop it from continuing or developing.

words.tr:
n. 灾难；祸患；鞭子
v. 鞭打；折磨；使受苦难
words.ex: Pollution is a scourge on the environment.
words.ex_cn: 污染是对环境的祸害。
words.en: A scourge is something that causes a lot of trouble or suffering, or a whip used as an instrument of punishment.

words.tr:
n. 顾虑；顾忌；踌躇
v. 顾虑；有顾忌
words.ex: He had a scruple about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎感到不安。
words.en: A scruple is a feeling of doubt or hesitation with regard to the morality or propriety of a course of action.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

words.tr:
v. 扭打；混战
n. 扭打；混战
words.ex: The two boys had a scuffle over the ball.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩为了球打了一架。
words.en: A scuffle is a short, confused fight or struggle at close quarters.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁辱骂的；恶语毁谤的；下流粗俗的
words.ex: The politician was criticized for making scurrilous remarks about his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客因对对手发表下流的言论而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something as scurrilous, you mean that it is vulgar and intended to damage someone's reputation.

words.tr:
v. 小步疾走；急赶
n. 快跑声；疾走
words.ex: The mouse scurried under the table.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠迅速跑到了桌子底下。
words.en: If people or small animals scurry somewhere, they move there quickly and hurriedly, especially because they are frightened.

words.ex: Old sailors often got scurvy from lack of fresh fruit.
words.ex_cn: 老水手因缺乏新鲜水果而患上坏血病。
words.en: A disease caused by a deficiency of vitamin C, characterized by spongy and bleeding gums, bleeding under the skin, and extreme weakness.

words.tr:
n. 舷窗；天窗；气窗；煤斗；煤箱
v. 碎步疾跑；急忙撤退；（故意）破坏；凿沉（船）
words.ex: The sailor cleaned the scuttle to let in more light.
words.ex_cn: 水手清洁了舷窗，以便让更多的光线照进来。
words.en: To scuttle means to run hurriedly or furtively with short quick steps. It can also refer to a small opening in a ship's deck or hull, or a container for coal.

words.tr: adj. 污秽的；肮脏丑恶的；恶劣的
words.ex: The seamy side of the entertainment industry was exposed in the documentary.
words.ex_cn: 这部纪录片揭露了娱乐行业丑恶的一面。
words.en: If you describe something as seamy, you mean that it involves unpleasant aspects of life such as crime, prostitution, or violence.

words.tr:
v. 烤焦；烧灼
adj. 烧焦的；枯萎的
n. 烙印；焦痕
words.ex: He sears the steak on the grill.
words.ex_cn: 他在烤架上把牛排煎至表面焦黄。
words.en: To burn or scorch the surface of something with a sudden, intense heat.

words.tr:
adj. 富有经验的；加佐料的；风干的
v. 给 ... 调味；适应；风干；“season”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a seasoned cook with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有多年经验的熟练厨师。
words.en: If someone is seasoned, they have a lot of experience of something and are therefore able to deal with it in a confident way.

words.ex: The secession of the southern states led to the Civil War.
words.ex_cn: 南方各州的脱离导致了内战。
words.en: The action of withdrawing formally from membership of a federation or body, especially a political state.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

words.ex: The gland secrete sweat to cool the body.
words.ex_cn: 腺体分泌汗液来降温。
words.en: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid or substance, it produces it.

words.ex: The sect held unusual beliefs that differed from the main religion.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别的信仰与主流宗教不同。
words.en: A sect is a group of people who have different religious beliefs from other people in the same religion.

words.tr: adj. 世俗的；非宗教的；长期的
words.ex: He lives a secular life without religion.
words.ex_cn: 他过着没有宗教的世俗生活。
words.en: Secular activities, attitudes, or things have no connection with religion.

words.tr:
adj. 安详的；安静的；镇静的
v. 给…服镇静剂
words.ex: The sedate old man sat quietly by the window.
words.ex_cn: 那位安详的老人安静地坐在窗边。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sedate, you mean that they are quiet, calm, and dignified.

words.tr: adj. 需要久坐的；惯于久坐不动的；不爱活动的；
words.ex: His sedentary job makes him sit all day.
words.ex_cn: 他的久坐工作让他整天坐着。
words.en: Someone who has a sedentary lifestyle or job sits down a lot of the time and does not take much exercise.

words.tr: n. 煽动叛乱的言论（或行动）
words.ex: He was arrested for sedition against the government.
words.ex_cn: 他因煽动叛乱反对政府而被逮捕。
words.en: Sedition is the act of encouraging people to oppose or fight against the authority of a state or monarch.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；勤苦工作的
words.ex: He is sedulous in practicing piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天勤奋地练习钢琴。
words.en: If you describe someone as sedulous, you mean that they work hard and pay great attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 多籽的；褴褛的；邋遢的；脏乱的
words.ex: The watermelon has a seedy center.
words.ex_cn: 西瓜的中心有很多籽。
words.en: If you describe a place or person as seedy, you disapprove of them because they look dirty and untidy, or they have a bad reputation.

words.tr: adj. 合适的；得体的；合乎礼仪的
words.ex: He dressed in a seemly way for the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他为了面试穿得得体。
words.en: Seemly behavior or actions are those that are appropriate and suitable for a particular situation.

words.tr:
n. 睡眠；
v. 睡觉；
words.ex: He needs more sleep to feel better.
words.ex_cn: 他需要更多的睡眠来感觉好些。
words.en: Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind is unconscious.

words.tr: v. 沸腾；翻涌；骚动；激昂；大发雷霆
words.ex: The water began to seethe on the stove.
words.ex_cn: 水在炉子上开始沸腾。
words.en: If you say that someone is seething, you mean that they are very angry, but they are trying not to show it.

words.ex: We walked along the Seine at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 我们在日落时沿着塞纳河散步。
words.en: A seine is a type of fishing net that hangs vertically in the water with its bottom edge held down by weights and its top edge buoyed by floats.

words.ex: The seismic wave shook the ground.
words.ex_cn: 地震波震动了地面。
words.en: Seismic means relating to or caused by an earthquake or earth vibration.

words.tr: n. 外观；样子；相似；表象
words.ex: She tried to maintain a semblance of normality.
words.ex_cn: 她试图维持一种正常的假象。
words.en: The outward appearance or apparent form of something, especially when the reality is different.

words.ex: That paper was a seminal work in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 那篇论文是计算机科学领域一部影响深远的著作。
words.en: Seminal is used to describe things such as books, works, events, and people that have a great influence in a particular field.

words.ex: He studied theology at a prestigious seminary.
words.ex_cn: 他在一所著名的神学院学习神学。
words.en: A seminary is a college for training people to become priests or ministers.

words.ex: Her senility made it difficult for her to remember recent events.
words.ex_cn: 她的衰老使她难以记住最近发生的事情。
words.en: Senility refers to the mental and physical decline associated with old age, often characterized by memory loss, confusion, and a decrease in cognitive abilities.

words.ex: The sensitization process allowed the material to react more quickly to light.
words.ex_cn: 敏化过程使材料对光的反应更快。
words.en: Sensitization refers to the process of becoming sensitive or responsive to a particular stimulus or allergen, often leading to an allergic reaction upon subsequent exposures.

words.tr: adj. 感官的；肉欲的；愉悦感官的；耽于肉欲的
words.ex: The sensual smell of fresh bread made her hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的感官香味让她感到饥饿。
words.en: Relating to or involving gratification of the senses and physical, especially sexual, pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 感觉上的；感官的；（引起）美感的
words.ex: She wore a sensuous silk dress.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件性感的丝绸裙子。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the senses rather than the intellect; characterized by a pleasing or luxurious quality that appeals to the senses.

words.tr: adj. 说教的；过分认真的；简洁的；富于警句的
words.ex: His speech was full of sententious remarks.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了简洁精炼的格言。
words.en: If you describe someone as sententious, you mean that they try to appear wise, intelligent, and moral, but in a way that is often perceived as pompous or insincere.

words.tr: adj. 有知觉的；有感觉力的；
words.ex: The robot became sentient and could feel pain.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人变得有知觉，能够感受到疼痛。
words.en: A sentient being is capable of perception or feeling.

words.ex: The sentinel stands guard at the gate.
words.ex_cn: 哨兵站在门口站岗。
words.en: A sentinel is a soldier or guard whose job is to stand and keep watch.

words.tr: adj. 感染病菌的；脓毒性的；败血的；腐败性的
words.ex: The wound became septic after several days.
words.ex_cn: 伤口几天后变得脓毒性。
words.en: relating to or denoting sepsis, especially septicemia.

words.tr: n. 坟墓；圣物置放处; vt. 埋葬
words.ex: The ancient sepulcher was discovered during the excavation.
words.ex_cn: 在挖掘过程中发现了这座古老的坟墓。
words.en: A sepulcher is a burial chamber or tomb, especially one that is large and impressive.

words.ex: The jury was sequestered during the trial.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团在审判期间被隔离。
words.en: To sequester means to isolate or hide away; it can also refer to the legal process of seizing property until a debt is paid or a dispute is resolved.

words.tr:
adj. 干枯的
n. 演替系列
words.ex: The once lush garden had become sere and barren.
words.ex_cn: 曾经郁郁葱葱的花园已经变得干枯荒芜。
words.en: If you describe something as sere, you mean that it is dried up or withered.

words.ex: Finding my lost keys while walking in the park was pure serendipity.
words.ex_cn: 在公园散步时偶然找到了丢失的钥匙，这真是易遇奇缘的运气。
words.en: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.

words.ex: She sits in the garden with serenity.
words.ex_cn: 她坐在花园里，内心平静。
words.en: The state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled.

words.ex: The serpentine road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯弯曲曲的路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: Something that is serpentine is curving and winding in shape, like a snake when it moves.

words.tr:
adj. 锯齿状的；有锯齿的
v. 使成锯齿状；“serrate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The blade of the knife was serrated for cutting bread.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀的刀刃是锯齿状的，适合切面包。
words.en: Having a row of small sharp projections along the edge like a saw.

words.tr: adj. 屈从的；奴隶的；逢迎的
words.ex: He gave a servile answer to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他向老板给出了卑躬屈膝的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as servile, you disapprove of them because they are too eager to obey someone or do things for them.

words.ex: He escaped from servitude and found freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他逃离了奴役，获得了自由。
words.en: The state of being a slave or completely subject to someone more powerful.

words.tr: v. 切断；脱离；切成两段
words.ex: He severed the rope with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀把绳子割断了。
words.en: To sever something means to cut through it or to break it off completely.

words.ex: The severity of the storm caused many power outages.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴的严重性导致了许多停电。
words.en: The severity of something is the degree to which it is serious or severe.

words.ex: The sailor used a sextant to find his position at sea.
words.ex_cn: 水手用六分仪确定他在海上的位置。
words.en: A sextant is an instrument used for measuring angles, especially the angle between the horizon and a celestial body, used in navigation to determine latitude and longitude.

words.tr:
n. 手铐；脚镣；镣铐；束缚物
v. 给...戴上镣铐；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner wore iron shackle on his ankle.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯脚上戴着铁镣。
words.en: A shackle is a pair of metal rings connected by a chain which are fastened around someone's wrists or ankles in order to prevent them from moving or escaping.

words.tr:
n. 假象；假冒者；冒牌货
adj. 虚假的
v. 假装
words.ex: The gift was a sham, not real.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物是假的，不是真的。
words.en: A sham is something that is not what it appears to be and is intended to deceive people.

words.tr:
n. 混乱；一团糟
v. 蹒跚地走；踉跄而行；“shamble”的第三人称单数
words.ex: The room was a complete shambles after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对过后，房间一片狼藉。
words.en: A state of total disorder.

words.ex: He stepped on a shard of broken glass.
words.ex_cn: 他踩到了一块碎玻璃片。
words.en: A shard is a piece of broken glass, pottery, or metal.

words.tr: n. 刮胡须； v. “shave”的现在分词；
words.ex: He does his shaving every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上刮胡须。
words.en: The act of removing hair from the face or body using a razor.

words.ex: The farmer tied the sheaf of wheat with rope.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用绳子把一束小麦捆在一起。
words.en: A sheaf is a bundle of grain stalks laid lengthwise and tied together after reaping.

words.tr: v. （将刀剑）入鞘；放进套里；包；覆盖
words.ex: He sheathes his knife after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后把刀收进刀鞘。
words.en: To put something, especially a weapon, into a sheath; to cover or protect something with a sheath.

words.ex: She enjoyed a refreshing scoop of raspberry sherbet.
words.ex_cn: 她享受了一勺清爽的覆盆子冰冻果子露。
words.en: A sweet frozen dessert made from fruit juice, sugar, and water, often with milk or cream added.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；发微光
n. 微光；闪光
words.ex: The lake shimmers under the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 湖面在月光下闪烁。
words.en: To shine with a soft, slightly wavering light.

words.ex: He shirks his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天逃避作业。
words.en: If someone shirks their duties or responsibilities, they deliberately avoid doing them.

words.tr: adj. 劣质的；次品的；卑劣的
words.ex: He bought a shoddy chair that broke after one day.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一把劣质的椅子，一天就坏了。
words.en: If you describe something as shoddy, you mean that it has been done or made carelessly or badly.

words.ex: The shrew ran quickly under the leaves.
words.ex_cn: 鼩鼱在树叶下快速奔跑。
words.en: A shrew is a small, mouse-like mammal with a pointed snout, or it can refer to a bad-tempered or aggressively assertive woman.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的；
words.ex: He made a shrewd decision to buy the house low.
words.ex_cn: 他精明地决定低价买下这栋房子。
