words.en: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.tr:
v. 使转轨；使分流；转向一边
n. 转轨；分流器
words.ex: The train was shunted to a side track.
words.ex_cn: 火车被调到了侧线。
words.en: If a train or a railway carriage is shunted, it is moved from one track to another, usually in order to make space for another train or carriage.

words.tr: n. 手段卑鄙的人；不择手段的律师
words.ex: He was known as a shyster who would do anything to win a case.
words.ex_cn: 他以不择手段赢得官司而臭名昭著。
words.en: A shyster is a person, especially a lawyer, who uses unethical or tricky methods in business or legal matters.

words.ex: My sibling plays soccer every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我的兄弟/姐妹每个周末都踢足球。
words.en: A sibling is a brother or sister.

words.ex: The sibylline prophecy left the townspeople in awe.
words.ex_cn: 女巫的预言让镇上的人们感到敬畏。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a sibyl; prophetic or oracular.

words.ex: The star's position is measured in sidereal time.
words.ex_cn: 这颗恒星的位置用恒星时测量。
words.en: Relating to the stars or constellations; measured by the apparent motion of the stars.

words.ex: The river deposited silt on the banks.
words.ex_cn: 河流在河岸上沉积了淤泥。
words.en: Silt is fine sand, soil, or mud which is carried along by a river and then left on the land.

words.tr:
adj. 类人猿的；像猴的
n. 类人猿；猴
words.ex: The simian climbed quickly up the tree.
words.ex_cn: 那只猿猴迅速爬上了树。
words.en: Relating to, resembling, or being a monkey or ape.

words.ex: He used a simile to compare her eyes to stars.
words.ex_cn: 他用了明喻把她的眼睛比作星星。
words.en: A simile is a figure of speech that directly compares two different things, usually by employing the words 'like' or 'as'.

words.tr:
n. 傻笑；假笑；痴笑
v. 傻笑；假笑；痴笑
words.ex: She simpered at him, trying to catch his attention.
words.ex_cn: 她对他假笑，试图引起他的注意。
words.en: To smile in a silly or affected way, often to appear more attractive or to hide one's true feelings.

words.ex: His answer was too simplistic.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答太简单化了。
words.en: If you describe something as simplistic, you disapprove of it because it is so simple that it ignores important details or difficulties.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.tr: n. 工作清闲但报酬优厚的职位；闲职；美差
words.ex: He got a sinecure in the government office.
words.ex_cn: 他在政府部门得到了一个闲职。
words.en: A sinecure is a position requiring little or no work but giving the holder status or financial benefit.

words.tr: adj. （多）肌腱的；坚韧的；肌肉强壮有力的
words.ex: He had a sinewy build, with muscles that stood out clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他肌肉发达，肌肉线条清晰可见。
words.en: Having or consisting of sinews; muscular and strong.

words.tr: adj. 单个的；单数的；特异的；
words.ex: Each singular student must submit a form.
words.ex_cn: 每个学生都必须提交一份表格。
words.en: In grammar, singular means relating to or being a form of a word that refers to one person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 邪恶的；险恶的；不祥的
words.ex: The old house looked sinister in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 那座老房子在月光下显得阴森可怖。
words.en: Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.

words.ex: The river has a sinuous path through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河在森林中蜿蜒流淌。
words.en: Something that is sinuous has many smooth turns and curves.

words.tr: n. 怀疑论者；怀疑宗教主张的人；无神论者
words.ex: He is a skeptic about new health claims.
words.ex_cn: 他对新的健康说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: A skeptic is a person who questions the validity or authenticity of something purporting to be factual.

words.tr: n. 小艇；小型帆船；小船
words.ex: They rowed the skiff across the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他们划着小艇穿过湖面。
words.en: A skiff is a small, light boat for rowing or sailing, typically for one person.

words.tr: v. 舍不得给；节省；克扣
words.ex: She skimped on the ingredients to save money.
words.ex_cn: 她为了省钱，在食材上克扣。
words.en: To skimp means to spend less time, money, or effort on something than is really needed, often resulting in a lower quality outcome.

words.ex: He was known as a skinflint who never spent a penny on anything.
words.ex_cn: 他以吝啬鬼著称，从不为任何东西花一分钱。
words.en: A skinflint is someone who is extremely unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: The snake slithered through the grass.
words.ex_cn: 蛇在草丛中滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and quietly with a twisting or oscillating motion, like a snake.

words.ex: The sloth moves very slowly in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 树懒在树上移动得非常慢。
words.en: Sloth is a disinclination to work or exert oneself; laziness, or a slow-moving tropical American mammal that lives in trees.

words.ex: He is slothful and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他懒惰，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as slothful, you mean that they are lazy.

words.ex: The snake sloughs its skin every year.
words.ex_cn: 蛇每年都会蜕皮。
words.en: A slough is an area of soft, muddy ground, especially a marshy area by a river or lake. As a verb, it means to shed or cast off a layer of dead skin, a shell, or an old layer of tissue.

words.tr: adj. 不修边幅的；邋遢的
words.ex: He wore slovenly clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着邋遢的衣服去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as slovenly, you disapprove of them because they are careless and untidy in their appearance or habits.

words.tr: n. 游手好闲的人；懒鬼
words.ex: He was known as a sluggard who never contributed to the household chores.
words.ex_cn: 他以游手好闲著称，从不帮忙做家务。
words.en: A sluggard is someone who is habitually lazy or idle.

words.ex: The turtle moves in a sluggish way.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟移动得很缓慢。
words.en: If you describe something as sluggish, you mean that it is moving or working more slowly than usual.

words.tr:
n. 闸门
v. 冲洗
words.ex: The sluice gate was opened to release the water.
words.ex_cn: 水闸门被打开以释放水流。
words.en: A sluice is a channel that is used to control the flow of water, especially in a river or a stream. It can also mean to wash or rinse something with a large amount of water.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr:
n. 浅薄的知识；一知半解；微量
v.  充内行；“smatter”的现在分词
words.ex: He has a smattering of knowledge in many subjects.
words.ex_cn: 他在许多科目上只有一知半解的知识。
words.en: A smattering of something is a small amount of it or a few things about it.

words.tr:
v. 熔炼；冶炼
v. 嗅；闻；散发气味；察觉；“smell”的过去式和过去分词
n. 胡瓜鱼
words.ex: They smelt iron ore to make steel.
words.ex_cn: 他们熔炼铁矿石来制造钢铁。
words.en: To smelt means to extract metal from ore by a process involving heating and melting.

words.tr:
n. 傻笑；假笑
v. 傻笑；自鸣得意地笑
words.ex: He gave a smirk when he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛时露出了冷笑。
words.en: A smirk is a smile expressing smugness or scorn instead of pleasure.

words.tr:
v. 闷烧；冒烟；郁积
n. 闷烧
words.ex: The fire still smolders in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 火还在壁炉里闷烧。
words.en: To burn slowly with smoke but without flame, or to exist in a suppressed state.

words.tr:
v. 窃笑
n. 窃笑
words.ex: She couldn't help but snicker at the joke.
words.ex_cn: 她忍不住对那个笑话窃笑。
words.en: To laugh in a half-suppressed, typically scornful way.

words.tr:
v. 吸鼻子；流鼻涕；啜泣
n. 吸鼻子；流鼻涕；啜泣
words.ex: He keeps sniveling about his broken toy.
words.ex_cn: 他一直哭哭啼啼地说他的玩具坏了。
words.en: If someone snivels, they cry or sniff in a way that irritates you.

words.tr: n. 清醒；镇定；严肃；节制
words.ex: He values sobriety after his accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后重视清醒。
words.en: The state of being sober, especially in terms of not being under the influence of alcohol.

words.ex: The sodden clothes stuck to her skin.
words.ex_cn: 湿透的衣服贴在她的皮肤上。
words.en: Something that is sodden is extremely wet.

words.ex: His sojourn in Paris lasted two years.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎旅居了两年。
words.en: A sojourn is a temporary stay in a place.

words.ex: Her hug gave me solace after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 在失去亲人后，她的拥抱给了我安慰。
words.en: Solace is comfort that you feel when you are consoled in times of disappointment or sadness.

words.tr:
n. 焊料；焊锡
v. 焊接；焊合
words.ex: He used solder to fix the broken wire.
words.ex_cn: 他用焊料修理了断掉的电线。
words.en: Solder is a fusible metal alloy used to create a permanent bond between metal workpieces.

words.tr: n. 违反语法；文法错误；举止失礼
words.ex: He made a solecism when he said 'between you and I'.
words.ex_cn: 当他说出'between you and I'时，犯了一个语法错误。
words.en: A solecism is a grammatical mistake in speech or writing, or a breach of etiquette.

words.ex: The solemnity of the ceremony made everyone quiet.
words.ex_cn: 仪式的庄重让所有人都安静了下来。
words.en: The state or quality of being serious and dignified.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

words.tr: adj. 关怀的；切望的；惦记的；悬虑的
words.ex: He was solicitous about her health.
words.ex_cn: 他非常关心她的健康。
words.en: If you are solicitous, you are very concerned about someone's safety, health, or comfort.

words.ex: He spoke a soliloquy alone on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他独自在舞台上说了一段独白。
words.en: A soliloquy is a speech in a play in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, often when they are alone on stage.

words.ex: He enjoys solitude in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在森林中独处。
words.en: The state or situation of being alone.

words.ex: The solstice happens in June and December.
words.ex_cn: 夏至和冬至分别发生在六月和十二月。
words.en: The solstice is the time of the year when the sun is at its greatest distance from the celestial equator, occurring around June 21 and December 21.

words.ex: Salt is soluble in water.
words.ex_cn: 盐可以溶于水。
words.en: A substance that is soluble can be dissolved in a liquid.

words.ex: Water is a common solvent for salt.
words.ex_cn: 水是盐的常见溶剂。
words.en: A solvent is a substance that can dissolve other substances, or a person or company that has enough money to pay their debts.

words.tr: adj. 躯体的；肉体的；体细胞的
words.ex: The doctor checked his somatic symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的躯体症状。
words.en: Relating to the body, especially as distinct from the mind.

words.tr: adj.  忧郁的；阴沉的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room had a somber mood.
words.ex_cn: 房间里有一种阴郁的气氛。
words.en: If someone is somber, they are serious or sad.

words.tr: n. 梦游者；梦游症患者
words.ex: The somnambulist walked in his sleep.
words.ex_cn: 这个梦游者在睡梦中行走。
words.en: A somnambulist is a person who walks around while they are asleep.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: The somnolent boy nodded off during class.
words.ex_cn: 那个昏昏欲睡的男孩在课堂上睡着了。
words.en: If you are somnolent, you feel sleepy.

words.tr: adj. 深沉响亮的；洪亮的
words.ex: The bell rang with a sonorous sound.
words.ex_cn: 钟发出洪亮的声音。
words.en: A sonorous sound is deep, full, and rich, often pleasing to the ear.

words.ex: The ancient Sophists were known for their teachings on rhetoric and philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 古希腊的诡辩家以其修辞学和哲学教导而闻名。
words.en: A sophist is a person who uses clever but false arguments, especially in order to deceive people.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.ex: His argument was full of sophistry, making it difficult to discern the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点充满了诡辩，让人难以分辨真相。
words.en: Sophistry is the use of clever but false arguments, especially with the intention of deceiving.

words.tr: adj. 二年级学生的；一知半解的；自信但幼稚浅薄的
words.ex: His sophomoric remarks showed a lack of depth in understanding.
words.ex_cn: 他一知半解的评论显示了他理解上的浅薄。
words.en: If you describe something as sophomoric, you mean that it is silly and immature, often in a way that is typical of a young person who is trying to be clever or funny.

words.tr:
adj. 催眠的；让人瞌睡的
n. 安眠药
words.ex: The monotonous lecture was so soporific that I couldn't keep my eyes open.
words.ex_cn: 那个单调乏味的讲座让我昏昏欲睡，眼睛都睁不开了。
words.en: A soporific substance or activity makes you feel sleepy.

words.tr: adj. 卑鄙的；污秽的；肮脏的
words.ex: He made a sordid deal to cheat his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一笔卑鄙的交易来欺骗他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as sordid, you mean that it is very immoral or dishonest.

words.tr:
n. 闪光塑料片；亮晶晶的金属片
v. 用闪光片布满（或装饰）
words.ex: The dress is covered with spangle.
words.ex_cn: 这件裙子上布满了亮片。
words.en: A spangle is a small piece of shiny material used for decoration, especially on clothing.

words.ex: The village has a sparse population.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄人口稀少。
words.en: Something that is sparse is small in number or amount and spread out over an area.

words.ex: He lives a spartan life with little food and no luxuries.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，食物很少，也没有奢侈品。
words.en: If you describe something as spartan, you mean that it is very simple and not at all luxurious, often because it is intended to be useful or practical rather than attractive.

words.tr: adj. 痉挛的；间歇的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had spasmodic coughing at night.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上有阵发性的咳嗽。
words.en: Something that is spasmodic happens suddenly and irregularly, often in short periods of time.

words.tr: v. 吐；“spit”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The cat spat out the pill.
words.ex_cn: 猫把药丸吐了出来。
words.en: A spat is a short, usually minor, argument or disagreement.

words.tr: n. 泛滥；猛涨；大批；一连串
words.ex: A spate of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴雨淹没了街道。
words.en: A spate of things, especially unpleasant ones, is a large number of them that happen or appear within a short period of time.

words.ex: He has good spatial skills for drawing maps.
words.ex_cn: 他画地图有很好的空间能力。
words.en: Relating to or occupying space.

words.tr: n. 抹刀；调色刀；刮勺；刮铲
words.ex: He flipped the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子翻了煎饼。
words.en: A spatula is a tool with a broad, flat, flexible blade used for mixing, spreading, and lifting materials.

words.ex: The fish spawn in the river each spring.
words.ex_cn: 鱼每年春天在河里产卵。
words.en: To spawn means to produce or deposit eggs, especially in large quantities, as fish, frogs, etc. do. It can also mean to give rise to or generate something.

words.tr: adj. 似是而非的；貌似有理的
words.ex: His argument is specious and misleading.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点看似有理但具有误导性。
words.en: Something that is specious seems to be good, sound, or correct but is actually wrong or false.

words.ex: The spectral lines show the elements in the star.
words.ex_cn: 光谱线显示了恒星中的元素。
words.en: Relating to or suggesting a spectrum; especially relating to or suggesting a ghost.

words.ex: The colors in the rainbow cover a wide spectrum.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹中的颜色覆盖了广泛的范围。
words.en: A spectrum is a range of a particular type of thing, often a range of colors, ideas, or opinions.

words.tr:
adj. 乱花钱的；挥霍的
n. 浪费金钱的人；挥金如土的人
words.ex: He is a spendthrift who buys things he doesn't need.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乱花钱的人，买很多不需要的东西。
words.en: A spendthrift is someone who spends money in an extravagant, irresponsible way.

words.ex: The old man sat sphinx-like, saying nothing.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人像斯芬克斯一样坐着，一言不发。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a sphinx; enigmatic or mysterious.

words.tr:
v. 捻接；粘接；结合
n. 粘接处；绞接处
words.ex: He spliced the two ropes together.
words.ex_cn: 他把两根绳子捻接在一起。
words.en: To join or unite (ropes or rope ends) by interweaving the strands.

words.ex: His spontaneity made the party fun.
words.ex_cn: 他的自发性让派对变得有趣。
words.en: The condition of being spontaneous; impulsive or natural action or behavior.

words.ex: He said 'flamingo' instead of 'flying machine'—that was a spoonerism.
words.ex_cn: 他说了'flamingo'而不是'flying machine'——那是一个首音互换。
words.en: A spoonerism is a mistake in speech in which the initial sounds or letters of two or more words are accidentally swapped, often with a humorous effect.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.tr: adj. 爱玩的；嬉戏玩笑的；喜爱运动的
words.ex: He is sportive and loves playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他很有运动精神，喜欢打篮球。
words.en: If you describe someone as sportive, you mean that they are lively and enjoy playing games or sports.

words.tr:
n. 云杉；云杉木
adj. 整洁漂亮的
v. 弄整洁；打扮漂亮
words.ex: The forest is full of tall spruce trees.
words.ex_cn: 森林里长满了高大的云杉树。
words.en: A spruce is a type of evergreen tree with needle-like leaves. As an adjective, it describes something neat and trim in appearance. As a verb, it means to make someone or something neat and smart in appearance.

words.tr: adj. 活泼的；敏捷的；充满生气的
words.ex: The old man is still spry and walks fast.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人仍然身手敏捷，走得很慢。
words.en: Someone who is spry, especially an older person, is lively and active.

words.tr: adj. 假的；伪造的；欺骗性的；谬误的
words.ex: The data is spurious and cannot be trusted.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据是虚假的，不可信。
words.en: Something that is spurious seems to be genuine, but is false.

words.ex: He spurned the offer because it was too low.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个提议，因为报酬太低。
words.en: If you spurn someone or something, you reject them with contempt.

words.tr:
n. 争吵
v. 争吵
words.ex: The two boys squabble over toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天为玩具争吵。
words.en: A squabble is a noisy disagreement about something unimportant.

words.tr: n. 肮脏；污秽；恶劣条件
words.ex: The family lived in squalor with no clean water.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭生活在肮脏的环境中，没有干净的水。
words.en: A state of being extremely dirty and unpleasant, especially as a result of poverty or neglect.

words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.tr:
v. 蹲；蹲坐；擅自占住
n. 蹲；偷住的房子；蹲坐
adj. 矮而宽的；矮胖的
words.ex: He does a squat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做深蹲。
words.en: If you squat, you lower yourself towards the ground, balancing on your feet with your legs bent.

words.tr:
adj. 断音的；不连贯的
adv. 断音地；不连贯地
n. 断奏；断续的一段音乐
words.ex: The piano played staccato notes.
words.ex_cn: 钢琴弹奏了断奏的音符。
words.en: In music, staccato is a method of playing notes in a detached, separated manner, as opposed to legato.

words.ex: The water in the pond was stagnant.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里的水不流动。
words.en: If something such as a business or economy is stagnant, there is little activity or change.

words.ex: He is a staid man who never wears casual clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个古板的人，从不穿休闲服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as staid, you mean that they are serious, dull, and rather old-fashioned.

words.tr:
n. 僵局；和棋；僵持状态
v. 使陷入僵局
words.ex: The two players are in a stalemate.
words.ex_cn: 两位选手陷入了僵局。
words.en: A situation in which further action or progress by opposing parties seems impossible.

words.ex: He is a stalwart of the environmental movement.
words.ex_cn: 他是环保运动的坚定分子。
words.en: A stalwart person is someone who is very loyal and committed to a person, belief, or cause and is not likely to change their views or behavior.

words.ex: He has great stamina for running long distances.
words.ex_cn: 他有很强的耐力来跑长距离。
words.en: Stamina is the physical or mental energy needed to do a tiring activity for a long time.

words.tr:
v. （使）止血；使不漏
adj. 不透水的；坚固的；坚强的；忠实的
words.ex: He tried to stanch the bleeding with a cloth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一块布止血。
words.en: To stop the flow of a liquid, especially blood, from a wound.

words.ex: The poem has four stanzas.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有四节。
words.en: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem that are separated from other groups by a space.

words.ex: The car remained static at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在红灯前静止不动。
words.en: Something that is static does not move or change.

words.ex: The statute says drivers must stop at red lights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律规定司机必须在红灯时停车。
words.en: A statute is a formal written law of a country or state, enacted by its legislative authority.

words.tr: adj. 法定的；依照法规的；
words.ex: The statutory minimum wage is $10 per hour.
words.ex_cn: 法定最低工资是每小时10美元。
words.en: Statutory means relating to rules or laws which have been formally written down.

words.ex: He is steadfast in his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念坚定不移。
words.en: If someone is steadfast, they are very loyal and constant in their attitudes or actions.

words.tr: n. 秘密行动；偷偷摸摸
words.ex: The cat moved in stealth to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫悄悄地移动去抓老鼠。
words.en: Stealth is the action of moving or behaving in a secretive way in order to avoid being noticed.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.ex: He gave a stellar performance in the play.
words.ex_cn: 他在剧中表现出色。
words.en: Of or relating to stars; outstanding or excellent.

words.tr:
n. 茎；词干；
v. 起源于(~ from)；
words.ex: The flower grows on a long green stem.
words.ex_cn: 花长在一根长长的绿色茎上。
words.en: The main body or stalk of a plant or shrub, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean; to stop or restrict (the flow of something).

words.ex: His love of music stems from his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的热爱源于他的童年。
words.en: If a condition or problem stems from something, it was caused originally by that thing.

words.tr: adj. 洪亮的；声音极大的
words.ex: His stentorian voice filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 他洪亮的声音充满了整个房间。
words.en: A stentorian voice is very loud and powerful.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.ex: He is a stickler for punctuality.
words.ex_cn: 他是个对守时非常严格的人。
words.en: A stickler is someone who insists on a certain quality or type of behavior.

words.ex: The smoke began to stifle her breathing.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾开始让她窒息。
words.en: To stifle something means to prevent it from happening, continuing, or developing.

words.ex: He felt the stigma of being unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了失业的耻辱。
words.en: A stigma is a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something, especially when this is unfair.

words.tr:
adj. 生硬的；不自然的
v. 用高跷行走；“stilt”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His stilted speech made everyone feel uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他僵硬的演讲让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If someone's way of speaking, writing, or behaving is stilted, they speak, write, or behave in a formal or unnatural way, for example because they are not relaxed.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.ex: He receives a small stipend for his internship.
words.ex_cn: 他因实习获得少量薪金。
words.en: A stipend is a sum of money paid regularly as a salary or allowance.

words.ex: He stipple the paper with small dots.
words.ex_cn: 他用小点点缀了纸张。
words.en: To stipple means to paint, engrave, or draw by means of dots or small touches.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr:
n. 库存；股票；家畜；
v. 备有；贮存；
words.ex: The store has low stock of winter coats.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的冬衣库存很少。
words.en: The supply of goods available for sale in a store; the capital raised by a company through the issue of shares.

words.tr:
n. 栅栏；围栏
v. 用栅栏围住；用栅栏防卫
words.ex: The prisoners were locked in a wooden stockade.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯们被关在木制栅栏里。
words.en: A stockade is a defensive barrier made from upright wooden posts or stakes, especially as a temporary defense against attack.

words.tr: adj. 难消化的，使人胀饱的；古板的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The stodgy pudding made him feel full and uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这道难消化的布丁让他感到胀满不适。
words.en: If you describe something as stodgy, you mean that it is dull, boring, and rather formal.

words.tr:
n. 斯多葛派人；坚忍克己之人；
adj. 斯多葛派的；坚忍克己的；
words.ex: He is a stoic who never shows his emotions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个从不流露情感的斯多葛派人。
words.en: Someone who is stoic does not show their feelings or complain when bad things happen to them.

words.ex: The speech stoked anger among the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲激起了人群的愤怒。
words.en: To stoke a fire means to add fuel to it to make it burn more strongly. It can also mean to encourage or increase strong feelings or emotions.

words.tr: adj. 不动声色的；无动于衷的；不易激动的
words.ex: He remained stolid in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 面对逆境，他依然冷漠。
words.en: If you describe someone as stolid, you mean that they do not show much emotion or are not very exciting or interesting.

words.ex: The general used a clever stratagem to win the battle.
words.ex_cn: 将军使用了一个巧妙的战略赢得了战斗。
words.en: A stratagem is a plan or scheme, especially one used to outwit an opponent or achieve an end.

words.tr: adj. 分层的；形成阶层的；分为不同等级的; v. 使成层（stratify 的过去分词）
words.ex: The class is stratified by age groups.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级按年龄组进行分层。
words.en: Arranged in layers or strata.

words.tr: n. 岩层；地层；社会阶层
words.ex: The geologist examined the stratum for fossils.
words.ex_cn: 地质学家检查了岩层以寻找化石。
words.en: A stratum is a layer of material, naturally or artificially formed, often one of a number of parallel layers one upon another.

words.ex: The wind strews leaves on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得满地都是。
words.en: To scatter or spread things untidily over a surface or area.

words.tr: adj. 有条纹的；有条痕的
words.ex: The rock had a striated surface, showing layers of different minerals.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石的表面有条纹，显示了不同矿物的层理。
words.en: Marked with striae; striped or grooved.

words.tr:
n. 结构；建筑物；
v. 组织；
words.ex: The structure of the bridge is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
words.en: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.tr:
n. 撑杆；支柱
v. 趾高气扬地走；昂首阔步
words.ex: The bridge has metal struts to support the weight.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有金属撑杆来支撑重量。
words.en: If someone struts, they walk in a proud way, with their chest out and trying to look important.

words.tr: v. 研究；学习；“study”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He studied the behavior of birds in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他研究了森林中鸟类的行为。
words.en: If you describe something as studied, you mean that it is deliberate and planned, rather than natural or spontaneous.

words.tr: v. 使无效；使显得愚蠢
words.ex: The boring meeting stultifies his creativity.
words.ex_cn: 这个无聊的会议扼杀了他的创造力。
words.en: To stultify someone or something means to cause them to appear foolish or to be ineffective.

words.tr: v. 使惊呆；使惊愕；使神志不清
words.ex: The sudden noise stupefied everyone.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: To stupefy someone means to make them unable to think clearly or to be surprised or shocked.

words.tr: n. 昏迷；不省人事；恍惚
words.ex: He fell into a stupor after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，他陷入了昏迷状态。
words.en: A state of near-unconsciousness or insensibility.

words.ex: The stygian cave was dark and cold.
words.ex_cn: 那个阴森的洞穴又黑又冷。
words.en: extremely dark, gloomy, or forbidding

words.ex: The rain stymied our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨水阻碍了我们去远足的计划。
words.en: To stymie someone or something means to prevent them from achieving their aims.

words.ex: His suavity made everyone feel comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他的温文尔雅让每个人都感到舒适。
words.en: Suavity is the quality of being suave, which means being smoothly agreeable and polite.

words.tr:
n. 中尉；副官
adj. 副的
words.ex: The subaltern followed the officer's order.
words.ex_cn: 下级士兵遵从了军官的命令。
words.en: A subaltern is someone who has a lower rank or position in an organization, especially in the armed forces.

words.tr:
adj. 柔和的；减弱的；郁郁不乐的
v. 征服；克制；制服；“subdue”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The room had subdued lights.
words.ex_cn: 房间里灯光柔和。
words.en: If a color or light is subdued, it is not very bright.

words.ex: His opinion is subjective and not based on facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点是主观的，不是基于事实的。
words.en: Based on or influenced by personal feelings, tastes, or opinions.

words.ex: The king tried to subjugate the rebels.
words.ex_cn: 国王试图征服叛乱者。
words.en: To subjugate a country or group of people means to take complete control of them, especially by defeating them in a war.

words.tr:
v. （使）升华；使净化
adj. 升华的；纯化的
words.ex: He tries to sublimate his anger into art.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把愤怒升华成艺术。
words.en: To sublimate means to transform something, especially a strong emotion or desire, into a more positive or acceptable form, often through a process of refinement or elevation.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.tr: adj. 下意识的；潜意识的；
words.ex: The ad used subliminal messages to influence buyers.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告使用了下意识的信息来影响买家。
words.en: Subliminal refers to something that is below the threshold of sensation or consciousness; it is perceived by or affecting someone's mind without their being aware of it.

words.tr: adj. 顺从的；服从的；恭顺的；
words.ex: The submissive dog waited quietly for its owner's command.
words.ex_cn: 这只顺从的狗安静地等待主人的命令。
words.en: If you are submissive, you obey someone without arguing.

words.ex: His opinion is subordinate to the manager's.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见比经理的次要。
words.en: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.

words.tr: v. 教唆；收买；贿赂某人作伪证
words.ex: He tried to suborn a witness with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱收买证人。
words.en: To induce someone to commit an unlawful or wrongful act, especially to give false testimony in court.

words.tr:
v. 以传票传唤；传讯
n. 传票
words.ex: The court subpoenaed the witness to appear next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 法院传唤证人下周一出庭。
words.en: A subpoena is a legal document ordering someone to attend a court of law and give evidence as a witness.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.tr: adj. 卑屈的；恭顺的；次要的；从属的
words.ex: He is subservient to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的老板唯命是从。
words.en: If you are subservient, you do whatever someone wants you to do.

words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: The government gives a subsidy to farmers.
words.ex_cn: 政府向农民提供补贴。
words.en: A subsidy is money that is paid by a government or other authority in order to help an industry or business, or to pay for a public service.

words.ex: He works hard to earn his subsistence.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以维持生计。
words.en: Subsistence is the condition of just having enough food or money to stay alive.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 本质上的；实质性的；
words.ex: The change was substantive, not just cosmetic.
words.ex_cn: 这个改变是本质上的，而不仅仅是表面上的。
words.en: Something that is substantive is significant, meaningful, or important in a way that is not just superficial or formal.

words.ex: The rule subsumes all similar cases.
words.ex_cn: 这个规则涵盖所有类似的情况。
words.en: If something is subsumed within a larger group or class, it is included within it, rather than being considered as something separate.

words.ex: He used subterfuge to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用遁词来避免回答问题。
words.en: Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal.

words.ex: The subtlety of her smile made everyone curious.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的微妙之处让所有人都感到好奇。
words.en: The quality of being subtle, especially in a way that is difficult to notice or understand.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.tr:
n. 救援；援助者
v. 救援
words.ex: The nurse gave succor to the injured man.
words.ex_cn: 护士向受伤的男人提供了援助。
words.en: Succor is assistance and support given to someone in times of hardship or distress.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.tr: n. 主张妇女参政的人
words.ex: She was a suffragist who fought for women's right to vote.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位为女性争取投票权而斗争的女权运动者。
words.en: A suffragist is someone who campaigns for the right to vote, especially for women.

words.tr: v. 弥漫于；充满；扩散；布满
words.ex: The sunset suffuses the sky with orange light.
words.ex_cn: 日落将天空染成橙色。
words.en: If something such as a colour, emotion, or light suffuses a person or thing, it gradually spreads over or through them.

words.ex: He sullied his reputation by lying.
words.ex_cn: 他通过撒谎玷污了自己的声誉。
words.en: To sully something means to spoil or reduce the value of something, especially someone's reputation or the purity of something.

words.tr: adj. 闷热的；性感的；撩人的
words.ex: The sultry weather made everyone feel tired.
words.ex_cn: 闷热的天气让每个人都感到疲惫。
words.en: Sultry weather is hot and damp in a way that makes you feel uncomfortable.

words.ex: The summation of all the evidence was that he was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 所有证据的结论是他无罪。
words.en: A summation is a summary or the act of summarizing, especially in a legal context where it refers to the final argument made by an attorney at the end of a trial.

words.ex: The king ate a sumptuous meal in his palace.
words.ex_cn: 国王在他的宫殿里享用了一顿丰盛的饭菜。
words.en: Something that is sumptuous is very impressive and expensive, especially in a way that involves large amounts of money.

words.ex: The storm sundered the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树劈开了。
words.en: To break or split apart, especially along a natural line or grain.

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；杂七杂八的
words.ex: He bought sundry items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了各种物品。
words.en: If someone refers to sundry people or things, they are referring to several people or things that are all different from each other.

words.tr:
adj. 领取退休金而退休的；过时的
v. 因年老而辞退；给养老金使…退休；“superannuate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The superannuated teacher still works part-time.
words.ex_cn: 这位退休的老师仍然兼职工作。
words.en: Too old to be effective or useful, especially in the context of employment.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；目空一切的；自大的
words.ex: He gave a supercilious smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is supercilious, you disapprove of them because they behave in a way that shows they think they are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 职责以外的；多余的
words.ex: His extra help was supererogatory, since the job was already done.
words.ex_cn: 他的额外帮助是多余的，因为工作已经完成了。
words.en: Supererogatory actions are those that go beyond what is required or expected, often considered morally commendable but not obligatory.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.tr: v. 置于某物之上；添加
words.ex: He superimposes a map on the photo.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图叠加在照片上。
words.en: To superimpose something means to place or lay one thing over another, typically so that both are still evident.

words.tr:
adj. 多余的；额外的
n. 定额以外的人；临时雇工
words.ex: He is a supernumerary teacher at the school.
words.ex_cn: 他是学校里一名额外的老师。
words.en: A supernumerary person or thing is one that is extra or more than the usual number.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.ex: He lay supine on the couch, staring at the ceiling.
words.ex_cn: 他仰卧在沙发上，盯着天花板。
words.en: If you are supine, you are lying on your back. It can also describe someone who is passive or not willing to act.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr: adj. 柔软的；灵活的；思维敏捷的
words.ex: The yoga teacher has supple legs.
words.ex_cn: 瑜伽老师腿很柔软。
words.en: A supple object or material bends or changes shape easily without breaking or cracking.

words.tr:
adj. 恳求的
n. 恳求者
words.ex: The suppliant knelt before the king.
words.ex_cn: 恳求者在国王面前跪下。
words.en: A suppliant is someone who asks for something in a very humble or earnest way, often by kneeling or bowing.

words.ex: He supplicated for mercy.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求宽恕。
words.en: to ask for something in a humble way; to beg earnestly and humbly

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.tr: adj. 假想的；冒充的；想像的
words.ex: The supposititious child was not his real son.
words.ex_cn: 那个被假称是他的孩子并不是他的亲生儿子。
words.en: Supposititious is used to describe something that is assumed or supposed to be true, but may not be, or something that is not genuine but is presented as such.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；乖戾的；傲慢的
words.ex: The surly man refused to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 那个脾气暴躁的人拒绝打招呼。
words.en: If someone is surly, they are unfriendly and bad-tempered.

words.tr:
v. 臆测；猜想
n. 臆测；猜度
words.ex: He surmises that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you surmise that something is true, you guess it from the available evidence, although you do not know for certain.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；鬼鬼祟祟的；偷偷摸摸的
words.ex: He gave a surreptitious glance at his phone during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时偷偷瞥了一眼手机。
words.en: If something is done surreptitiously, it is done secretly, often because it would not be approved of.

words.tr:
adj. 代理的；代用的
n. 代理人；代用品
words.ex: He acted as a surrogate father to the child.
words.ex_cn: 他作为孩子的代理父亲。
words.en: A surrogate is a person or thing that takes the place of or acts for another, especially in a role or function that is typically filled by someone else.

words.ex: The police used surveillance to watch the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用监视来观察那栋大楼。
words.en: The careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected.

words.ex: Children are susceptible to colds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子容易感冒。
words.en: If you are susceptible to something or someone, you are very likely to be influenced by them.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.tr: n. 食物；营养；维持生计
words.ex: Water and food are basic sustenance for life.
words.ex_cn: 水和食物是生命的基本生存物资。
words.en: Sustenance refers to the food and drink that people, animals, and plants need to live and stay healthy. It can also mean the means of maintaining life or supporting existence.

words.tr:
n. 缝线；缝合处
v. 缝合（伤口）
words.ex: The doctor used a suture to close the wound.
words.ex_cn: 医生用缝合线缝合了伤口。
words.en: A suture is a stitch or row of stitches holding together the edges of a wound or surgical incision.

words.ex: He has a swarthy complexion from working outside.
words.ex_cn: 他因在户外工作而皮肤黝黑。
words.en: Having a dark complexion or skin color, especially as a result of exposure to the sun.

words.tr:
v. 用布包裹；用绷带缠
n. 长而宽的一长条；割刈的带状地
words.ex: She swathed the baby in a soft blanket.
words.ex_cn: 她用一条柔软的毯子把婴儿裹起来。
words.en: To wrap or bind in or as if in a bandage or cloth.

words.tr:
v. 热得难受；中暑
n. 热昏；中暑
words.ex: He swelters in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 他在烈日下热得难受。
words.en: If you swelter, you are very uncomfortable because the weather is extremely hot.

words.tr:
v. 突然转向；改变方向
n. 转向
words.ex: He swerved to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为了避开狗而转向。
words.en: If a vehicle or other moving thing swerves, it suddenly changes direction, often in order to avoid hitting something.

words.tr:
v. 冲洗；灌洗；涮；大口喝
n. 涮；冲洗；痛饮；泔水
words.ex: He drank the swill from the old bucket.
words.ex_cn: 他喝掉了旧桶里的脏水。
words.en: To drink something quickly and in large amounts, or to wash something by pouring large amounts of water over or through it.

words.tr: n. 骗子；江湖骗子；诈骗犯
words.ex: The swindler tricked old people with fake promises.
words.ex_cn: 这个骗子用虚假的承诺欺骗了老人。
words.en: A swindler is someone who swindles, that is, someone who cheats or tricks someone else out of money or property.

words.tr: n. 好享受的人；贪图安逸的人
words.ex: He is a sybarite who loves luxury foods and soft beds.
words.ex_cn: 他是个享乐主义者，喜欢美味的食物和柔软的床。
words.en: A sybarite is someone who loves luxury and pleasure and tends to live a life of indulgence.

words.tr: n. 阿谀奉承的人；谄媚者；马屁精
words.ex: He is a sycophant who always agrees with his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是附和老板的马屁精。
words.en: A sycophant is someone who praises powerful or rich people in an insincere way in order to get an advantage.

words.tr: n. 三段论法；推论法；演绎
words.ex: He used a syllogism to prove his point.
words.ex_cn: 他用三段论来证明他的观点。
words.en: A syllogism is a form of reasoning in which a conclusion is drawn from two given or assumed propositions (premises); a common or middle term is present in the two premises but not in the conclusion, which is deduced from the premises.

words.tr:
adj. 森林的
n. 森林中的人或物
words.ex: The sylvan path was quiet and green.
words.ex_cn: 这条林间小路安静而翠绿。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of woods or forest regions.

words.ex: Bees and flowers have symbiosis.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂和花朵之间有共生关系。
words.en: Symbiosis is a close relationship between two different kinds of living things in which each provides something that the other needs.

words.ex: The butterfly has perfect symmetry.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶有完美的对称性。
words.en: Symmetry is the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other or around an axis.

words.tr: adj. 同时发生的；同步的；
words.ex: The two events happened synchronous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.ex: He gave a synoptic view of the history.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史做了概括性的概述。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a synopsis; presenting a summary or general view of a whole.

words.ex: The synthesis of ideas helped solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这些想法的综合帮助解决了问题。
words.en: The act of combining different ideas, influences, or objects into a new and coherent whole.

words.ex: The shirt is made of synthetic fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫是合成纤维制成的。
words.en: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words T

words.tr: adj. 心照不宣的；不作声的
words.ex: They have a tacit understanding about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们对规则有一种心照不宣的理解。
words.en: If you refer to someone's tacit agreement or approval, you mean they are agreeing to something or approving it without actually saying so, often because they are unwilling to admit to doing so.

words.ex: He is taciturn and rarely speaks.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默寡言，很少说话。
words.en: A taciturn person does not say very much and can seem unfriendly.

words.tr: adj. 触觉的；能触知的；手感好的
words.ex: The child learns through tactile objects like blocks.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过触觉物体如积木来学习。
words.en: Relating to the sense of touch; perceptible by touch.

words.tr:
n. 污染；腐坏；玷污
v. 污染；使腐坏；玷污
words.ex: The water has a taint from the factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这种水因工厂废料而受到污染。
words.en: If something is tainted, it is affected by something bad or undesirable.

words.tr: n. 护身符；驱邪物；能产生奇迹的东西；法宝
words.ex: He wears a talisman for good luck.
words.ex_cn: 他戴一个护身符以求好运。
words.en: A talisman is an object which is believed to have magic powers to protect its owner or to bring good luck.

words.ex: The eagle gripped the rabbit with its talon.
words.ex_cn: 老鹰用它的爪子抓住了兔子。
words.en: The claw of a bird of prey.

words.ex: His comment was tangential to the main topic.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论离题了。
words.en: If you describe something as tangential, you mean that it has only a slight or indirect connection with the thing you are concerned with, and is therefore not worth considering seriously.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

words.ex: He works as a tanner in a small town.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个小镇上做皮革工。
words.en: A tanner is a person whose job is to tan animal hides to make leather.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可及之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of cookies tantalize him.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.ex: The child threw a tantrum when he couldn't get what he wanted.
words.ex_cn: 孩子因为得不到想要的东西而发脾气。
words.en: A tantrum is an uncontrolled outburst of anger and frustration, typically in a young child.

words.tr: v. 逐渐变细；逐渐减少；
words.ex: The candle tapers toward the top.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛向顶部逐渐变细。
words.en: A taper is a long thin candle or a gradual decrease in width or thickness.

words.ex: The tarantula is a large, hairy spider known for its venomous bite.
words.ex_cn: 狼蛛是一种体型大、多毛的蜘蛛，以其毒性咬伤而闻名。
words.en: A tarantula is a large and often hairy spider which is found mainly in tropical and subtropical regions. Some species can be kept as pets.

words.tr:
adj. 用柏油覆盖的
v. 耽搁；逗留
words.ex: The workers tarry at the road, waiting for the asphalt to dry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在道路上耽搁，等着沥青变干。
words.en: To tarry means to stay longer than intended or to delay leaving a place.

words.tr: adj. 不整洁的；破烂的；简陋的
words.ex: The room was in tatty condition, with peeling wallpaper and broken furniture.
words.ex_cn: 房间状况很破旧，墙纸剥落，家具损坏。
words.en: If you describe something as tatty, you mean that it is in poor condition or of poor quality.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.tr: adj. 同义反复的；类语叠用的
words.ex: The statement was tautological and added no new information.
words.ex_cn: 这个陈述是同义反复的，没有提供新的信息。
words.en: If you describe something as tautological, you mean that it is a tautology or is like a tautology.

words.tr: adj. 俗丽而不值钱的；花里胡哨的
words.ex: She wore a tawdry dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一件俗丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as tawdry, you mean that it is showy and bright but of very poor quality.

words.ex: The taxonomist meticulously categorized the specimens.
words.ex_cn: 分类学者一丝不苟地对标本进行了分类。
words.en: A taxonomist is a scientist who specializes in the classification of organisms into groups on the basis of their structure, origin, behavior, etc.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.ex: The church promotes teetotalism as a way to maintain spiritual purity.
words.ex_cn: 教会提倡绝对禁酒，以此来保持精神上的纯洁。
words.en: Teetotalism is the practice or promotion of complete personal abstinence from alcoholic beverages.

words.ex: He showed great temerity by challenging the expert without any preparation.
words.ex_cn: 他没有做任何准备就挑战专家，显得非常鲁莽。
words.en: If you say that someone has the temerity to do something, you are annoyed about something they have done which you think took a lot of nerve.

words.tr:
n. 暴躁脾气；情绪；心情；性情
v. 使…缓和；冲淡
words.ex: He loses his temper when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会发脾气。
words.en: If you refer to someone's temper or say that they have a temper, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.ex: His calm temperament helps him stay peaceful in stress.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的性情让他在压力下保持平和。
words.en: Your temperament is your basic nature, especially as it is shown in the way that you react to situations or to other people.

words.ex: He is a temperate person who never shouts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个温和的人，从不大喊大叫。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as temperate, you mean that it is calm and reasonable, not extreme or emotional.

words.tr: adj. 有狂风暴雨的；狂暴的
words.ex: The tempestuous sea made the voyage dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨的海面使得航行变得危险。
words.en: If you describe a relationship or a situation as tempestuous, you mean that it is full of strong emotions, especially anger or passion.

words.ex: The drummer changed the tempo of the song.
words.ex_cn: 鼓手改变了这首歌的拍子。
words.en: The speed at which a piece of music is played or the rate or speed of motion or activity.

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.tr: v. 敷衍；拖延；见风驶舵
words.ex: He decided to temporize until he had more information.
words.ex_cn: 他决定拖延时间，直到获得更多信息。
words.en: To temporize means to delay making a decision or giving a definite answer in order to gain time or avoid committing oneself.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.ex: His tenacity helped him finish the marathon despite the pain.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚韧让他即使疼痛也完成了马拉松。
words.en: The quality or fact of being able to grip something firmly; the quality or fact of being very determined and not giving up easily.

words.tr: adj. 倾向性的；有偏见的；有争议的
words.ex: The media's tendentious reporting often misrepresents the truth.
words.ex_cn: 媒体的带有倾向性的报道常常歪曲事实。
words.en: If something is tendentious, it expresses a particular opinion or point of view very strongly, especially one that many people disagree with.

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.ex: The rope has high tensile strength.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子有很高的抗拉强度。
words.en: relating to tension; capable of being stretched or drawn out

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.tr: adj. 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
words.ex: He drank the tepid water slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地喝着温吞的水。
words.en: Slightly warm; lukewarm. Also, showing little enthusiasm.

words.ex: The termination of the contract surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 合同的终止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The act of ending something or the end of something.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.ex: The train stops at the terminus.
words.ex_cn: 火车在终点站停下。
words.en: A terminus is the end of a transportation line or the station at the end of a railway or bus route.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.

words.ex: Her terse reply left no room for further discussion.
words.ex_cn: 她简洁的回答没有留下进一步讨论的余地。
words.en: A terse statement or comment is brief and to the point, often seeming rude or unfriendly because of its brevity.

words.tr: adj. 第三的；高等教育的
words.ex: He works in the tertiary sector as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他作为一名教师在第三产业工作。
words.en: In the context of an economy, the tertiary sector is the part of the economy that provides services rather than producing goods. In geology, the Tertiary period is a former term for the period of time now called the Paleogene and Neogene periods, which followed the Cretaceous period.

words.tr: adj. 棋盘格状的；镶嵌的花样的；“tessellate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The floor was covered with a tessellated pattern of tiles.
words.ex_cn: 地板上铺满了镶嵌成棋盘花纹的瓷砖。
words.en: Something that is tessellated is decorated with a pattern of small squares or blocks of different colors, arranged in a regular pattern.

words.ex: The will of the testator was contested by his heirs.
words.ex_cn: 立遗嘱者的遗嘱被他的继承人质疑。
words.en: A person who has made a will or given a testament.

words.ex: He became testy when he was asked about his past.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及他的过去时，他变得易怒。
words.en: If someone is testy, they are easily annoyed and impatient.

words.tr:
n. 系绳；系链；界限
v. 用绳拴住
words.ex: The horse was tied to the post with a tether.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马被用拴绳系在了柱子上。
words.en: A tether is a rope or chain used to tie an animal to a post or other fixed point so that it cannot move away.

words.ex: The movie has a thematic focus on friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的主题聚焦于友谊。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a theme or themes.

words.ex: The theocracy ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 神权政体以铁腕统治。
words.en: A theocracy is a form of government in which a deity is recognized as the supreme civil ruler, the deity's laws being interpreted by ecclesiastical authorities.

words.ex: He is learning theoretical physics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习理论物理。
words.en: A theoretical study or explanation is based on or uses the ideas and abstract principles of a subject, rather than the practical aspects or uses of it.

words.ex: The therapeutic massage helped her relax.
words.ex_cn: 这种治疗性的按摩帮助她放松了。
words.en: If something is therapeutic, it helps you to relax or to feel better about things, especially if you have been feeling worried or upset.

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.ex: He has a thespian talent for acting.
words.ex_cn: 他有戏剧表演的天赋。
words.en: Relating to drama and the theater; an actor or actress.

words.ex: He was held in thrall by his addiction.
words.ex_cn: 他被他的瘾所束缚。
words.en: If you say that someone is in thrall to a person or thing, you mean that they are completely in their power or are greatly influenced by them.

words.ex: His coat is threadbare from many years of use.
words.ex_cn: 他的外套因为用了多年而变得破旧。
words.en: Worn out by overuse; shabby and old.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.ex: He was in the throes of a difficult decision.
words.ex_cn: 他正处在艰难抉择的痛苦中。
words.en: If someone is experiencing something very unpleasant or emotionally painful, you can say that they are in the throes of it.

words.tr:
n. 人群；一大群；众多
v. 群集；挤满；涌进
words.ex: A throng of people waited outside the store.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人站在商店外面等候。
words.en: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals.

words.ex: The mechanic checked the throttle on the car engine.
words.ex_cn: 机械师检查了汽车发动机的节流阀。
words.en: To throttle someone means to kill or injure them by squeezing their throat or tightening something around it and preventing them from breathing. A throttle is a device that controls the amount of fuel going into an engine.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.tr: n. 吝啬鬼；小气鬼；守财奴
words.ex: He was known as a tightwad who never spent a penny unnecessarily.
words.ex_cn: 他以吝啬鬼闻名，从不花不必要的钱。
words.en: A tightwad is a person who is very reluctant to spend money; a miser.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；谄媚
n. 谄媚者；马屁精
words.ex: He was always the first to toady to the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他总是第一个拍老板马屁的人。
words.en: A toady is someone who flatters or ingratiates themselves with someone else in order to gain advantage.

words.ex: The senator wore his toga with pride.
words.ex_cn: 这位参议员自豪地穿着他的宽外袍。
words.en: A toga is a loose flowing outer garment worn by the citizens of ancient Rome, made of a single piece of cloth wrapped around the body.

words.tr: n. 大部头的书；大册书
words.ex: He read a large tome about ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于古代历史的厚书。
words.en: A tome is a large, heavy book, especially one dealing with a serious topic.

words.tr:
n. 削发仪式
v. 削发
words.ex: The monk received his tonsure as part of his ordination.
words.ex_cn: 这位僧侣在受戒仪式中接受了削发。
words.en: The act of shaving the head or part of the head, especially as a religious rite or as a sign of entering a monastic order.

words.ex: The map shows the topography of the mountain area.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山区的地形。
words.en: The topography of an area is the physical features of its surface, such as hills, valleys, and rivers, especially the representation of these features on maps.

words.ex: The cold weather put the animal into torpor.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的天气让动物陷入麻木状态。
words.en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy.

words.ex: The engine produces a lot of torque.
words.ex_cn: 发动机产生很大的扭矩。
words.en: Torque is a twisting force that causes rotation.

words.ex: The rain caused a torrent down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨在山间形成了一股急流。
words.en: A torrent is a fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.

words.tr: adj. 炎热的；炽热的；情欲强烈的
words.ex: The torrid sun burned the dry land.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的太阳炙烤着干涸的土地。
words.en: If you describe something as torrid, you mean that it is very hot and dry.

words.ex: The statue has a strong torso.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像有一个强壮的躯干。
words.en: The main part of the human body, not including the head, arms, or legs.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.tr: v. 蹒跚；踉跄；摇摇欲坠
words.ex: The old man totters when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人走路时摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move in a feeble or unsteady way.

words.ex: His first book is a touchstone for modern writers.
words.ex_cn: 他的第一本书是现代作家的典范。
words.en: A touchstone is a criterion or standard by which something is judged or recognized.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难以处理的；敏感的
words.ex: He is touchy about his weight.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己体重很敏感。
words.en: If you describe someone as touchy, you mean that they are easily upset, offended, or irritated.

words.tr: v. 兜售；招徕；吹捧；倒卖（高价票）
words.ex: He touts the new phone as the best on the market.
words.ex_cn: 他吹捧这款新手机是市场上最好的。
words.en: If someone touts something, they try to sell it or convince people that it is good, especially in an aggressive or exaggerated way.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.tr: n. 大片土地；体内管道；
words.ex: The farmer owns a large tract of land near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民拥有靠近河边的一大片土地。
words.en: A tract is a large area of land or a system of connected organs in the body.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.ex: He can translate words into pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他能把词语转化为图画。
words.en: To translate means to change written or spoken words from one language into another, or to explain something in a way that is easier to understand.

words.ex: The ball followed a smooth trajectory.
words.ex_cn: 球沿着一条平滑的轨迹飞行。
words.en: The path followed by a projectile flying or an object moving under the action of given forces.

words.ex: The lake offers tranquillity after a long day.
words.ex_cn: 湖水在漫长的一天后带来宁静。
words.en: Tranquillity refers to a state of peace and quiet.

words.tr: adj. 超越的；杰出的；卓越的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was transcendent.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是超凡的。
words.en: If you describe something as transcendent, you mean that it is extremely good or impressive, often in a way that goes beyond the ordinary.

words.ex: The lab technician transcribes the DNA sequence into RNA.
words.ex_cn: 实验室技术员将DNA序列转录成RNA。
words.en: To transcribe something means to write it down or to copy it from one form of recording to another.

words.tr: v. 使变形；使改观；美化
words.ex: The makeup artist transfigured the actress for the role.
words.ex_cn: 化妆师为演员的角色进行了改观。
words.en: To transform into something more beautiful or elevated.

words.ex: He committed a transgression by stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了过错。
words.en: A transgression is an act that goes against a law, rule, or code of conduct; an offense.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.ex: The wizard can transmute lead into gold.
words.ex_cn: 巫师可以把铅变成金子。
words.en: To change something completely, especially into something different and better.

words.ex: The glass is transparent.
words.ex_cn: 这玻璃是透明的。
words.en: If something is transparent, you can see through it.

words.tr: v. 蒸发；排出；为人所知；发生
words.ex: Water transpires from the leaves in hot weather.
words.ex_cn: 水在炎热的天气中从叶子中蒸发。
words.en: If it transpires that something has happened, this previously secret or unknown fact becomes known.

words.tr:
n. 运输；
v. 运输；
words.ex: He uses public transport to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐公共交通去上班。
words.en: To transport something or someone is to move them from one place to another, especially over long distances.

words.tr: n. 服饰；马饰；装饰；外部标志
words.ex: He wore the trappings of a judge during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上穿上了法官的服饰。
words.en: The trappings of a particular role or job are the extra things, such as titles and ceremonies, that go with it but are not necessary to it.

words.tr: adj. 造成创伤的；痛苦的；不愉快的
words.ex: The car accident was a traumatic experience.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次创伤性的经历。
words.en: If something is traumatic, it causes you severe emotional distress and anxiety.

words.tr:
n. 艰辛；艰苦劳动；痛苦；分娩的阵痛
v. 辛苦工作；发生或经受阵痛
words.ex: His travail helped him succeed in the end.
words.ex_cn: 他的艰辛最终让他取得了成功。
words.en: Travail refers to painful or laborious effort, especially in the context of work or childbirth.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr:
n. 滑稽拙劣的模仿；嘲弄；歪曲
v. 滑稽化；嘲弄
words.ex: The trial was a travesty of justice.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判是对正义的嘲弄。
words.en: If you describe something as a travesty of another thing, you mean that it is a very bad representation of that other thing.

words.ex: He wrote a treatise on ancient Chinese philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于中国古代哲学的专著。
words.en: A treatise is a formal and systematic written discourse on some subject, generally longer and more detailed than an essay.

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a strong tremor in the building.
words.ex_cn: 地震使大楼发生了强烈的震动。
words.en: A tremor is a small earthquake or a shaking or vibrating movement, especially one caused by fear or nervousness.

words.tr: adj. 颤抖的；战栗的；畏缩的
words.ex: Her voice was tremulous when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时声音颤抖。
words.en: If someone's voice, smile, or actions are tremulous, they are unsteady because the person is uncertain, afraid, or upset.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.ex: The tribulations of war left many families devastated.
words.ex_cn: 战争的苦难使许多家庭陷入了绝望。
words.en: A tribulation is a cause of great trouble or suffering.

words.ex: The tribunal decided the case quickly.
words.ex_cn: 法庭迅速作出了裁决。
words.en: A tribunal is a special court or committee that is officially chosen to examine a particular problem or situation.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.tr: n. 三叉戟；三叉戟式飞机
words.ex: The statue held a trident in its right hand.
words.ex_cn: 雕像的右手握着一把三叉戟。
words.en: A trident is a three-pronged spear, especially as an attribute of Poseidon (Neptune) or Britannia.

words.tr:
adj. 微不足道的；无关紧要的
v. 闹着玩；玩弄；“trifle”的现在分词
words.ex: He ignored the trifling mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个微不足道的错误。
words.en: If you describe something as trifling, you mean that it is unimportant or insignificant.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.ex: He watched the Harry Potter trilogy last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他上周末看了《哈利·波特》三部曲。
words.en: A trilogy is a series of three books, plays, or films that have the same subject or the same characters.

words.tr: n. 小装饰品；廉价首饰
words.ex: She bought a small trinket at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买了一个小饰物。
words.en: A trinket is a small ornament or item of jewelry that is of little value.

words.ex: His speech was full of trite phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了陈腐的表达。
words.en: If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite, you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.

words.tr: n. 琐事；微不足道的东西；各种科目知识
words.ex: He loves to share trivia at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在晚餐时分享冷知识。
words.en: Trivia refers to unimportant matters or pieces of information that are considered to be of little value or significance.

words.ex: He gave his troth to her in a traditional ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个传统仪式上向她许下了诺言。
words.en: Faithfulness, fidelity, or loyalty, especially in a pledge or promise; also, a betrothal.

words.ex: The pig eats from the wooden trough.
words.ex_cn: 猪从木槽里吃东西。
words.en: A long, narrow open container for animals to eat or drink from; a period of low economic activity.

words.ex: The truculence of the opponent's team was evident in their aggressive play.
words.ex_cn: 对手球队的好战性在他们激烈的比赛中显而易见。
words.en: The quality of being eager or quick to argue, fight, or start a conflict; aggressiveness.

words.tr: n. 自明之理；不言而喻的道理；老生常谈
words.ex: It is a truism that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 水在100摄氏度沸腾，这是一个不言而喻的事实。
words.en: A truism is a statement that is obviously true and says nothing new or interesting.

words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.tr: n. 约会；幽会；幽会地点
words.ex: They met at a secret tryst in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们在树林里一个秘密的地方相会。
words.en: A tryst is a secret meeting between lovers.

words.tr: adj. 肿大的；肿胀的；浮夸的
words.ex: His tumid face looked swollen after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 他的脸在被昆虫叮咬后显得肿胀。
words.en: Swollen or distended; pompous or bombastic in style.

words.tr: n. 骚动；骚乱；心烦意乱
words.ex: The crowd caused a tumult after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，人群引起了混乱。
words.en: A tumult is a state of confusion, noise, and excitement, often involving a large group of people.

words.ex: Reindeer live in the tundra near the North Pole.
words.ex_cn: 驯鹿生活在北极附近的苔原上。
words.en: A tundra is a vast, flat, treeless Arctic region of Europe, Asia, and North America in which the subsoil is permanently frozen.

words.ex: The soup was served in a beautiful tureen.
words.ex_cn: 汤被盛在一只漂亮的盖碗里。
words.en: A tureen is a large, deep, covered dish from which soup is served.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words U

words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.ex: His ulterior motive was to get money.
words.ex_cn: 他别有用心，目的是弄到钱。
words.en: If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.ex: He gave an ultimatum: leave now or stay forever.
words.ex_cn: 他发出最后通牒：现在走，或者永远留下。
words.en: An ultimatum is a final demand or statement of terms, the rejection of which will result in retaliation or a breakdown in relations.

words.ex: We sat under the umbrage of the big tree.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在大树的树荫下。
words.en: A feeling of pique or resentment at some often fancied slight or insult.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；不能理解的；无责任的
words.ex: The manager made unaccountable decisions.
words.ex_cn: 这位经理做出了无法解释的决定。
words.en: If someone or something is unaccountable, there is no way of explaining why they behave in a particular way, and it is often strange or surprising.

words.tr: n. 一致同意；全体赞同
words.ex: The team showed unanimity in voting for the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队在投票支持新计划时意见一致。
words.en: Unanimity is complete agreement among all members of a group.

words.tr: adj. 无可争辩的；攻不破的；不容置疑的
words.ex: His alibi is unassailable.
words.ex_cn: 他的不在场证明是无可置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something such as a person's reputation or an argument as unassailable, you mean that it cannot be criticized or attacked because it is completely right or true.

words.tr: adj. （愤怒等强烈情绪）未平息的；（人）未安静下来的；（肉体或精神上的痛苦）未减轻的，未缓和的；...
words.ex: Her grief remained unassuaged despite all efforts to comfort her.
words.ex_cn: 尽管尽了所有努力安慰她，她的悲伤依然未减轻。
words.en: If a feeling such as desire or need is unassuaged, it has not been satisfied or lessened.

words.tr: adj. 不装腔作势的；低调谦逊的；
words.ex: He is an unassuming man who never talks about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不装腔作势的人，从不谈论自己的成就。
words.en: If you describe someone as unassuming, you approve of them because they are quiet and do not try to appear important.

words.tr: adj. 无辔头的；不受控制的；放纵的
words.ex: The unbridled horse ran across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹无辔头的马在田野上奔跑。
words.en: If you describe behaviour or feelings as unbridled, you mean that they are not controlled or limited in any way.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.tr: adj. 违背良心的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: The prices they were charging were unconscionable.
words.ex_cn: 他们收取的价格是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe something as unconscionable, you mean that it is morally unacceptable, often because it is too large, too extreme, or too severe.

words.ex: He made an uncouth remark at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚餐时说了句粗俗的话。
words.en: If you describe a person as uncouth, you mean that their behavior is vulgar, rude, or socially unacceptable.

words.ex: He spoke with great unction about the importance of the event.
words.ex_cn: 他非常津津有味地谈论着这个活动的重要性。
words.en: A religious or ceremonial anointing with oil, often as part of a sacrament or ritual.

words.tr: adj. 假情假义的；油腔滑调的
words.ex: His unctuous manner made me uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他油腔滑调的态度让我感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as unctuous, you are critical of them because they seem to be full of praise, kindness, or interest, but in a way that is not sincere.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；潜在的； v. “underlie”的现在分词；
words.ex: The underlying cause of the problem is poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的根本原因是贫困。
words.en: An underlying thing is the thing that is the most important or basic, although it is not easily noticed or stated directly.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr:
adj. 波动的；起伏的
v. 使波动；使起伏；“undulate”的现在分词
words.ex: The road is undulating through the hills.
words.ex_cn: 这条路在山丘间起伏蜿蜒。
words.en: Moving with a smooth wavelike motion.

words.ex: They unearthed an old coin in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们在花园里挖出了一枚旧硬币。
words.en: To unearth something means to find it by digging in the ground or to discover something that was hidden or unknown.

words.tr: adj. 非尘世的；怪异的；可怕的；时间过早或不便的
words.ex: The unearthly glow of the northern lights was mesmerizing.
words.ex_cn: 北极光那神秘的光辉令人着迷。
words.en: If you describe something as unearthly, you mean that it seems strange and unnatural, not like anything that exists in the natural world.

words.tr: adj. 毫不含糊的；清楚明白的
words.ex: His answer was unequivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答是明确无误的。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude as unequivocal, you mean that it is completely clear and very firm.

words.ex: She unerringly picked the correct answer.
words.ex_cn: 她毫无差错地选择了正确答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's judgement or ability as unerring, you mean that they are always correct and never make mistakes.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的
words.ex: Her performance was unexceptionable.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现无可挑剔。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unexceptionable, you mean that they are unlikely to be criticized or objected to, because they are very good, standard, or normal.

words.ex: She maintained an unfaltering gaze throughout the presentation.
words.ex_cn: 她在整个演讲过程中始终保持坚定的目光。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behaviour as unfaltering, you mean that it is strong and firm and does not weaken.

words.ex: He showed unfeigned joy when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 当他赢得奖品时，他表现出真诚的喜悦。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or actions as unfeigned, you mean that they are genuine and not pretended.

words.tr: adj. 无拘束的；无牵挂的
words.ex: She felt an overwhelming sense of unfettered freedom.
words.ex_cn: 她感到一种无拘无束的自由感。
words.en: If you describe something as unfettered, you mean that it is not controlled or limited by anyone or anything.

words.tr: adj. 羽毛未丰的；未充分发达的；未成熟的
words.ex: The company is still unfledged and needs more time to grow.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司仍然羽翼未丰，需要更多时间来成长。
words.en: not yet fledged or having feathers; immature

words.tr: v. 脱去…的法衣；免去…的圣职
words.ex: The priest was unfrocked for his misconduct.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧师因行为不端而被解除僧职。
words.en: To remove someone from their position as a priest or minister, especially as a punishment.

words.ex: The ungainly boy tripped over his own feet.
words.ex_cn: 这个笨拙的男孩被自己的脚绊倒了。
words.en: If you describe a person, animal, or vehicle as ungainly, you mean that they look awkward or clumsy, often because they are big.

words.ex: She applied a soothing unguent to the wound.
words.ex_cn: 她在伤口上涂了一种舒缓的药膏。
words.en: A soft greasy or viscous substance used as an ointment or for lubrication.

words.ex: The rules show uniformity in all schools.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则在所有学校中都保持一致。
words.en: The state or quality of being uniform; consistency.

words.ex: The country made a unilateral decision to close the border.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家单方面决定关闭边境。
words.en: Involving only one group or country.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的；可靠的
