words.ex: His unimpeachable honesty earned everyone's trust.
words.ex_cn: 他无可挑剔的诚实赢得了每个人的信任。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimpeachable, you mean that they are completely honest and reliable.

words.tr: adj. 不受约束的；无拘无束的
words.ex: He sang uninhibited at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上毫无拘束地唱歌。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as uninhibited, you mean that they express their opinions and feelings openly, and behave as they want to, without worrying what other people think.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: The team acted in unison to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 团队一致行动赢得了比赛。
words.en: If two or more people do something in unison, they do it together at the same time.

words.ex: This rule is universal for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则对所有学生都是普遍适用的。
words.en: Something that is universal affects or relates to every part of the world or the universe.

words.tr: adj. 不整洁的；凌乱的；不修边幅的
words.ex: Her hair was unkempt and her clothes were disheveled.
words.ex_cn: 她的头发蓬乱，衣服也凌乱不堪。
words.en: If you describe someone's hair or appearance as unkempt, you mean that it is untidy or messy.

words.tr: adj. 没有减轻的；十足的；绝对的
words.ex: The criticism was unmitigated and harsh.
words.ex_cn: 批评是全然的严厉。
words.en: If you describe something as unmitigated, you are emphasizing that it is completely bad or good, without any qualification.

words.ex: The door handle was unobtrusive and blended with the wall.
words.ex_cn: 门把手不显眼，与墙壁融为一体。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unobtrusive, you mean that they are not easily noticed or do not draw attention to themselves.

words.tr: adj. 味道不好的；让人不快的；难以接受的；
words.ex: The soup was unpalatable and too salty.
words.ex_cn: 这汤味道不好，太咸了。
words.en: If you describe an idea as unpalatable, you mean that you find it unpleasant and difficult to accept.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.tr: adj. 不讨人喜欢的；不吸引人的；
words.ex: He has an unprepossessing appearance, but he is very kind.
words.ex_cn: 他外表不讨人喜欢，但他非常善良。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unprepossessing, you mean that they look rather plain or ordinary, and not at all impressive or attractive.

words.ex: He unraveled the knotted string.
words.ex_cn: 他把打结的绳子拆散了。
words.en: To unravel means to separate or disentangle the threads of a fabric or a rope, or to solve or explain something that is complicated or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 没有回报的；无报酬的；有仇未报的；单方面的
words.ex: She suffered from unrequited love for many years.
words.ex_cn: 多年来，她一直承受着单恋之苦。
words.en: If you say that something such as love or affection is unrequited, you mean that it is not returned by the person it is directed towards.

words.tr: adj. 不守规矩的；难控制的；难管束的
words.ex: The unruly child refused to sit quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这个不守规矩的孩子不肯安静地坐着。
words.en: If you describe people, especially children, as unruly, you mean that they behave badly and are difficult to control.

words.tr: adj. 味道不佳的；令人讨厌的；声名狼藉的；不道德的
words.ex: The fish had an unsavory smell.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unsavory, you mean that they are unpleasant or morally unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 没有受伤的；未受损害的；
words.ex: He walked away from the crash unscathed.
words.ex_cn: 他从车祸中安然无恙地走开了。
words.en: If someone is unscathed after a dangerous experience, they have not been injured or harmed by it.

words.tr: adj. 不体面的；不相配的；不适宜的
words.ex: It is unseemly to shout in a library.
words.ex_cn: 在图书馆大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that someone's behaviour is unseemly, you disapprove of it because it is not appropriate in a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 难看的；不悦目的；不雅观的
words.ex: The construction site was an unsightly mess.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地看起来一片狼藉，很不雅观。
words.en: If you describe something as unsightly, you mean that it is unattractive to look at.

words.ex: The lake remains unsullied by pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这片湖泊没有受到污染，依然纯净。
words.en: If something is unsullied, it remains clean and pure, not spoiled or made dirty by anything.

words.tr: adj. 难以捍卫的；站不住脚的；不堪一击的
words.ex: His excuse was untenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口站不住脚。
words.en: If an argument, theory, or position is untenable, it cannot be defended or supported against criticism.

words.tr: adj. 不利的；麻烦的；异常的；意外的；棘手的
words.ex: He faced untoward remarks from his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他遭到了同学的不友好的评论。
words.en: If you say that something is untoward, you mean that it is unexpected and causes difficulties.

words.tr: adj. 自由的；不受约束的
words.ex: She felt an untrammeled sense of freedom while hiking in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中徒步时感受到了一种无拘无束的自由感。
words.en: Not limited or restricted; free.

words.tr: adj. 不合理的；没有根据的；无端的
words.ex: The teacher gave an unwarranted warning.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个没有理由的警告。
words.en: If you describe something as unwarranted, you are critical of it because there is no need or reason for it.

words.tr: adj. 笨重的；难处理的；臃肿的；庞大的
words.ex: The box was unwieldy and hard to carry.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子又大又笨重，很难搬。
words.en: An unwieldy object is difficult to move or handle because of its size, shape, or weight.

words.tr: adj. 不知情的；不经意的
words.ex: He was the unwitting victim of a prank.
words.ex_cn: 他是不知情的恶作剧受害者。
words.en: If someone is unwitting, they do not know or realize something.

words.ex: He made an unwonted silence during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上出乎意料地保持了沉默。
words.en: Not usual or common; unusual.

words.ex: She upbraided him for his carelessness.
words.ex_cn: 她因他的粗心大意而责骂他。
words.en: To criticize or reproach severely; to scold.

words.tr: adj. 喧嚣的；吵闹的；令人捧腹大笑的
words.ex: The party became uproarious as the night went on.
words.ex_cn: 随着夜晚的深入，派对变得喧嚣起来。
words.en: If something is uproarious, it is very noisy and loud, often because people are laughing or shouting.

words.ex: The upshot of the meeting was a new plan.
words.ex_cn: 会议的结果是一个新计划。
words.en: The final result or outcome of a situation or event.

words.tr: adj. 温文儒雅的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: He is an urbane man who speaks politely.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个举止文雅、说话有礼貌的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as urbane, you mean that they are polite, confident, and comfortable in social situations.

words.tr: n. 顽童；淘气鬼；小乞丐；海胆
words.ex: The little urchin stole an apple from the market.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽童从市场上偷了一个苹果。
words.en: An urchin is a small child who is dirty and poorly dressed, or a sea creature with a round shell covered with sharp points.

words.ex: The ursine creature lumbered through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 那只熊一样的生物笨拙地穿过森林。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of bears.

words.ex: He tried to usurp the throne from his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从他兄弟手中篡夺王位。
words.en: If you say that someone usurps a job, role, title, or position, they take it from someone when they have no right to do this.

words.ex: He paid high usury on his loan.
words.ex_cn: 他支付了高额的高利贷。
words.en: The practice of lending money at an exorbitant interest rate.

words.ex: He dreams of a perfect utopia where everyone is happy.
words.ex_cn: 他梦想一个每个人都很幸福的完美乌托邦。
words.en: An imagined place or state of things in which everything is perfect.

words.tr: adj. 过分宠爱妻子的；怕老婆的
words.ex: He was known for his uxorious nature, always putting his wife's needs before his own.
words.ex_cn: 他以怕老婆著称，总是把妻子的需求放在自己的需求之前。
words.en: If you describe a man as uxorious, you mean that he is extremely fond of his wife and shows it in his behavior towards her.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words V

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: The vagabond sleeps under the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪汉睡在桥下。
words.en: A vagabond is someone who wanders from place to place without a home or job.

words.tr: n. 奇想；异想天开；怪异多变
words.ex: His plans change with every vagary of mood.
words.ex_cn: 他的计划随着情绪的每个变化而改变。
words.en: A vagary is an unexpected and inexplicable change in a situation or in someone's behavior.

words.tr:
n. 流浪汉；漂泊者；乞丐
adj. 流浪的；漂泊的
words.ex: The vagrant slept on the park bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个流浪汉睡在公园的长椅上。
words.en: A vagrant is someone who moves from place to place and does not have a permanent home or job.

words.tr: adj. 非常自负的；自命不凡的
words.ex: He was so vainglorious that he believed his own press clippings.
words.ex_cn: 他非常自负，以至于相信了自己的新闻剪报。
words.en: If you describe someone as vainglorious, you are critical of them because they are very proud of their own status, abilities, or achievements.

words.tr:
adj. 告别的
n. 告别辞；告别演说
words.ex: He gave a valedictory speech at graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他在毕业典礼上发表了告别演讲。
words.en: A valedictory speech, letter, or performance is one that is intended as a goodbye.

words.ex: This coupon is valid until next month.
words.ex_cn: 这张优惠券到下个月都有效。
words.en: If something such as a document or agreement is valid, it is legally acceptable or officially recognized.

words.ex: The system will validate your password.
words.ex_cn: 系统将验证你的密码。
words.en: To validate something such as a claim or statement means to prove or confirm that it is true or correct.

words.ex: The soldier was honored for his valor in battle.
words.ex_cn: 这位士兵因在战斗中的英勇表现而受到表彰。
words.en: Valor is great courage, especially in a battle or war.

words.ex: The vampire drinks blood at night.
words.ex_cn: 吸血鬼在夜里喝血。
words.en: A vampire is a mythical creature that subsists by feeding on the vital essence (generally in the form of blood) of the living.

words.tr: n. 前锋；前卫；先头部队；先驱
words.ex: He is at the vanguard of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他在新技术的前沿。
words.en: The vanguard is the leading part of an advancing military formation. It has a broader meaning, signifying the forefront of any movement or field.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.tr: adj. 乏味的；无味的；枯燥的
words.ex: The movie was vapid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影乏味又无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vapid, you are criticizing them because they are dull and uninteresting.

words.ex: The sun vaporizes water from the lake.
words.ex_cn: 太阳把湖里的水蒸发了。
words.en: To convert or be converted into vapor.

words.tr: adj. 五花八门的； v. “variegate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The garden has variegated flowers in many colors.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有五花八门的彩色花朵。
words.en: Having patches, stripes, or marks of different colors; diversified in appearance.

words.tr: n. 诸侯；封臣; adj. 臣属的; n. （Vassal）人名；（英、法、德、罗）瓦萨尔；（西）...
words.ex: The king's vassals pledged their loyalty to him.
words.ex_cn: 国王的诸侯们向他宣誓效忠。
words.en: In medieval Europe, a vassal was a person who held land from a superior lord and owed him homage and allegiance.

words.ex: The vaunted new technology turned out to be a disappointment.
words.ex_cn: 这项被大肆吹嘘的新技术结果令人失望。
words.en: If you describe something as vaunted or much vaunted, you mean that people praise it more than it deserves.

words.tr:
v. 改变方向；转向
n. 转向
words.ex: The car veers to the left when the driver turns too fast.
words.ex_cn: 当司机转得太快时，汽车会向左偏转。
words.en: If something veers in a certain direction, it suddenly changes direction and moves in that direction.

words.tr: v. 生长；植物似地生长；过单调呆板的生活
words.ex: The plants vegetate quickly in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这些植物在春天生长得很快。
words.en: To vegetate means to live in a monotonous, passive, or mentally inactive way; to grow or sprout as a plant does.

words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

words.ex: The car's velocity increased on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在高速公路上的速度增加了。
words.en: Velocity is the speed at which something moves in a particular direction.

words.tr: adj. 贪赃枉法的；腐败的
words.ex: The official was venal and took bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员贪腐，接受了贿赂。
words.en: If you describe someone as venal, you disapprove of them because they are prepared to do almost anything in return for money, even things which are dishonest or immoral.

words.ex: He swore a vendetta against his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他向邻居发誓要报仇。
words.en: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter quarrel with or campaign against someone.

words.ex: The vendor sells fresh fruits at the market.
words.ex_cn: 这个商贩在市场卖新鲜水果。
words.en: A vendor is a person or company that sells goods or services.

words.ex: The table has a wooden veneer on top.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子的表面有一层木制饰板。
words.en: A veneer is a thin layer of wood or other material that is used to cover a surface, especially in furniture making, to make it look more attractive.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.ex: He made a venial mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告中犯了一个可以原谅的错误。
words.en: If you describe a wrong action as venial, you mean that it is not very serious or grave, and therefore easy to forgive.

words.ex: He ate venison at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上吃了鹿肉。
words.en: The flesh of a deer used as food.

words.ex: The snake released venom into its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇向猎物释放了毒液。
words.en: Venom is a poisonous substance secreted by animals such as snakes and spiders, used for defense or to kill prey.

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.ex: The ventral side of the fish is lighter in color.
words.ex_cn: 鱼的腹侧颜色较浅。
words.en: Relating to or situated on or close to the abdomen; abdominal.

words.tr: n. 口技表演者；腹语表演者；
words.ex: The ventriloquist made his doll talk funny.
words.ex_cn: 这位口技表演者让他的玩偶说起了滑稽的话。
words.en: A ventriloquist is someone who can speak without moving their lips and who entertains people by making it seem as if a puppet is talking.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: He was known for his venturesome spirit and willingness to take risks.
words.ex_cn: 他以冒险精神和愿意承担风险而闻名。
words.en: If you describe someone as venturesome, you mean that they are willing to take risks, especially in order to try out new things.

words.tr: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场；
words.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。
words.en: A place where an event or meeting is held, such as a concert hall or conference center.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；说实话的；准确的
words.ex: He is a veracious person who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个诚实的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is veracious is truthful and honest.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

words.tr: v. 用言语（或文字）表达
words.ex: He can verbalize his thoughts clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: To verbalize means to express something in words, especially to articulate feelings or thoughts clearly.

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

words.ex: He used too much verbiage in his email.
words.ex_cn: 他在邮件中用了太多的冗词。
words.en: Verbiage refers to an overabundance of words in writing or speech, often seen as unnecessary or overly complex.

words.ex: He gave a verbose answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对简单的问题给出了冗长的回答。
words.en: Using or containing more words than are necessary; long-winded.

words.ex: The verdant hills looked beautiful in spring.
words.ex_cn: 青翠的山丘在春天看起来很美。
words.en: Green with grass or other rich vegetation.

words.ex: The statue had developed a layer of verdigris over the years.
words.ex_cn: 多年来，雕像上长出了一层铜绿。
words.en: a green or bluish patina formed on copper, brass, or bronze surfaces exposed to the atmosphere for long periods

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.tr: adj. 貌似真实的; 可能的
words.ex: The story she told sounded verisimilar, but we later found out it was fabricated.
words.ex_cn: 她讲述的故事听起来很真实，但我们后来发现它是捏造的。
words.en: Having the appearance of truth; probable or likely.

words.ex: The movie has verisimilitude because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有逼真性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: the quality of seeming to be true or real

words.tr: adj. 真实的；确实的；真正的
words.ex: It was a veritable treasure trove of old books.
words.ex_cn: 那是一个真正的旧书宝库。
words.en: You use veritable to emphasize the size, amount, or nature of something.

words.ex: The verity of his story was proven by the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他故事的真实性被证据证明了。
words.en: Verity refers to the quality or state of being true or real.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

words.ex: The vernal equinox marks the beginning of spring.
words.ex_cn: 春分标志着春天的开始。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in spring.

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

words.ex: The vertex of the triangle is at the top.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的顶点在顶部。
words.en: The highest point of something; the top or apex.

words.ex: He felt vertigo after spinning around quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速转圈后感到头晕。
words.en: A sensation of whirling and loss of balance, associated particularly with looking down from a great height, or caused by disease affecting the inner ear or the vestibular nerve; giddiness.

words.ex: She painted with great verve.
words.ex_cn: 她作画时充满热情。
words.en: If you say that someone has verve, you mean that they seem to have a lot of energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The old house has a vestige of its original design.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子还保留着它原始设计的痕迹。
words.en: A vestige is a small part or amount of something that remains after the rest has disappeared or been destroyed.

words.ex: The loud noise vexes my little brother.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让我的小弟弟很烦。
words.en: If someone or something vexes you, they make you feel annoyed, puzzled, and frustrated.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: The menu offered a variety of viands to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 菜单提供了多种食物供选择。
words.en: Viand refers to an item of food, especially a choice or delicious dish.

words.ex: He did not agree with the policy, but he did not want to vilify those who supported it.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这项政策，但不想诋毁那些支持它的人。
words.en: To vilify someone means to say or write very unpleasant things about them in order to hurt their reputation.

words.tr: adj. 充满智慧的；明智的；英明的；
words.ex: The wise old man gave good advice.
words.ex_cn: 这位充满智慧的老人给出了很好的建议。
words.en: If you describe someone as wise, you mean that they have experience, knowledge, and good judgment.

words.tr:
adj. 幻想的；有远见的
n. 空想家；有远见的人
words.ex: He had a visionary idea about flying cars.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个关于飞行汽车的幻想想法。
words.en: A visionary is someone who has strong ideas about how things might be different in the future, especially in a way that leads to changes in society or technology.

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.tr: v. 使变质；损害；使失效
words.ex: The poison vitiated the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒物使水源变质。
words.en: To vitiate something means to impair or reduce the quality, value, or effectiveness of it.

words.tr: adj. 玻璃的；玻璃状的；玻璃似的
words.ex: The vitreous humor fills the space between the lens and the retina.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃体液填充了晶状体和视网膜之间的空间。
words.en: Vitreous is used to describe something that is like glass, especially in being smooth, shiny, or transparent.

words.tr: adj. 刻薄的；尖刻的；恶意的
words.ex: His vitriolic words hurt everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他刻薄的话伤害了房间里所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as vitriolic, you disapprove of it because it is full of bitterness and hate, and so causes a lot of distress and pain.

words.tr: adj. 充满辱骂的；责骂的
words.ex: His vituperative remarks were uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他那些责骂的话是多余的。
words.en: If you describe something that is said or written as vituperative, you mean that it is full of bitter criticism or anger.

words.ex: She is a vivacious girl who laughs loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个活泼的女孩，笑得很响亮。
words.en: If you describe someone as vivacious, you mean that they are lively, exciting, and attractive.

words.ex: He opposes vivisection because it hurts animals.
words.ex_cn: 他反对活体解剖，因为这会伤害动物。
words.en: The practice of performing operations on live animals for the purpose of experimentation or scientific research (often considered to be cruel).

words.tr: n. 雌狐；泼妇，刁妇；唠叨的女人；坏心眼的女人
words.ex: She was known for her sharp tongue and was often called a vixen by her peers.
words.ex_cn: 她以言辞犀利著称，常被同龄人称为泼妇。
words.en: A vixen is a female fox. The term can also be used to describe a quarrelsome or shrewish woman.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.ex: Blue jeans are in vogue this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年牛仔裤很时髦。
words.en: If something is in vogue, it is very popular and fashionable.

words.ex: The alcohol is volatile and evaporates quickly.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是易挥发的，会迅速蒸发。
words.en: A volatile situation or person is one that is likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially by getting worse.

words.tr: n. 意志力；自愿选择；自行决断
words.ex: He did it of his own volition.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于自己的意愿做的。
words.en: The power to make your own decisions or choices.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 宽松的；容积大的；部头大的；卷数多的
words.ex: She wore a voluminous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条宽松的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is voluminous is very large or contains a lot of things.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

words.ex: The water forms a vortex down the drain.
words.ex_cn: 水在排水口形成一个漩涡。
words.en: A vortex is a mass of wind or water that spins around very fast and pulls objects into its empty center.

words.ex: The king vouchsafed a generous grant to the university.
words.ex_cn: 国王慷慨地赐予了大学一笔赠款。
words.en: If you vouchsafe something to someone, you give or tell it to them, especially in a gracious or condescending manner.

words.tr: n. 窥淫癖者；好刺探他人隐私者
words.ex: He was arrested for being a voyeur, spying on people in their private moments.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窥他人隐私时刻而被捕，是一个窥淫狂者。
words.en: A voyeur is someone who gets sexual pleasure from secretly watching other people, especially when they are naked or having sex.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: His vulpine smile made everyone suspicious.
words.ex_cn: 他那狐狸般的微笑让每个人都起了疑心。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a fox; crafty or cunning.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words W

words.ex: He ate a waffle with maple syrup for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一块淋上枫糖浆的华夫饼。
words.en: If you say that someone waffles, you are critical of them because they talk or write a lot without actually making any clear or important points.

words.tr:
v. 吹拂；（随风）飘荡；使飘荡
n. 一股（在空气中飘荡的味或烟）；风信旗；飘荡
words.ex: The smell of bread wafted from the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味从厨房里飘来。
words.en: If sounds or smells waft through the air, or if something such as a light wind wafts them, they move gently through the air.

words.tr: adj. 滑稽的；诙谐的；爱恶作剧的
words.ex: His waggish sense of humor often lightened the mood at serious meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的幽默感经常在严肃的会议上活跃气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as waggish, you mean that they are humorous and often make jokes or amusing remarks.

words.tr: n. 无家可归的人；流浪儿；无主的动物
words.ex: The waif was found wandering the streets alone.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪儿被发现独自一人在街上徘徊。
words.en: A waif is a person, especially a child, who has no home or friends and is very thin and poorly dressed.

words.ex: He decided to waive the fee.
words.ex_cn: 他决定放弃这笔费用。
words.en: If you waive a right, claim, or privilege, you do not insist on it or do not use it.

words.ex: He wakes up at six every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上六点醒来。
words.en: To wake means to stop sleeping or to cause someone to stop sleeping. It can also refer to the trail left by a moving ship.

words.tr: v. 打滚；躺卧；（船）颠簸；沉湎
words.ex: The pig wallow in the mud.
words.ex_cn: 猪在泥里打滚。
words.en: If you say that someone is wallowing in an unpleasant situation, you are criticizing them for being deliberately unhappy.

words.ex: I want a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you want something, you feel a desire or a need for it.

words.ex: She had a strong wanderlust and traveled to many countries.
words.ex_cn: 她有强烈的旅游热，去过许多国家。
words.en: A strong desire to travel.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

words.tr:
v. 骗取；伪造
n. 哄骗
words.ex: She managed to wangle an invitation to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她设法弄到了派对的邀请。
words.en: If you wangle something that you want, you manage to get it by being clever or persuading someone.

words.ex: The wanton destruction of the forest shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对森林的恣意破坏让每个人都感到震惊。
words.en: If someone describes a person or their behaviour as wanton, they are critical of them for behaving in a very uncontrolled or unacceptable way, often without caring about the consequences.

words.tr:
v. （鸟）啼啭；用颤音唱
n. 啼啭；颤音
words.ex: The warble of the songbird filled the morning air.
words.ex_cn: 歌鸟的啭鸣声充满了清晨的空气。
words.en: To warble means to sing with trills, quavers, or melodic embellishments, often used to describe the sound made by birds. It can also refer to the act of singing in a trilling or quavering voice.

words.tr: adj. 保证的； v. “warrant”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The repair was warranted by the store.
words.ex_cn: 这次维修由商店保证。
words.en: If something is warranted, there is a good reason for it and it can be accepted.

words.tr: n. 保证；保修单；保证书
words.ex: The phone comes with a one-year warranty.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一年的保修期。
words.en: A warranty is a written guarantee, often given to the purchaser of an article by its manufacturer, promising to repair or replace it if necessary within a specified period of time.

words.tr: n. 兔子窝；狭窄拥挤的街区
words.ex: The rabbits live in a warren under the hill.
words.ex_cn: 兔子住在山下的兔子窝里。
words.en: A warren is a network of interconnecting rabbit burrows or a place where rabbits are kept in captivity. It can also refer to a densely populated or labyrinthine area.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.tr: n. 挥霍无度的人；败家子
words.ex: He was criticized for being a wastrel with his inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他因挥霍继承的财产而受到批评。
words.en: A wastrel is someone who wastes their time, money, or resources in a careless or irresponsible way.

words.tr:
n. 蜡；
v. 给…上蜡；
words.ex: Bees make wax to build their hives.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂用蜡建造蜂巢。
words.en: Wax is a solid, slightly shiny substance made of fat or oil that is used to make candles, polish, and other products. It can also refer to the process of applying wax to something or the natural substance found in the ear.

words.ex: The thief tried to waylay the man on the dark street.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图在黑暗的街道上拦住那个男人。
words.en: To lie in wait for and attack from ambush

words.ex: She is weaning her baby off milk.
words.ex_cn: 她正在让宝宝戒掉牛奶。
words.en: To wean someone off something means to make them gradually stop using or depending on it, especially something harmful or unnecessary.

words.ex: The weather is sunny today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气晴朗。
words.en: The condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, especially with regard to temperature, precipitation, and wind.

words.ex: The welt on his arm hurt after the burn.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上的烧伤疤痕很疼。
words.en: A welt is a raised mark on the skin caused by a blow, especially from a whip or stick.

words.tr:
v. 打滚；翻滚
n. 混乱的一堆
words.ex: The box was full of a welter of old toys.
words.ex_cn: 盒子里堆满了各种旧玩具。
words.en: A welter is a state of general confusion or disorder. It can also refer to a heavy or confused mass of something, such as a welter of papers.

words.ex: He tried to wheedle money from his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗父母给他钱。
words.en: If someone wheedles, they try to persuade someone to do or give them something, often by flattery or by being very nice.

words.tr:
n. 小狗；幼犬
v. 下（崽）；产（仔）
words.ex: The dog gave birth to three whelps last night.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗昨晚生了三只小狗。
words.en: A whelp is a young offspring of a dog or other carnivorous animal, or the act of giving birth to such offspring.

words.ex: The smell of food whetted his appetite.
words.ex_cn: 食物的香味刺激了他的食欲。
words.en: To whet something means to make it sharper or more intense.

words.ex: I caught a whiff of fresh bread.
words.ex_cn: 我闻到了一点新鲜面包的气味。
words.en: A whiff is a brief, gentle gust of air, or a slight smell of something.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

words.tr:
v. 马嘶；轻声嘶鸣
n. 马嘶；嘶声
words.ex: The horse whinny loudly when it sees the farmer.
words.ex_cn: 马一看到农夫就嘶鸣。
words.en: A whinny is a gentle, high-pitched sound made by a horse, often as a greeting or to express excitement.

words.ex: I have a whit of patience left.
words.ex_cn: 我只剩下一点点耐心了。
words.en: A whit is a very small amount of something, used especially in negative expressions to mean 'not at all'.

words.ex: He whittled a small bird from wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用木头削出了一只小鸟。
words.en: To whittle means to cut or shape a piece of wood by repeatedly cutting small slices from it, or to reduce something in size, amount, or extent by a gradual series of steps.

words.tr:
n. 螺纹；涡 
v. 盘旋
words.ex: The fingerprint has a clear whorl pattern.
words.ex_cn: 这个指纹有一个清晰的旋涡图案。
words.en: A whorl is a pattern of spirals or concentric circles, especially in the arrangement of leaves or petals around a stem.

words.tr: adj. 任性的；故意的；蓄意的
words.ex: The willful child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个任性的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe actions or attitudes as willful, you are critical of them because they are done or expressed deliberately, especially with the intention of causing harm, or they are stubborn and unreasonable.

words.tr: adj. 狡猾的；诡计多端的
words.ex: The wily fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as wily, you mean that they are clever at achieving what they want, especially by tricking people.

words.tr:
n. 皱眉蹙额；退缩
v. 皱眉蹙额；退避
words.ex: He let out a wince when he touched his sore arm.
words.ex_cn: 当他碰触到疼痛的手臂时，他皱了一下眉。
words.en: If you wince, you make a slight, sudden movement of your face, especially when you are in pain or when you see or hear something unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 意外之财；意外的收获；风吹落的果子
words.ex: He got a windfall from his uncle's inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他从叔叔的遗产中获得了一笔意外之财。
words.en: A windfall is an unexpected gain, piece of good fortune, or financial benefit.

words.tr: v. 簸扬（谷）；分出好坏；筛选
words.ex: He winnows the wheat to remove the chaff.
words.ex_cn: 他用扬谷法去除麦子中的糠壳。
words.en: To winnow means to separate the grain from the chaff or to separate the good from the bad.

words.tr: adj. 漂亮的；迷人的；讨人喜欢的
words.ex: The winsome girl smiled at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个可爱的女孩对每个人微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as winsome, you mean that they are attractive and charming.

words.tr: adj. 小束状的；稀疏的；纤弱的
words.ex: She has wispy hair that floats in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 她有轻盈的头发，在风中飘动。
words.en: Something that is wispy is thin and weak, and often seems to be floating or moving gently.

words.tr: adj. 扭曲的；弯曲的；复杂的
words.ex: The twistful road made driving difficult.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路让驾驶变得困难。
words.en: Characterized by twists or turns; winding.

words.tr:
adj. 偏僻的；离群的；孤独的；内向的
v. 撤回；撤退；“withdraw”的过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is in a withdrawn area, far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋位于一个偏僻的地方，远离城镇。
words.en: If someone is withdrawn, they are very quiet, and do not want to talk to other people. If something is withdrawn, it is taken back or removed.

words.ex: The flowers wither in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在烈日下枯萎。
words.en: If a plant withers, it dries up and dies. If something withers, it becomes weaker or less important until it disappears completely.

words.ex: The company will withhold his salary until he signs the contract.
words.ex_cn: 公司会扣留他的工资，直到他签署合同。
words.en: If you withhold something that someone wants, you refuse to let them have it.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；不动脑筋的；不明事理的
words.ex: He made a witless mistake and lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 他犯了一个愚蠢的错误，输掉了比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone as witless, you mean that they are very foolish or stupid.

words.tr: n. 俏皮话；妙语；诙谐语
words.ex: His speech was filled with witticisms that kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了妙语，让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A witticism is a clever and amusing remark.

words.tr: n. 巫术；魔法；杰出的成就；非凡的才能
words.ex: The magician's wizardry amazed the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师的魔法让孩子们感到惊奇。
words.en: The skill of performing magic tricks or the practice of magic.

words.tr: adj. 干瘦的；干瘪的；皱缩的
words.ex: The wizened old man told stories by the fire.
words.ex_cn: 那位皱纹满面的老人在火炉旁讲故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as wizened, you mean they are old and have a lot of lines on their skin, often because they have had a hard life.

words.ex: He felt great woe after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 他失去狗后感到极大的悲伤。
words.en: Woe is great sadness.

words.tr: contr.contr. 不会，将不（等于 will not）
words.ex: He won't go to school today.
words.ex_cn: 他今天不去学校。
words.en: Won't is the usual spoken form of 'will not'.

words.ex: He gave up worldly pleasures to live a simple life.
words.ex_cn: 他放弃了世俗的享乐，过着简朴的生活。
words.en: Worldly means relating to the world and the practical matters of life, rather than to spiritual or religious matters.

words.tr:
v. 争论；争执；吵架
n. 争吵；口角
words.ex: They wrangle over the price every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为价格争执。
words.en: If you wrangle with someone, you argue with them in a noisy or angry way.

words.ex: His wrath scared everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒吓到了房间里的每个人。
words.en: Extreme anger.

words.tr: v. 造成（混乱或破坏）；施行（报复）
words.ex: The storm wreaked havoc on the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了破坏。
words.en: To cause something to happen in a violent and often uncontrolled way.

words.tr:
v. 猛扭；扭伤；挣脱
n. 扳手；扳钳；（离别的）痛苦
words.ex: He wrenched the door open with all his strength.
words.ex_cn: 他用尽全力猛扭门，把它打开了。
words.en: A wrench is a tool used for gripping and turning nuts, bolts, pipes, etc. It can also refer to a sudden violent twist or pull, or a feeling of sadness or distress caused by separation.

words.tr:
v. 夺取；费力取得；歪曲
n. 扭；拧
words.ex: He wrests the ball from his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他从对手那里抢走球。
words.en: To wrest something from someone means to take it from them with a lot of effort, often because they do not want to give it to you.

words.ex: He writes a letter every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天写一封信。
words.en: To write means to form letters, words, or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

words.tr:
v. 扭动；翻滚；苦恼
n. 扭动；翻滚
words.ex: The child writhe in pain after falling.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒后痛苦地扭动。
words.en: If you writhe, your body twists and turns violently backwards and forwards, usually because you are in great pain or discomfort.

words.tr: adj. 扭歪的；啼笑皆非的；挖苦的；讽刺的
words.ex: He gave a wry smile when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时露出了苦笑。
words.en: If someone has a wry expression, it shows that they find a bad situation or a change in a situation slightly amusing.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words X

words.ex: He showed xenophobia toward people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人表现出恐外心理。
words.en: Xenophobia is a strong feeling of dislike or fear of people from other countries.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words Y

words.ex: He paid 1000 yen for the sushi.
words.ex_cn: 他用一千日元买了寿司。
words.en: The yen is the unit of currency used in Japan. It can also mean a strong desire or craving for something.

words.ex: The yeoman worked hard on the farm every day.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天在农场辛勤工作。
words.en: A yeoman is a man who owns and cultivates a small farm, or a servant in a royal or noble household, or a member of a volunteer cavalry force in Britain.

words.tr:
v. 生产；获利；
n. 产量；
words.ex: This farm yields a lot of wheat each year.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场每年生产大量小麦。
words.en: If you yield to someone or something, you stop resisting them. If a tree or plant yields fruit or flowers, it produces them.

words.tr:
n. 轭；枷锁；束缚
v. 上轭；使强行结合
words.ex: The farmer put a yoke on the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫给牛套上了轭。
words.en: A yoke is a wooden bar that is fastened over the necks of two animals, especially cattle, and connected to the vehicle or load that they are pulling. It can also refer to something that binds people together or something that people find oppressive.

words.ex: The yokel laughed at the city lights.
words.ex_cn: 这个乡下人对城市灯光笑了。
words.en: A yokel is an uneducated and unsophisticated person from the countryside.

words.ex: Is this your book?
words.ex_cn: 这是你的书吗？
words.en: Belonging to or associated with the person or people that the speaker is addressing.

chapters.name: 3500 Master Words Z

words.tr:
adj. 滑稽的
n. 小丑；丑角
words.ex: The zany clown made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯狂的小丑让所有人都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as zany, you mean that they are strange or eccentric in a humorous way.

words.ex: He showed great zeal in helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他在帮助他人时表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Zeal is great enthusiasm, especially in connection with work, religion, or politics.

words.ex: He is a zealot for environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心者。
words.en: A zealot is someone who is extremely enthusiastic about something, especially religion or politics.

words.ex: The sun is at its zenith at noon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在正午时分达到最高点。
words.en: The zenith is the time at which something is most powerful or successful.

words.ex: A gentle zephyr blew through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一阵轻柔的微风吹过树林。
words.en: A zephyr is a gentle, mild breeze, traditionally from the west, and especially one of the soft, mild breezes of spring or summer.
